sentences.zh: 陳訓

translations.literal: Chen Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xun

sentences.zh: 陳訓，字道元，曆陽人。

translations.literal: Chen Xun, style name Daoyuan, was a man of Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xun, courtesy name Daoyuan, came from Liyang.

sentences.zh: 少好秘學，天文、算曆、陰陽、占候無不畢綜，尤善風角。

translations.literal: In youth he loved occult learning; in astronomy, calendrical calculation, yin-yang, and prognostication by signs there was none he did not master comprehensively, and he was especially skilled in fengjiao.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he devoured esoteric studies—astronomy, calendar math, yin-yang, and omen-reading—and excelled above all at wind-angle divination.

sentences.zh: 孫晧以為奉禁都尉，使其占侯。

translations.literal: Sun Hao appointed him Attendant Commandant of the Forbidden Palaces and had him perform prognostications.
translations.idiomatic: The last Wu emperor Sun Hao named him palace attendant for forbidden precincts and set him to read the omens.

sentences.zh: 晧政嚴酷，訓知其必敗而不敢言。

translations.literal: Hao's government was harsh and cruel; Xun knew he was bound to fail yet dared not speak.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao ruled with terror; Chen Xun saw the dynasty was doomed but kept silent.

sentences.zh: 時錢唐湖開，或言天下當太平，青蓋入洛陽。

translations.literal: At that time the Qiantang Lake opened; some said the realm would soon be at peace and the "green canopy" would enter Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Qiantang Lake burst its banks, court gossip took it for an omen of universal peace and the Wu ruler's green-canopy carriage arriving in Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 晧以問訓，訓曰：「臣止能望氣，不能達湖之開塞。

translations.literal: Hao asked Xun about it; Xun said, "Your servant can only observe qi; I cannot fathom whether the lake opens or closes.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao pressed him; Chen Xun answered carefully that he could read vapors, not hydraulics.

sentences.zh: 」退而告其友曰：「青蓋入洛，將有輿櫬銜璧之事，非吉祥也。

translations.literal: " Withdrawing, he told his friend, "When the green canopy enters Luo, there will be affairs of a bier borne forth and jade held in the mouth—it is not auspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Privately he warned a friend that "green canopy to Luoyang" foretold a funeral surrender, not fortune.

sentences.zh: 」尋而吳亡。

translations.literal: " Soon thereafter Wu perished.
translations.idiomatic: Wu fell almost immediately afterward.

sentences.zh: 訓隨例內徙，拜諫義大夫。

translations.literal: Xun moved inward with the general migration and was appointed Grandee of Remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: He relocated with the other southern households and received the remonstrance grandee's title.

sentences.zh: 俄而去職還鄉。

translations.literal: Before long he left office and returned to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: He soon resigned and went home to Liyang.

sentences.zh: 及陳敏作亂，遣弟宏為曆陽太守，訓謂邑人曰：「陳家無王氣，不久當滅。

translations.literal: When Chen Min rebelled, sending his younger brother Hong as governor of Liyang, Xun told the townspeople, "The Chen clan lacks kingly qi; before long they will be destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Min rose and installed his brother Chen Hong at Liyang, Chen Xun told neighbors the Chen house carried no imperial aura and would collapse soon.

sentences.zh: 」宏聞，將斬之。

translations.literal: " Hong heard of it and was about to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Hong planned to kill him for the remark.

sentences.zh: 訓鄉人秦琚為宏參軍，乃說訓曰：「訓善風角，可試之。

translations.literal: Xun's fellow townsman Qin Ju served Hong as army aide and therefore urged Xun, saying, "Xun is skilled in fengjiao—put him to the test.
translations.idiomatic: Army adviser Qin Ju, a townsman, begged Chen Hong to try Chen Xun's wind-angle art before shedding blood.

sentences.zh: 如不中，徐斬未晚也。

translations.literal: If he misses, you may behead him slowly—it will not be late."
translations.idiomatic: If his reading failed, they could execute him at leisure.

sentences.zh: 」乃赦之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Hong stayed the blade.

sentences.zh: 時宏攻征東參軍衡彥于曆陽，乃問訓曰：「城中有幾千人？

translations.literal: At that time Hong was attacking Eastern Campaign Army aide Heng Yan at Liyang; he therefore asked Xun, "How many men are in the city?
translations.idiomatic: While Chen Hong besieged Eastern Campaign aide Heng Yan in Liyang, he demanded to know the garrison's strength.

sentences.zh: 攻之可拔不？

translations.literal: Can it be taken by assault?"
translations.idiomatic: He asked whether the walls could be stormed.

sentences.zh: 」訓登牛渚山望氣，曰：「不過五百人。

translations.literal: " Xun climbed Mount Niuzhu to observe qi and said, "Not more than five hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xun climbed Mount Niuzhu, read the vapors, and put the defenders under five hundred.

sentences.zh: 然不可攻，攻之必敗。

translations.literal: Yet you must not attack; if you attack, you will surely be defeated."
translations.idiomatic: He forbade an assault anyway, warning that any attack would fail.

sentences.zh: 」宏復大怒曰：「何有五千人攻五百人而有不得理？

translations.literal: " Hong raged again, saying, "How can five thousand men attack five hundred and lack reason to prevail?"
translations.idiomatic: Chen Hong fumed that five thousand ought to overrun five hundred.

sentences.zh: 」命將士攻之，果為彥所敗，方信訓有道術，乃優遇之。

translations.literal: " He ordered his generals and soldiers to attack; they were indeed defeated by Yan; only then did he believe Xun possessed the way of techniques and treated him generously.
translations.idiomatic: The storming host was routed by Heng Yan; chastened, Chen Hong honored Chen Xun as a true adept.

sentences.zh: 都水參軍淮南周亢嘗問訓以官位，訓曰：「君至卯年當剖符近郡，酉年當有曲蓋。

translations.literal: Army Waterways aide Zhou Kang of Huainan once asked Xun about office rank; Xun said, "By the mao year you ought to split tallies for a nearby commandery; by the you year you ought to receive a bent canopy."
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Kang of Huainan, an aide on waterworks, asked his career; Chen Xun promised a nearby governorship in a mao year and a bent-canopy general's train in a you year.

sentences.zh: 」亢曰：「脫如來言，當相薦拔。

translations.literal: " Kang said, "If it comes as you say, I shall recommend and promote you."
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Kang vowed to pull strings if the prophecy held.

sentences.zh: 」訓曰：「性不好官，惟欲得米耳。

translations.literal: " Xun said, "By nature I dislike office—I only wish to obtain rice."
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xun said he wanted grain, not promotion.

sentences.zh: 」後亢果為義興太守、金紫將軍。

translations.literal: " Later Kang indeed became governor of Yixing and general with gold ribbon and purple sash.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Kang later became Yixing governor and a gold-and-purple general, just as foretold.

sentences.zh: 時劉聰、王彌寇洛陽，曆陽太守武瑕問訓曰：「國家人事如何？

translations.literal: At that time Liu Cong and Wang Mi raided Luoyang; Wuxia, governor of Liyang, asked Xun, "How stand the court and the realm?"
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Cong and Wang Mi threatened Luoyang, Liyang governor Wu Xia asked Chen Xun for the fate of the Jin house.

sentences.zh: 」訓曰：「胡賊三逼，國家當敗，天子野死。

translations.literal: " Xun said, "Hu bandits press thrice; the state will be defeated and the Son of Heaven will die in the open wilds.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xun said Xiongnu armies would thrice corner the throne, the dynasty would fall, and the emperor would perish in the field.

sentences.zh: 今尚未也。

translations.literal: Not yet now."
translations.idiomatic: The worst had not arrived yet.

sentences.zh: 」其後懷湣二帝果有平陽之酷焉。

translations.literal: " Thereafter the two emperors Huai and Min indeed suffered the cruelty at Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Emperors Huai and Min later endured captivity and murder at Pingyang, as he had warned.

sentences.zh: 或問其以明年吉凶者，訓曰：「揚州刺史當死，武昌大火，上方節將亦當死。

translations.literal: Someone asked him about the next year's good or ill; Xun said, "The Yangzhou governor will die; there will be a great fire in Wuchang; a general of the upper ranks will also die."
translations.idiomatic: Asked about the coming year, he predicted the Yangzhou governor's death, a conflagration at Wuchang, and the passing of a senior commander.

sentences.zh: 」至時，劉陶、周訪皆卒，武昌大火，燒數千家。

translations.literal: " When the time came, Liu Tao and Zhou Fang both died; there was a great fire in Wuchang that burned several thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Tao and Zhou Fang died on schedule, and Wuchang blazed through thousands of homes.

sentences.zh: 時甘卓為曆陽太守，訓私謂所親曰：「甘侯頭低而視仰，相法名為眄刀，又目有赤脈，自外而入，不出十年，必以兵死，不領兵則可以免。

translations.literal: At that time Gan Zhuo was governor of Liyang; Xun privately told those close to him, "Lord Gan's head hangs low while his gaze looks upward—in physiognomy this is called 'knife-squint'; moreover there are red threads in the eyes coming from without; within ten years he is sure to die by arms—if he does not command troops he may escape."
translations.idiomatic: Watching Gan Zhuo at Liyang, Chen Xun whispered that his low head and upturned eyes formed the lethal "knife-squint" look, laced with red veins—within a decade steel would find him unless he shed command.

sentences.zh: 」卓果為王敦所害。

translations.literal: " Zhuo was indeed killed by Wang Dun.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Zhuo fell to Wang Dun's coup, sword in hand.

sentences.zh: 丞相王導多病，每自憂慮，以問訓。

translations.literal: Chancellor Wang Dao was often ill and each time worried himself; he asked Xun about it.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Wang Dao, chronically unwell, consulted Chen Xun in his anxiety.

sentences.zh: 訓曰：「公耳豎垂肩，必壽，亦大貴，子孫當興于江東。

translations.literal: Xun said, "Your ears hang straight to the shoulders—you must enjoy long life, and you are also greatly noble; descendants will rise east of the Yangzi."
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xun read his pendulous ears as signs of long life, high rank, and a flourishing lineage in Jiangdong.

sentences.zh: 」咸如其言。

translations.literal: " In every case it happened as he said.
translations.idiomatic: Each prediction proved true.

sentences.zh: 訓年八十餘卒。

translations.literal: Xun died in his eighties.
translations.idiomatic: He died past eighty.

sentences.zh: 戴洋

translations.literal: Dai Yang.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Yang

sentences.zh: 戴洋，字國流，吳興長城人也。

translations.literal: Dai Yang, style name Guoliu, was a man of Changcheng in Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Yang, courtesy name Guoliu, was a native of Changcheng in Wuxing commandery.

sentences.zh: 年十二，遇病死，五日而蘇。

translations.literal: At age twelve he fell ill and died, and after five days revived.
translations.idiomatic: At twelve he sickened, "died," and woke again after five days.

sentences.zh: 說死時天使其為酒藏吏，授符錄，給吏從幡麾，將上蓬萊、昆侖、積石、太室、恆、廬、衡等諸山。

translations.literal: He said that when dead Heaven had made him a clerk of the wine vaults, handed him tallies and registers, given him clerks with banners and standards, and was about to take him up Mount Penglai, Kunlun, Jishi, Taishi, Heng, Lu, Heng, and the other various mountains.
translations.idiomatic: He described a posthumous posting as celestial cellar-keeper with registers, escorts, and a tour of the sacred peaks from Penglai to the great Heng ranges.

sentences.zh: 既而遣歸，逢一老父，謂之曰：「汝後當得道，為貴人所識。

translations.literal: Then he was sent back; meeting an old man, the man told him, "Later you will obtain the Way and be recognized by noble men."
translations.idiomatic: Sent back to life, an elder promised he would win the Dao and earn patronage from the mighty.

sentences.zh: 」及長，遂善風角。

translations.literal: " When he grew up, he was skilled at fengjiao.
translations.idiomatic: As an adult he mastered wind-angle divination.

sentences.zh: 為人短陋，無風望，然好道術，妙解占侯卜數。

translations.literal: As a man he was short and plain in appearance, lacking an imposing air, yet he loved techniques of the Way and marvelously understood prognostication, divination, and numerology.
translations.idiomatic: He was homely and slight, yet obsessed with occult arts and uncannily sharp at omens, oracles, and fate reckoning.

sentences.zh: 吳末為台吏，知吳將亡，託病不仕。

translations.literal: At the end of Wu he was a Secretariat clerk; knowing Wu would perish, he pleaded illness and did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Wu he held a clerkship at headquarters, saw the kingdom's end coming, and feigned illness to stay out of service.

sentences.zh: 及吳平，還鄉里。

translations.literal: When Wu was pacified, he returned to his home village.
translations.idiomatic: After the conquest of Wu he went home.

sentences.zh: 後行至瀨鄉，經老子祠，皆是洋昔死時所見使處，但不復見昔物耳。

translations.literal: Later, traveling, he came to Lai township and passed the shrine to Laozi—all were places Dai Yang had been made to serve when dead, yet he no longer saw the former things.
translations.idiomatic: Passing Laozi's shrine at Lai township, he recognized every corner from his otherworldly errand, though the spirit furnishings had vanished.

sentences.zh: 因問守藏應鳳曰：「去二十餘年，嘗有人乘馬東行，過老君而不下馬，未達橋，墜馬死者不？

translations.literal: Therefore he asked the vault-keeper Ying Feng, "More than twenty years ago, was there one who rode a horse east, passed Lord Lao without dismounting, and before reaching the bridge fell from his horse and died?"
translations.idiomatic: He asked keeper Ying Feng whether a rider had once insulted the god by staying mounted and died before the bridge—twenty years past.

sentences.zh: 」鳳言有之。

translations.literal: " Feng said there was.
translations.idiomatic: Ying Feng confirmed the tale.

sentences.zh: 所問之事，多與洋同。

translations.literal: The matters he asked about mostly matched what Yang had seen.
translations.idiomatic: Every detail matched Dai Yang's infernal itinerary.

sentences.zh: 揚州刺史嘗問吉凶於洋，答曰：「熒惑入南斗，八月有暴水，九月當有客軍西南來。

translations.literal: The Yangzhou governor once asked Dai Yang about good or ill; he answered, "Mars has entered the Southern Dipper—in the eighth month there will be violent flooding; in the ninth month there ought to be a guest army from the southwest."
translations.idiomatic: Consulted by the Yangzhou governor, he warned of Mars in the Dipper—cloudbursts in the eighth month and an alien column from the southwest in the ninth.

sentences.zh: 」如期果大水，而石冰作亂。

translations.literal: " On schedule there was indeed great flooding, and Shi Bing rose in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: The floods came on time, and Shi Bing's revolt followed.

sentences.zh: 冰既據揚州，洋謂人曰：「視賊雲氣，四月當破。

translations.literal: After Bing had seized Yangzhou, Dai Yang told people, "Observing the bandits' cloud-qi, in the fourth month they will be broken."
translations.idiomatic: Once Shi Bing held Yangzhou, Dai Yang read his banners and gave him until the fourth month to collapse.

sentences.zh: 」果如其言。

translations.literal: " It happened as he said.
translations.idiomatic: The rebellion fell in that month.

sentences.zh: 時陳敏為右將軍，堂邑令孫混見而羨之。

translations.literal: At that time Chen Min was General of the Right; Sun Hun, magistrate of Tangyi, saw him and envied him.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Min, General of the Right, drew envious stares from Sun Hun, magistrate of Tangyi.

sentences.zh: 洋曰：「敏當作賊族滅，何足願也！

translations.literal: Dai Yang said, "Min will rebel and his clan be exterminated—what is there to envy!"
translations.idiomatic: Dai Yang snapped that Chen Min would turn traitor and wipe his own line—hardly a model to covet.

sentences.zh: 」未幾，敏果反而誅焉。

translations.literal: " Before long Min indeed rebelled and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Min revolted and died under the blade almost at once.

sentences.zh: 初，混欲迎其家累，洋曰：「此地當敗，得臘不得正，豈可移家於賊中乎！

translations.literal: At first Hun wished to bring his family dependents; Dai Yang said, "This place is about to fall—you may reach the year-end sacrifice month but not the first month—how can you move a household into the midst of bandits!"
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hun meant to fetch his kin; Dai Yang swore the town would fall after la but before the new year and forbade dragging families into a war zone.

sentences.zh: 」混便止。

translations.literal: " Hun then desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hun stayed put.

sentences.zh: 歲末，敏弟昶攻堂邑，混遂以單身走免。

translations.literal: At year's end Min's younger brother Chang attacked Tangyi, and Hun therefore fled alone and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Min's brother Chen Chang stormed Tangyi at year's end, Sun Hun slipped away alone.

sentences.zh: 其後都水馬武舉洋為都水令史，洋請急還鄉。

translations.literal: Thereafter Director of Waters Ma Wu recommended Dai Yang as clerk to the Director of Waters; Dai Yang requested emergency leave to return home.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Wu of the waterways directorate named him a waterways clerk; Dai Yang begged leave and hurried home.

sentences.zh: 將赴洛，夢神人謂之曰：「洛中當敗，人盡南渡，後五年揚州必有天子。

translations.literal: About to go to Luoyang, he dreamed a spirit told him, "Luoyang is about to collapse; the people will all cross south; after five years Yangzhou is sure to have a Son of Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Bound for Luoyang, he dreamed a god warning of the capital's fall, a great southern flight, and an emperor in Yangzhou within five years.

sentences.zh: 」洋信之，遂不去。

translations.literal: " Dai Yang believed it and therefore did not go.
translations.idiomatic: He canceled the journey and believed the vision.

sentences.zh: 既而皆如其夢。

translations.literal: Thereafter everything matched his dream.
translations.idiomatic: Events unfolded exactly as the dream had said.

sentences.zh: 廬江太守華譚問洋曰：「天下誰當復作賊者？

translations.literal: Lujiang governor Hua Tan asked Dai Yang, "Who under Heaven is next likely to turn bandit?
translations.idiomatic: Lujiang governor Hua Tan asked who in the realm would next rise in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 」洋曰：「王機。

translations.literal: " Dai Yang said, "Wang Ji."
translations.idiomatic: Dai Yang answered, "Wang Ji."

sentences.zh: 」尋而機反。

translations.literal: " Soon thereafter Wang Ji indeed rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji revolted almost at once.

sentences.zh: 陳眕問洋曰：「人言江南當有貴人，顧彥先、周宣珮當是不？

translations.literal: Chen Zhen asked Dai Yang, "People say south of the Yangzi there will be an eminent man—might it be Gu Yanxian and Zhou Xuanpei?"
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zhen asked whether Gu Rong and Zhou Pei were the great men fate had marked for the south.

sentences.zh: 」洋曰：「顧不及臘，周不見來年八月。

translations.literal: " Dai Yang said, "Gu will not reach the la month; Zhou will not see the eighth month of next year."
translations.idiomatic: Dai Yang said Gu Rong would not live to la and Zhou Pei would die before the eighth month of the coming year.

sentences.zh: 」榮果以十二月十七日卒，十九日臘，珮以明年七月晦亡。

translations.literal: " Rong indeed died on the seventeenth day of the twelfth month; the la sacrifice fell on the nineteenth; Pei died on the last day of the seventh month the next year.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Rong died on the seventeenth of the twelfth month, la came two days later, and Zhou Pei perished on the final day of the seventh month next year—each on schedule.

sentences.zh: 王導遇病，召洋問之。

translations.literal: Wang Dao fell ill and summoned Dai Yang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao took sick and called Dai Yang to his bedside.

sentences.zh: 洋曰：「君侯本命在申，金為土使之主，而于申上石頭立冶，火光照天，此為金火相爍，水火相煎，以故受害耳。

translations.literal: Dai Yang said, "Your lordship's natal stem sits in shen; metal is earth's controlling agent, yet on shen above Stone Citadel they have set a smeltery—firelight shines to heaven; this is metal and fire scorching each other, water and fire seething each other—therefore you suffer harm."
translations.idiomatic: He traced Wang Dao's fate to the shen stem, where a royal foundry atop Stone Citadel set metal and fire at war and poisoned the patron of earth.

sentences.zh: 」導即移居東府，病遂差。

translations.literal: " Dao immediately moved residence to the Eastern Bureau, and the illness then improved.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao relocated to the Eastern Secretariat compound and recovered.

sentences.zh: 鎮東從事中郎張闓舉洋為丞相令史。

translations.literal: Army aide to the General Who Guards the East Zhang Kai recommended Dai Yang as clerical secretary to the Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Kai, staff officer to the general who guards the east, recommended him as a chancellery clerk.

sentences.zh: 時司馬颺為烏程令，將赴職，洋曰：「君宜深慎下吏。

translations.literal: At that time Sima Yang was magistrate of Wucheng and was about to take up the post; Dai Yang said, "You ought deeply to beware your subordinate clerks."
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Yang left for his Wucheng magistracy, Dai Yang warned him to watch his underlings.

sentences.zh: 」揚後果坐吏免官。

translations.literal: " Yang later indeed lost office because of a clerk's crime.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yang was cashiered when a clerk's guilt touched him.

sentences.zh: 洋又謂曰：「卿雖免官，十一月當作郡，加將軍。

translations.literal: Dai Yang also told him, "Though you lose office, in the eleventh month you will become a governor and receive the title of general."
translations.idiomatic: Dai Yang added that in the eleventh month he would govern a commandery with a general's commission.

sentences.zh: 」至期，為太山太守、鎮武將軍。

translations.literal: " When the term arrived, he became governor of Taishan and General Who Guards Martial Might.
translations.idiomatic: On the date he was named Taishan governor and general who guards martial might.

sentences.zh: 颺賣宅將行，洋止之曰：「君不得至，當還，不可無宅。

translations.literal: Sima Yang sold his house and was about to depart; Dai Yang stopped him, saying, "You will not reach your post—you will return; you cannot be without a house."
translations.idiomatic: As Sima Yang sold his house to leave, Dai Yang told him he would never reach Taishan and must keep a roof in the capital.

sentences.zh: 」颺果為徐龕所逼，不得之郡。

translations.literal: " Yang was indeed harried by Xu Kan and could not reach the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Kan's revolt blocked his march and sent him home.

sentences.zh: 元帝增颺眾二千，使助祖逖。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan added two thousand men to Yang's forces to assist Zu Ti.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan bolstered Sima Yang with two thousand troops for Zu Ti's campaign.

sentences.zh: 洋勸颺不行，颺乃稱疾。

translations.literal: Dai Yang urged Yang not to go; Yang then pleaded illness.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Yang begged him not to march; Sima Yang pleaded sickness instead.

sentences.zh: 收付廷尉，俄而因赦得出。

translations.literal: He was seized and delivered to the minister of justice; before long, thanks to an amnesty, he was released.
translations.idiomatic: The court jailed him briefly until an amnesty freed him.

sentences.zh: 元帝將登阼，使洋擇日，洋以為宜用三月二十四日丙午。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan was about to ascend the throne, he had Dai Yang choose the day; Dai Yang held that the third month, twenty-fourth day, bingwu, ought to be used.
translations.idiomatic: For Yuan-di's enthronement Dai Yang picked the bingwu day of the third month's twenty-fourth.

sentences.zh: 太史令陳卓奏用二十二日，言：「昔越王用甲辰三月反國，范蠡稱在陽之前，當主盡出，上下盡空，德將出遊，刑入中宮，今與此同。

translations.literal: Grand Astrologer Chen Zhuo memorialized to use the twenty-second day, saying, "In olden days the king of Yue used jiachen in the third month to return to his state; Fan Li said that while yang had not yet fully emerged, the host qi was utterly out and the upper and lower utterly empty, virtue was about to go forth on tour, and punishment entered the central palace—today matches that."
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zhuo countered with the twenty-second, citing Yue's jiachen return and Fan Li's doctrine of empty hosts and wandering virtue.

sentences.zh: 」洋曰：「越王為吳所囚，雖當時遜媚，實懷怨憤，蠡故用甲辰，乘德而歸，留刑吳宮。

translations.literal: " Dai Yang said, "The king of Yue was imprisoned by Wu; though at the time he was submissive and ingratiating, in truth he harbored resentment and rage; Fan Li therefore used jiachen, riding virtue home while leaving punishment in Wu's palace.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Yang replied that Goujian's calendar trick had humiliated a captor-king, not crowned a legitimate heir.

sentences.zh: 今大王內無含咎，外無怨憤，當承天洪命，納祚無窮，何為追越王去國留殃故事邪！

translations.literal: " Now the great king harbors no hidden fault within and bears no resentment without—he ought to receive Heaven's great mandate and take the blessing without end—why chase the precedent of the Yue king's leaving his state and leaving calamity behind!"
translations.idiomatic: Yuan-di, he argued, was blameless and free of grudge—he should accept an auspicious enthronement date, not Yue's vengeful omen.

sentences.zh: 」乃從之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the court followed him.
translations.idiomatic: The throne accepted Dai Yang's day.

sentences.zh: 及祖約代兄鎮譙，請洋為中典軍，遷督護。

translations.literal: When Zu Yue replaced his elder brother in garrisoning Qiao, he invited Dai Yang as Central Army aide and promoted him to superintendent.
translations.idiomatic: When Zu Yue succeeded his brother on the Qiao front, he took Dai Yang as central-army adviser and raised him to superintendent.

sentences.zh: 四月庚辰，禺中時有大風，起自東南，折木。

translations.literal: On gengchen in the fourth month, at the yuzhong double-hour, there was a great wind rising from the southeast that broke trees.
translations.idiomatic: On a fourth-month gengchen day, midmorning brought a southeast gale that snapped trees.

sentences.zh: 洋謂約曰：「十月必有賊到譙城東，至曆陽，南方有反者。

translations.literal: Dai Yang said to Yue, "In the tenth month bandits are sure to reach east of Qiao city as far as Liyang; south of that there will be rebels."
translations.idiomatic: Dai Yang told Zu Yue that raiders would strike east of Qiao toward Liyang in the tenth month while the south also rose in revolt.

sentences.zh: 」主簿王振以洋為妖，白約收洋，付刺奸而絕其食五十日，言語如故。

translations.literal: " Registrar Wang Zhen, deeming Dai Yang a sorcerer, reported to Yue to seize Dai Yang; he was handed to the censorial jail and denied food for fifty days, yet his speech was as before.
translations.idiomatic: Registrar Wang Zhen called it witchcraft and had him starved fifty days in the interrogation cells without breaking him.

sentences.zh: 約知其有神術，乃赦之而讓振。

translations.literal: Yue knew he possessed spirit-like techniques; thereupon he pardoned him and rebuked Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Yue saw his power was real, freed him, and scolded Wang Zhen.

sentences.zh: 振後有罪被收，洋救之。

translations.literal: Later Zhen had a crime and was arrested; Dai Yang saved him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Zhen later faced charges, Dai Yang interceded.

sentences.zh: 約曰：「振往日相系，今何以救之？

translations.literal: Yue said, "Zhen in former days bound you—why now save him?"
translations.idiomatic: Zu Yue asked why he would rescue a man who had chained him.

sentences.zh: 」洋曰：「振不識風角，非有宿嫌。

translations.literal: " Dai Yang said, "Zhen did not understand fengjiao; there was no old grudge."
translations.idiomatic: Dai Yang said Wang Zhen had acted from ignorance, not malice.

sentences.zh: 振往時垂餓死，洋養活之，振猶尚遺忘。

translations.literal: " At the time Zhen was on the verge of starving to death; Dai Yang fed and kept him alive, yet Zhen still afterward forgot.
translations.idiomatic: He reminded Zu Yue that he had once fed Wang Zhen when the clerk was starving—a debt Wang Zhen forgot.

sentences.zh: 夫處富貴而不棄貧賤甚難。

translations.literal: " To dwell in wealth and honor yet not cast aside the poor and lowly is very difficult."
translations.idiomatic: Few who sit in silk remember friends in rags.

sentences.zh: 」約義之，即原振，賜洋米三十石。

translations.literal: " Yue deemed this righteous; he immediately pardoned Zhen and granted Dai Yang thirty shi of rice.
translations.idiomatic: Moved, Zu Yue spared Wang Zhen and paid Dai Yang thirty shi of grain.

sentences.zh: 至十月三日，石勒騎果到譙城東。

translations.literal: On the third day of the tenth month, Shi Le's cavalry indeed arrived east of Qiao city.
translations.idiomatic: On the third day of the tenth month, Shi Le's horsemen appeared east of Qiao, exactly as Dai Yang had said.

sentences.zh: 洋言於約曰：「賊必向城父，可遣騎水南追之，步軍于水北斷要路，賊必敗。

translations.literal: Yang said to Yue, "The bandits are sure to make for Chengfu; you may send horse south of the water to pursue them, and foot soldiers north of the water to block the choke points—the bandits will surely be crushed."
translations.idiomatic: Dai Yang urged Zu Yue: "They will strike for Chengfu—ride around the south bank to catch them, seal the fords on the north bank, and you will break them."

sentences.zh: 」約竟不追，賊乃掠城父婦女輜重而去。

translations.literal: " Yue in the end did not pursue; the bandits therefore plundered the women, baggage, and heavy carts of Chengfu and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Yue refused to move; the raiders looted Chengfu's people and wagons and rode away unopposed.

sentences.zh: 約將魯延求追賊，洋曰：「不可。

translations.literal: Yue's general Lu Yan requested to pursue the bandits; Yang said, "It cannot be done."
translations.idiomatic: General Lu Yan begged leave to pursue, but Dai Yang said, "Do not send them."

sentences.zh: 」約不從，使兄子智與延追之。

translations.literal: " Yue did not follow this; he sent his elder brother's son Zhi together with Yan to pursue them.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Yue ignored the warning and dispatched his nephew Zu Zhi alongside Lu Yan.

sentences.zh: 賊偽棄婦女輜重走，智與延等爭物，賊還掩之，智、延僅以身免，士卒皆死。

translations.literal: The bandits feigned abandoning women, baggage, and heavy carts and fled; Zhi and Yan and the others vied for the goods; the bandits turned back and ambushed them—Zhi and Yan barely escaped with their lives, while the soldiers all died.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy dropped camp followers and supply carts as bait; Zu Zhi and Lu Yan fell to looting, whereupon the riders doubled back and cut them to pieces. The two commanders fled alone; every trooper perished.

sentences.zh: 約表洋為下邑長。

translations.literal: Yue memorialized recommending Yang as magistrate of Xiayi.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Yue had him appointed magistrate of Xiayi in recognition of his counsel.

sentences.zh: 時梁國人反，逐太守袁晏。

translations.literal: At that time the people of Liang state rebelled and drove out Governor Yuan Yan.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Liang commandery rose up and expelled their governor, Yuan Yan.

sentences.zh: 梁城峻險，約欲討之而未決，洋曰：「賊以八月辛酉日反，日辰俱王，辛德在南方，酉受自刑，梁在譙北，乘德伐刑，賊必破亡。

translations.literal: Liang city was steep and perilous; Yue wished to punish them but had not decided; Yang said, "The bandits rebelled on the xinyou day of the eighth month; day and hour stems both sit as 'king'; xin's virtue lies in the south, while you bears self-punishment; Liang lies north of Qiao—riding virtue to strike a self-punishing stem, the bandits will surely be destroyed."
translations.idiomatic: Liang's walls were formidable and Zu Yue hesitated. Dai Yang read the stems: "They rose on xinyou in the eighth month when day and hour both read 'ruler'; xin's power lies south while the you branch turns on itself—Liang sits north of Qiao, so your host rides ascendant virtue against a self-consuming sign and the rebels cannot endure."

sentences.zh: 又甲子日東風而雷西行，譙在東南，雷在軍前，為軍驅除。

translations.literal: Moreover, on the jiazi day the east wind blew while thunder moved westward; Qiao lies southeast; thunder was before the army—it clears the path for the army.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, on a jiazi day an east wind carried thunder westward; Qiao lies southeast of that path, so the peal clears the road ahead of your host.

sentences.zh: 昔吳伐關羽，天雷在前，周瑜拜賀。

translations.literal: In the past when Wu attacked Guan Yu, heaven's thunder went before the army, and Zhou Yu bowed in congratulation.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu struck Guan Yu, lightning heralded the advance, and Zhou Yu hailed it as a good omen.

sentences.zh: 今與往同，故知必克。

translations.literal: Now it matches what went before; therefore I know we will surely prevail.
translations.idiomatic: The signs match that campaign—we will take Liang."

sentences.zh: 」約從之，果平梁城。

translations.literal: " Yue followed him and indeed pacified Liang city.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Yue listened and reduced Liang as predicted.

sentences.zh: 正月，有大流星東南行，洋曰：「至秋，府當移壽陽。

translations.literal: In the first month there was a great broom star moving southeast; Yang said, "By autumn the headquarters ought to shift to Shouyang."
translations.idiomatic: A great meteor streaked southeast in the first month; Dai Yang said, "Before autumn your command post will move to Shouyang."

sentences.zh: 」及王敦作逆，約問其勝敗，洋曰：「太白在東方，辰星不出。

translations.literal: " When Wang Dun rebelled, Yue asked him about victory and defeat; Yang said, "Taibai is in the east; the Chen star does not appear.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Dun turned traitor, Zu Yue asked the outcome. Dai Yang replied, "Venus hangs in the east and Mercury stays hidden.

sentences.zh: 兵法先起為主，應者為客。

translations.literal: In military doctrine he who rises first is host, he who responds is guest.
translations.idiomatic: By the art of war the first mover is 'host' and the responder is 'guest.'

sentences.zh: 辰星若出，太白為主，辰星為客。

translations.literal: If the Chen star should appear, Taibai is host and Chen is guest.
translations.idiomatic: If Mercury rises, Venus counts as host and Mercury as guest.

sentences.zh: 辰星不出，太白為客，先起兵者敗。

translations.literal: If the Chen star does not appear, Taibai is guest—whoever raises troops first will be defeated.
translations.idiomatic: With Mercury still absent, Venus plays guest: the side that strikes first loses."

sentences.zh: 今有客無主，有前無後，宜傳檄所部，應詔伐之。

translations.literal: Now there is a guest without a host, advance without rear—you ought to circulate proclamations through your command and answer the imperial summons to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Today you have a foe without a champion in the field—no depth behind the vanguard. Issue orders up and down the army and march under edict to crush him."

sentences.zh: 」約乃率眾向合肥。

translations.literal: " Yue thereupon led the host toward Hefei.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Yue marched his army toward Hefei.

sentences.zh: 俄而敦死眾敗，遂住壽陽。

translations.literal: Before long Dun died and the host was defeated; he then halted at Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun soon died and his forces scattered; Zu Yue ended up stationed at Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 洋又曰：「江淮之間當有軍事，譙城虛曠，宜還固守。

translations.literal: Yang also said, "Between the Yangzi and Huai there will be military affairs; Qiao city is empty and open—you ought to return and hold it fast.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Yang added, "Trouble is brewing between the Yangzi and the Huai. Qiao lies empty—you should fall back and fortify it.

sentences.zh: 不者，雍丘、沛皆非官有也。

translations.literal: If not, neither Yongqiu nor Pei will remain in official hands."
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise you will lose Yongqiu and Pei alike to the enemy."

sentences.zh: 」約不從，豫土遂陷於賊。

translations.literal: " Yue did not follow; the lands of Yu therefore fell into the hands of bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Yue ignored him, and the Central Plain south of the Yellow River slipped into rebel hands.

sentences.zh: 春，約南行佃，遇大雷雨西南來，洋曰：「甲子西南天雷，其夏必失大將。

translations.literal: In spring Yue went south to till the fields; he met a great thunderstorm coming from the southwest; Yang said, "Jiazi day, heaven's thunder in the southwest—in that summer you will surely lose a great general."
translations.idiomatic: That spring Zu Yue rode south to oversee the harvest and met a thunderstorm out of the southwest. Dai Yang warned, "Thunder from the southwest on a jiazi day means you will lose a major general that summer."

sentences.zh: 」至夏，汝南人反，執約兄子濟，送于石勒。

translations.literal: " When summer came, the people of Runan rebelled, seized Yue's elder brother's son Ji, and delivered him to Shi Le.
translations.idiomatic: That summer Runan rose in revolt, captured Zu Yue's nephew Zu Ji, and handed him to Shi Le.

sentences.zh: 約府內地忽赤如丹，洋曰：「案《河圖徵》云：『地赤如丹血丸丸，當有下反上者。

translations.literal: The ground inside Yue's headquarters suddenly turned red as cinnabar; Yang said, "According to the Hetu zheng, 'When the earth is red as cinnabar like blood pellets, there will be one below who rebels against those above."
translations.idiomatic: The soil inside Zu Yue's compound flushed red as lacquer. Dai Yang cited the River Chart augury: "When the ground turns cinnabar-red like clots of blood, inferiors will revolt against superiors."

sentences.zh: 』恐十月二十七日胡馬當來飲淮水。

translations.literal: " I fear on the twenty-seventh day of the tenth month Hu horses will come to drink at the Huai."
translations.idiomatic: I dread the twenty-seventh of the tenth month, when barbarian horses will drink from the Huai."

sentences.zh: 」至時，石勒騎大至，攻城大戰。

translations.literal: " When the time came, Shi Le's riders arrived in great numbers and assaulted the city in a great battle.
translations.idiomatic: On that day Shi Le's cavalry closed in and a fierce siege battle erupted.

sentences.zh: 其日西風，兵火俱發，約大懼。

translations.literal: That day the west wind blew; weapons and fire both sprang up; Yue was greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: A gale blew from the west; fire and arms flared together, and Zu Yue was terrified.

sentences.zh: 會風回，賊退。

translations.literal: Then the wind shifted and the bandits withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Then the wind swung round and the attackers drew off.

sentences.zh: 時傳言勒遣騎向壽陽，約欲送其家還江東，洋曰：「必無此事。

translations.literal: At that time rumor said Le was sending riders toward Shouyang; Yue wished to send his household back east of the Yangzi; Yang said, "Surely there will not be such a matter."
translations.idiomatic: Rumors claimed Shi Le was riding on Shouyang; Zu Yue prepared to evacuate his family to the southland. Dai Yang said the report was false.

sentences.zh: 」尋而傳言果妄。

translations.literal: " Before long the rumor indeed proved false.
translations.idiomatic: The scare proved baseless.

sentences.zh: 咸和初，月暈左角，有赤白珥。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Xianhe reign, the moon haloed the left horn and had red and white secondary arcs.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xianhe, a lunar halo ringed the moon's left horn with crimson and white 'ears.'

sentences.zh: 約問洋，洋曰：「角為天門，開布陽道，官門當有大戰。

translations.literal: Yue asked Yang; Yang said, "The horn is Heaven's Gate; it opens the yang road—there ought to be a great battle at the palace gates."
translations.idiomatic: Zu Yue asked the meaning. Dai Yang said, "The horn is the Gate of Heaven; when it opens the yang road, bloodshed reaches the palace."

sentences.zh: 」俄而蘇峻遣使招約俱反，洋謂約曰：「蘇峻必敗，然其初起，兵鋒不可當，可外和內嚴，以待其變。

translations.literal: " Before long Su Jun sent an envoy to summon Yue to rebel together; Yang said to Yue, "Su Jun will surely be defeated, yet at first his spearpoint cannot be withstood—you may treat him outwardly as ally while steeling yourself within, and await his change."
translations.idiomatic: Soon Su Jun invited Zu Yue into his revolt. Dai Yang warned, "Su Jun is doomed, but his first rush will be unstoppable—feign accord while tightening your guard and wait for his tide to turn."

sentences.zh: 」約不從，遂與峻反。

translations.literal: " Yue did not follow and thereupon joined Jun in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Yue refused the advice and cast his lot with Su Jun.

sentences.zh: 至三年五月，大風雷雨西北來，城內晦螟，洋謂約曰：「雷鳴人上，明使君當遠佞近直，愛下振貧。

translations.literal: By the fifth month of the third year a great wind and thunderstorm came from the northwest; inside the city it grew dark as twilight; Yang said to Yue, "Thunder rolls over men—this means the enlightened lord should cast off flatterers, draw near the upright, cherish subordinates, and relieve the poor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the third Xianhe year a northwest storm plunged the city into gloom. Dai Yang told Zu Yue, "Thunder over the people means the governor must banish sycophants, embrace honest men, care for the ranks, and succor the destitute.

sentences.zh: 昔秦有此變，卒致亂亡。

translations.literal: In antiquity Qin had this omen and in the end met chaos and ruin."
translations.idiomatic: Qin saw the same sign and fell to ruin."

sentences.zh: 」約大怒，收洋系之。

translations.literal: " Yue raged greatly, seized Yang, and bound him.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Yue flew into a rage and had Dai Yang thrown in chains.

sentences.zh: 遣部將李概將兵到盧江，其眾盡散。

translations.literal: He sent his division commander Li Gai to lead troops to Lujiang; the host entirely scattered.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched Li Gai toward Lujiang, but the column melted away.

sentences.zh: 約召洋出，問之曰：「吾還東何如留壽陽？

translations.literal: Yue summoned Yang out and asked him, "How would it be if I return east versus remaining at Shouyang?
translations.idiomatic: Zu Yue released Dai Yang and asked whether to retreat east or stay in Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 若留壽陽，何如入胡？

translations.literal: If I remain at Shouyang, how would it be to enter among the Hu?"
translations.idiomatic: If he stayed, should he next throw in with the barbarians?"

sentences.zh: 」洋曰：「東入失半，入胡滅門，留壽陽尚可。

translations.literal: " Yang said, "Going east you lose half; entering among the Hu exterminates the whole gate; remaining at Shouyang is still tolerable."
translations.idiomatic: Dai Yang answered, "Flight east costs you half your following; submission to the Hu wipes out your house; holding Shouyang is the least ill choice."

sentences.zh: 」約欲東向曆陽，其眾不樂東下，皆叛約，劫約姊及嫂奔于石勒。

translations.literal: " Yue wished to go east toward Liyang; his host was not pleased to go down east and all rebelled against Yue, seizing Yue's elder sister and sister-in-law and fleeing to Shi Le.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Yue tried to march for Liyang, but his troops refused to go east, mutinied, and carried his sister and sister-in-law off to Shi Le.

sentences.zh: 約到曆陽，祖煥問洋曰：「君昔言平西在壽陽可得五年，果如君言。

translations.literal: When Yue reached Liyang, Zu Huan asked Yang, "You once said the Pacifier of the West could hold Shouyang five years at Shouyang—it indeed matched your words.
translations.idiomatic: At Liyang, Zu Huan reminded Dai Yang, "You said the 'Pacifier of the West' could keep Shouyang five years, and you were right.

sentences.zh: 今在曆陽，可得幾時？

translations.literal: Now that he is at Liyang, how many seasons may he have?"
translations.idiomatic: Now that he is here in Liyang, how long does he have?"

sentences.zh: 」洋曰：「得六月耳。

translations.literal: " Yang said, "He will obtain six months, that is all."
translations.idiomatic: Dai Yang said, "Six months, no more."

sentences.zh: 」約問洋：「台下及此氣侯何如？

translations.literal: " Yue asked Yang, "How are the astrological signs below the terrace and here?"
translations.idiomatic: Zu Yue pressed him about omens at court and in the field.

sentences.zh: 」洋曰：「此當復有反者。

translations.literal: " Yang said, "Here there will again be a rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Yang replied, "Another revolt stirs here.

sentences.zh: 台下來年三月當太平，江州當大喪。

translations.literal: Below the terrace, in the third month of next year there will be peace; Jiangzhou will have a great mourning.
translations.idiomatic: The capital will quiet down by the third month of next year, but Jiangzhou will suffer a great bereavement.

sentences.zh: 後南方復有軍事，去此千里。

translations.literal: Afterward there will again be military affairs in the south, a thousand li from this place."
translations.idiomatic: Later still, fighting will flare a thousand li to the south."

sentences.zh: 」尋而牽騰叛約，約率所親將家屬奔于石勒。

translations.literal: " Before long Qian Teng rebelled against Yue; Yue led his intimate followers and moved dependents in flight to Shi Le.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Qian Teng turned on Zu Yue; Zu fled with kinsmen and clients to Shi Le.

sentences.zh: 二月而天子反正，四月而溫嶠卒，郭默據湓口以叛。

translations.literal: In the second month the Son of Heaven returned to normal rule; in the fourth month Wen Jiao died; Guo Mo seized Penkou in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: The second month saw the emperor restored; in the fourth month Wen Jiao died, and Guo Mo seized Penkou in revolt.

sentences.zh: 後勒誅約及親屬並盡，皆如洋言。

translations.literal: Later Le executed Yue and his kin to the last person—all as Yang had said.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le later executed Zu Yue and wiped out his entire clan—just as Dai Yang had foretold.

sentences.zh: 約既敗，洋往尋陽。

translations.literal: After Yue was defeated, Yang went to Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Zu Yue fell, Dai Yang made his way to Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 時劉胤鎮尋陽，胤問洋曰：「我病當差不？

translations.literal: At that time Liu Yin garrisoned Xunyang; Yin asked Yang, "Will my illness improve or not?"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yin, who held Xunyang, asked whether he would recover from his illness.

sentences.zh: 」洋曰：「不憂使君不差，憂使君今年有大厄。

translations.literal: " Yang said, "I do not worry that the lord will not improve; I worry that the lord has a great misfortune this year.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Yang said, "Your sickness is not what troubles me; this year brings you a far worse stroke of fate.

sentences.zh: 使君年四十七，行年入庚寅。

translations.literal: The lord is forty-seven years of age; the annual cycle enters gengyin.
translations.idiomatic: You are forty-seven, and your annual star has entered gengyin.

sentences.zh: 《太公陰謀》曰：『六庚為白獸，在上為客星，在下為害氣。

translations.literal: The Taigong yinmou says, 'The six geng are the white beast; above they are the guest star, below they are the baleful qi."
translations.idiomatic: The Taigong yinmou says, "The six geng days are the White Beast—above they mark the guest star, below they unleash baleful qi."

sentences.zh: 』年與命並，必凶當忌。

translations.literal: " When the year and fate align, it is surely inauspicious and ought to be shunned.
translations.idiomatic: When the year-pillar matches your nativity, disaster follows unless you ward it off.

sentences.zh: 十二月二十二日庚寅勿見客。

translations.literal: On the twenty-second day of the twelfth month, gengyin, do not receive guests."
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-second of the twelfth month, a gengyin day, admit no visitors."

sentences.zh: 」胤曰：「我當解職，將君還野中治病。

translations.literal: " Yin said, "I shall resign office and take you back to the wilds to cure the illness."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yin said, "I will resign and retire with you to the countryside to heal."

sentences.zh: 」洋曰：「使君當作江州，不得解職。

translations.literal: " Yang said, "The lord will become governor of Jiangzhou; you cannot resign office."
translations.idiomatic: Dai Yang answered, "You are fated to govern Jiangzhou—you cannot step down."

sentences.zh: 」胤曰：「溫公不復還邪？

translations.literal: " Yin said, "Will Lord Wen not return?"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yin asked, "Will Minister Wen not come back from the capital?"

sentences.zh: 」洋曰：「溫公雖還，使君故作江州。

translations.literal: " Yang said, "Although Lord Wen returns, the lord will still become governor of Jiangzhou."
translations.idiomatic: Dai Yang said, "Even when Wen returns, you will still take Jiangzhou."

sentences.zh: 」俄如其言。

translations.literal: " Before long it was as he had said.
translations.idiomatic: Events unfolded exactly as he predicted.

sentences.zh: 九月甲寅申時，回風從東來，入胤兒船中，西過，狀如匹練，長五六丈。

translations.literal: On jiayin in the ninth month, at the shen double-hour, a whirlwind came from the east, entered Yin's son's boat, passed westward, shaped like a bolt of plain silk, five or six zhang long.
translations.idiomatic: On a jiayin day in the ninth month, around midafternoon, a whirlwind blew from the east into Liu Yin's son's boat, then swept westward like a five- or six-zhang ribbon of cloth.

sentences.zh: 洋曰：「風從咸池下來，攝提下去，咸池為刀兵，大殺為死喪。

translations.literal: Yang said, "The wind came down from the Xianchi pool; Sheti sank below—Xianchi means blades and weapons, great killing means death and mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Yang said, "That wind dropped from the Xianchi asterism while Sheti sank below—Xianchi presages arms, and 'great killing' means death.

sentences.zh: 到甲子日申時，府內大聚骨理之。

translations.literal: At the jiazi day shen double-hour, inside the headquarters they will greatly gather bones and bury them."
translations.idiomatic: On the next jiazi day at the shen hour your staff will gather a great heap of bones for burial."

sentences.zh: 胤問在何處，洋曰：「不出州府門也。

translations.literal: Yin asked where it would be; Yang said, "It will not go outside the gate of the provincial headquarters."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yin asked where; Dai Yang said, "Within the walls of your command—not beyond the gate."

sentences.zh: 」胤架府東門。

translations.literal: " Yin erected scaffolding at the east gate of the headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yin had scaffolding raised at the east gate of his compound.

sentences.zh: 洋又曰：「東為天牢，牢下開門，憂天獄至。

translations.literal: Yang also said, "East is Heaven's prison; opening a gate beneath the prison means worry that Heaven's jail will arrive."
translations.idiomatic: Dai Yang added, "East is the Celestial Prison; opening a gate under it invites heaven's dungeon to close on you."

sentences.zh: 」十二月十七日，洋又曰：「臘近可閉門，以五十人備守，並以百人備東北寅上，以卻害氣。

translations.literal: " On the seventeenth day of the twelfth month Yang again said, "The la sacrifice nears—you ought to close the gates, with fifty men on guard, and also a hundred men posted northeast on the yin position, to repel the baleful qi."
translations.idiomatic: On the seventeenth of the twelfth month he warned again: "Seal the gates for the year-end rites—fifty guards on the doors and a hundred men on the northeast yin corner to turn the baleful qi."

sentences.zh: 」胤不從。

translations.literal: " Yin did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yin ignored him.

sentences.zh: 二十四日壬辰，胤遂為郭默所害。

translations.literal: On the twenty-fourth day, renchen, Yin was thereupon killed by Guo Mo.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-fourth, a renchen day, Guo Mo murdered Liu Yin.

sentences.zh: 南中郎將桓宣以洋為參軍，將隨宣往襄陽，太尉陶侃留之住武昌。

translations.literal: General of the Center of the South Huan Xuan appointed Yang adjutant; he was about to follow Xuan to Xiangyang, but Grand Commandant Tao Kan detained him to stay at Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: General Huan Xuan took Dai Yang as adjutant for a march to Xiangyang, but Grand Commandant Tao Kan kept him at Wuchang instead.

sentences.zh: 時侃謀北伐，洋曰：「前年十一月熒惑守胃昴，至今年四月，積五百餘日。

translations.literal: At that time Kan planned a northern expedition; Yang said, "In the eleventh month of the year before last Yinghuo guarded Mao and Mao for more than five hundred days until this year's fourth month.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan was planning a northern strike. Dai Yang said, "Mars lingered in the Pleiades and Hyades from the eleventh month of before last until the fourth month of this year—more than five hundred days.

sentences.zh: 昴，趙之分野，石勒遂死。

translations.literal: Mao is Zhao's field division; Shi Le thereupon died.
translations.idiomatic: Those lodges mark the Zhao sector; Shi Le died under that sign.

sentences.zh: 熒惑以七月退，從畢右順行入黃道，未及天關，以八月二十二日復逆行還鉤，繞畢向昴。

translations.literal: Yinghuo withdrew in the seventh month, moving rightward with direct motion along the Yellow Path from Bi; it had not yet reached the Celestial Pass when on the twenty-second day of the eighth month it again moved retrograde back to the Hook, encircled Bi, and headed toward Mao.
translations.idiomatic: Mars went direct in the seventh month, sliding east along the ecliptic from the Net; before it reached the Celestial Gate it turned retrograde on the twenty-second of the eighth, looped through the Hook, skirted the Net, and bore down on the Pleiades again.

sentences.zh: 昴畢為邊兵，主胡夷，故置天弓以射之。

translations.literal: Mao and Bi mean frontier troops and govern the Hu and Yi; therefore Heaven sets the Bow to shoot at them.
translations.idiomatic: The Net and Pleiades govern border hosts and northern tribes—heaven strings the Bow to shoot them down.

sentences.zh: 熒惑逆行，司無德之國，石勒死是也。

translations.literal: Yinghuo's retrograde motion punishes a state without virtue—Shi Le's death is a case of this.
translations.idiomatic: Retrograde Mars punishes a realm without virtue; Shi Le's end fits the pattern.

sentences.zh: 勒之餘燼，以自殘害。

translations.literal: What remains of Le's embers will harm one another by themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The sparks of his house will consume one another.

sentences.zh: 今年官與太歲、太陰三合癸巳，癸為北方，北方當受災。

translations.literal: This year the official star joins Grand Year and Grand Yin in a triple conjunction at guisi; gui is the north—the north ought to suffer disaster.
translations.idiomatic: This year the bureaucracy star, Jupiter, and Saturn meet in guisi; gui points north—calamity will strike the northern heartland.

sentences.zh: 歲鎮二星共合翼軫，從子及巳，徘徊六年。

translations.literal: The year and garrison stars together join Yi and Zhen, from zi to si, lingering six years.
translations.idiomatic: Jupiter and Saturn share the lodges Yi and Zhen from zi through si, hovering there six years.

sentences.zh: 荊楚之分，歲鎮所守，其下國昌，豈非功德之徵也！

translations.literal: That is the division of Jing and Chu; what year and garrison guard will thrive below—is this not a sign of merit and virtue!"
translations.idiomatic: Those stars watch the Jing-Chu sector—where they stand long, the state below flourishes. Surely that marks your merit!"

sentences.zh: 今年六月，鎮星前角亢。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of this year the garrison star moves before Horn and Gullet.
translations.idiomatic: This sixth month Saturn advances before Horn and Gullet.

sentences.zh: 角亢，鄭之分。

translations.literal: Horn and Gullet are Zheng's division.
translations.idiomatic: Horn and Gullet are the Zheng heartland.

sentences.zh: 歲星移入房，太白在心。

translations.literal: The year star moves into Room; Taibai is in Heart.
translations.idiomatic: Jupiter enters Room while Venus sits in Heart.

sentences.zh: 心房，宋分。

translations.literal: Heart and Room are Song's division.
translations.idiomatic: Heart and Room mark the Song sector.

sentences.zh: 順之者昌，逆之者亡。

translations.literal: Those who follow it thrive; those who oppose it perish.
translations.idiomatic: Follow heaven's pointer and you prosper; defy it and you perish.

sentences.zh: 石季龍若興兵東南，此其死會也。

translations.literal: If Shi Jilong raises troops toward the southeast, this will be the assembly of his death.
translations.idiomatic: If Shi Hu marches southeast, he walks into his own death day.

sentences.zh: 官若應天伐刑，徑據宋鄭，則無敵矣。

translations.literal: If the court responds to Heaven and punishes guilt, striking straight at Song and Zheng, then there will be no match.
translations.idiomatic: If the court rides those signs to punish evil and seizes Song and Zheng, no enemy will withstand you.

sentences.zh: 若天與不取，反受其咎。

translations.literal: If Heaven grants and you do not take, you will instead receive its blame.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven offers the chance—refuse it and you invite disaster on yourself.

sentences.zh: 」侃志在中原，聞而大喜。

translations.literal: " Kan's ambition lay in the Central Plain; hearing this he was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan's heart was set on the north; the reading delighted him.

sentences.zh: 會病篤，不果行。

translations.literal: It happened that he was gravely ill and in the end could not go.
translations.idiomatic: He fell mortally ill and never marched.

sentences.zh: 侃薨，征西將軍庾亮代鎮武昌，復引洋問氣侯。

translations.literal: When Kan died, General Who Conquers the West Yu Liang replaced him at Wuchang and again summoned Yang to ask about astrological signs.
translations.idiomatic: After Tao Kan died, Yu Liang succeeded him at Wuchang and again consulted Dai Yang on the omens.

sentences.zh: 洋曰：「天有白氣，喪必東行，不過數年必應。

translations.literal: Yang said, "There is white qi in the sky—mourning will surely move eastward; within a few years it will respond."
translations.idiomatic: Dai Yang said, "A white vapor spans the sky—bereavement is traveling east and will show itself within a few years."

sentences.zh: 」尋有大鹿向西城門，洋曰：「野獸向城，主人將去。

translations.literal: " Before long a great deer went toward the west city gate; Yang said, "When wild beasts face the city, the master will depart."
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward a huge deer walked toward the west gate. Dai Yang said, "Beasts turning on the walls mean the lord will leave."

sentences.zh: 」城東家夜半望見城內有數炬火，從城上出，如大車狀，白布幔覆，與火俱出城東北行，至江乃滅。

translations.literal: " A family east of the city at midnight saw several torch fires inside the city emerge from atop the wall, shaped like great carts, covered with white cloth canopies; together with the fire they went out northeast of the city, reached the river, and were extinguished."
translations.idiomatic: That night townsfolk east of the wall saw balls of flame lift from the battlements like covered wagons swathed in white; they drifted northeast out of the city, reached the river, and vanished.

sentences.zh: 洋聞而歎曰：「此與前白氣同。

translations.literal: When Yang heard this he sighed and said, "This is the same as the white qi before."
translations.idiomatic: Dai Yang heard the tale and murmured, "That is the same white vapor I warned about."

sentences.zh: 」時亮欲西鎮石城，或問洋：「此西足當欲東不？

translations.literal: At that time Liang wished to move west and garrison Stone Rampart; someone asked Yang, "By this move west, is it enough to block the wish to go east?"
translations.idiomatic: Yu Liang meant to shift his seat west to Stone City; someone asked Dai Yang whether that would check an eastward push.

sentences.zh: 」洋曰：「不當也。

translations.literal: Yang said, "It is not adequate."
translations.idiomatic: Dai Yang said, "No—that will not answer the threat."

sentences.zh: 」，洋言於亮曰：「武昌土地有山無林，政可圖始，不可居終。

translations.literal: ", Yang said to Liang, "Wuchang's terrain has hills but no forest—it may serve to begin a venture, but it cannot be the final seat."
translations.idiomatic: He then told Yu Liang, "Wuchang is ridged and bare of woodland: fine for founding a foothold, fatal as a long-term capital."

sentences.zh: 山作八字，數不及九。

translations.literal: The hills form the character "eight"; the reckoning does not reach nine.
translations.idiomatic: The hills trace the form of the graph for "eight," and the numerology never reaches nine—a place that cannot endure.

sentences.zh: 昔吳用壬寅來上；

translations.literal: In the past Wu used renyin to come upriver;
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wu once chose a renyin year to move upstream;

sentences.zh: 創立宮城，至己酉，還下秣陵。

translations.literal: they founded the palace city, and by jiyou they returned down to Moling.
translations.idiomatic: they raised the palace there, yet by jiyou they had retreated again to Moling below.

sentences.zh: 陶公亦涉八年。

translations.literal: Lord Tao likewise crossed eight years.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan too held the place only eight years.

sentences.zh: 土地盛衰有數，人心去就有期，不可移也。

translations.literal: The rise and fall of land has its reckoning; the people's coming and going has its term—it cannot be shifted.
translations.idiomatic: Soil has its seasons of fortune, and popular allegiance its term—no edict can fix what heaven has timed.

sentences.zh: 公宜更擇吉處，武昌不可久住。

translations.literal: You ought to choose another auspicious site; Wuchang cannot be dwelt in long.
translations.idiomatic: You must pick a luckier seat; Wuchang will not hold you long."

sentences.zh: 」五年，亮令毛寶屯邾城。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Liang ordered Mao Bao to encamp at Zhucheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Yu Liang posted Mao Bao to garrison Zhucheng.

sentences.zh: 九月，洋言於亮曰：「毛豫州今年受死問。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Yang said to Liang, "Prefect Mao of Yu Province this year receives the query of death."
translations.idiomatic: That ninth month Dai Yang warned Yu Liang, "Your prefect Mao Bao carries a death omen this year."

sentences.zh: 昨朝大霧晏風，當有怨賊報仇，攻圍諸侯，誠宜遠偵邏。

translations.literal: This morning's great fog and late wind mean resentful bandits will take revenge and besiege a feudal lord—you truly ought to send scouts far afield."
translations.idiomatic: Heavy fog and a tardy wind mean vengeful raiders will ring a border town—double your patrols."

sentences.zh: 」寶問當在何時，答曰：「五十日內。

translations.literal: " Bao asked when it would be; he answered, "Within fifty days."
translations.idiomatic: Mao Bao asked the timing; Dai Yang answered, "Inside fifty days."

sentences.zh: 」其夕，又曰：「九月建戌，硃雀飛驚，征軍還歸，乘戴火光，天示有信，災發東房，葉落歸本，慮有後患。

translations.literal: " That evening he again said, "In the ninth month the month is founded on xu; the Vermilion Bird flies in alarm; the expedition army returns home, riding the fire light—Heaven shows faith; disaster breaks in the eastern chamber; leaves fall to the root—I fear there will be after trouble."
translations.idiomatic: That night he added arcana about the xu month, the Vermilion Bird, and fire omens—warning that ruin would strike the eastern wing and leave lasting trouble.

sentences.zh: 」明日，又曰：「昨夜火殃，非國福，今年架屋，致使君病，可因燒屋，移家南渡，無嫌也。

translations.literal: " The next day he again said, "Last night's fire calamity is not the state's blessing; this year you roofed houses and made the lord ill—you may burn the houses, move the family south across the river, and there will be no blame."
translations.idiomatic: Next morning he said the overnight blaze boded ill for the realm, blamed recent roofing for Yu Liang's illness, and urged burning the new halls and moving the household south.

sentences.zh: 」寶即遣兒婦還武昌。

translations.literal: " Bao thereupon sent his son's wife back to Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Bao sent his daughter-in-law back to Wuchang at once.

sentences.zh: 尋傳賊當來攻城，洋曰：「十月丁亥夜半時得賊問，幹為君，支為臣，丁為征西府，亥為邾城，功曹為賊神，加子時十月水王木相，王相氣合，賊必來。

translations.literal: Soon rumor said bandits would come to attack the city; Yang said, "On dinghai of the tenth month, at the midnight double-hour, you will obtain news of bandits: stem is lord, branch is minister; ding is the Western Expedition headquarters, hai is Zhucheng; the merit clerk is the bandit spirit; adding the zi hour, in the tenth month water is king and wood is minister—king and minister qi unite, so bandits will surely come."
translations.idiomatic: When word spread of a siege, Dai Yang cast the stems: at midnight on dinghai in the tenth month the divination showed the enemy would appear, with strengths between seven and nine thousand.

sentences.zh: 寅數七，子數九，賊高可九千人，下可七千人。

translations.literal: Yin's number is seven, zi 's number is nine; the bandits are high at about nine thousand men, low at about seven thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The oracle reckoned their strength at seven to nine thousand men.

sentences.zh: 從魁為貴人加丁，下克上，有空亡之事，不敢進武昌也。

translations.literal: Congkui is the noble man added to ding; below overcomes above; there is the affair of emptiness—they dare not advance on Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Other lines showed "emptiness"—they would not dare strike Wuchang itself.

sentences.zh: 」賊果陷邾城而去。

translations.literal: " The bandits indeed took Zhucheng and departed.
translations.idiomatic: The raiders did seize Zhucheng, then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 亮問洋曰：「故當不失石城否？

translations.literal: Liang asked Yang, "So we should not lose Stone Rampart after all?"
translations.idiomatic: Yu Liang asked whether Stone City would still hold.

sentences.zh: 」洋曰：「賊從安陸向石城，逆太白，當伐身，無所慮。

translations.literal: Yang said, "The bandits go from Anlu toward Stone Rampart, against Taibai—they will wound themselves; there is nothing to worry about."
translations.idiomatic: Dai Yang said their march from Anlu toward Stone City ran counter to Venus—they would hurt themselves; the rock fort was safe.

sentences.zh: 」亮曰：「天何以利胡而病我？

translations.literal: Liang said, "Why does Heaven favor the Hu and afflict us?"
translations.idiomatic: Yu Liang cried, "Why does Heaven bless the barbarians and scourge us?"

sentences.zh: 」洋曰：「天符有吉凶，土地有盛衰，今年害氣三合己亥，己為天下，亥為戎胡，季龍亦當受死。

translations.literal: Yang said, "Heaven's tallies have good and ill; land has rise and decay; this year the baleful qi triple-conjoins at jihai—ji is All-under-Heaven, hai is the Rong Hu; Jilong likewise ought to receive death."
translations.idiomatic: Dai Yang answered that heaven's signs cut both ways—this year baleful stars joined at jihai, marking the barbarians and predicting Shi Hu's death as well.

sentences.zh: 今乃不憂賊，但憂公病耳。

translations.literal: Now do not worry about the bandits—only worry about the lord's illness."
translations.idiomatic: Forget the enemy, he said; worry instead about Yu Liang's own sickness."

sentences.zh: 」亮曰：「何方救我疾？

translations.literal: Liang said, "From what direction may my illness be saved?"
translations.idiomatic: Yu Liang asked where to seek a cure.

sentences.zh: 」洋曰：「荊州受兵，江州受災，公可去此二州。

translations.literal: Yang said, "Jing Province receives arms; Jiang Province receives disaster—you may leave these two provinces."
translations.idiomatic: Dai Yang told him to quit both Jingzhou and Jiangzhou—the stars marked them for war and plague.

sentences.zh: 」亮曰：「如此，當有解不」？

translations.literal: Liang said, "If so, will there be relief?"
translations.idiomatic: Yu Liang asked, "Is there still a way out?"

sentences.zh: 」洋曰：「恨晚，猶差不也。

translations.literal: Yang said, "It is late, but there is still some improvement."
translations.idiomatic: Dai Yang said, "Very late—but partial relief remains possible."

sentences.zh: 」亮竟不能解二州，遂至大困。

translations.literal: " Liang in the end could not give up the two provinces, and thereupon came to great distress.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Liang could not abandon either command and sank into crisis.

sentences.zh: 洋曰：「昔蘇峻時，公于白石祠中祈福，許賽其牛，至今未解，故為此鬼所考。

translations.literal: Yang said, "In Su Jun's time you prayed for blessing in the Baishi shrine, vowing to repay it with an ox—you have never discharged it; therefore this ghost torments you."
translations.idiomatic: Dai Yang explained an unpaid vow—a promised ox at Baishi shrine during Su Jun's rebellion—that a lingering spirit now collected.

sentences.zh: 」亮曰：「有之，君是神人也。

translations.literal: Liang said, "There is such a thing—you are a spirit man."
translations.idiomatic: Yu Liang admitted the vow and called him a seer.

sentences.zh: 」或問洋曰：「庾公可得幾時？

translations.literal: Someone asked Yang, "How long may Lord Yu obtain?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked how long Yu Liang would live.

sentences.zh: 」洋曰：「見明年。

translations.literal: Yang said, "He will be seen until next year."
translations.idiomatic: Dai Yang said, "Only into next year."

sentences.zh: 」時亮已不識人，咸以為妄，果至正月一日而薨。

translations.literal: " At that time Liang already did not recognize people; all thought it wild talk, yet indeed on the first day of the first month he died.
translations.idiomatic: By then Yu Liang was beyond speech; courtiers mocked the prophecy—yet he died on New Year's Day.

sentences.zh: 庾翼代亮，洋復為占侯。

translations.literal: Yu Yi replaced Liang, and Yang again performed prognostications.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yi succeeded his brother, and Dai Yang continued casting omens for him.

sentences.zh: 少時卒，年八十餘。

translations.literal: Before long he died, aged over eighty.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Yang died in his eighties not long after.

sentences.zh: 所占驗者不可勝紀。

translations.literal: The hits he scored in divination cannot be fully recorded.
translations.idiomatic: His verified predictions are too many to list.

sentences.zh: 韓友

translations.literal: Han You.
translations.idiomatic: Han You

sentences.zh: 韓友，字景先，廬江舒人也。

translations.literal: Han You, style name Jingxian, was a man of Shu in Lujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Han You, courtesy name Jingxian, came from Shu county in Lujiang commandery.

sentences.zh: 為書生，受《易》于會稽伍振，善占卜，能圖宅相塚，亦行京費厭勝之術。

translations.literal: As a student he received the Changes from Wu Zhen of Kuaiji; he was good at divination, could chart dwellings and read tombs, and also practiced the Jing and Fei apotropaic arts.
translations.idiomatic: He studied the Zhouyi under Wu Zhen of Kuaiji, excelled at yarrow divination, geomancy of houses and graves, and the apotropaic methods of Jing Fang and Fei Zhi.

sentences.zh: 龍舒長鄧林婦病積年，垂死，醫巫皆息意。

translations.literal: The magistrate of Longshu, Deng Lin, had a wife who had been ill many years and was at the point of death; physicians and shamans had given up hope.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Lin, magistrate of Longshu, had a wife dying of a chronic malady after healers and exorcists had abandoned hope.

sentences.zh: 友為筮之，使畫作野豬著臥處屏風上，一宿覺佳，於是遂差。

translations.literal: You divined for her, had a wild boar painted and placed on the screen at her bed place; after one night she felt better, and then recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Han You cast the yarrow and told them to paint a boar on her bedside screen; overnight she rallied and then mended.

sentences.zh: 舒縣廷掾王睦病死，已復魄。

translations.literal: Wang Mu, clerk of Shu county, died of illness, then revived.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mu, a county clerk, had died and then returned to life.

sentences.zh: 友為筮之，令以丹畫版作日月置床頭，又以豹皮馬鄣泥臥上，立愈。

translations.literal: You divined for him, ordered cinnabar-painted boards with sun and moon placed at the head of the bed, and also leopard skin, a horse blind, and mud placed where he slept—he immediately recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Han You prescribed cinnabar sun-and-moon tablets at the pillow, leopard skin, a horse curtain, and clay on the couch—cures that worked at once.

sentences.zh: 劉世則女病魅積年，巫為攻禱，伐空塚故城間，得狸鼉數十，病猶不差。

translations.literal: Liu Shize's daughter was possessed for years; shamans attacked and prayed, felling empty tombs between old ramparts, and obtained dozens of badgers and soft-shelled turtles, yet the illness still did not improve.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shize's daughter suffered a long haunting; exorcists razed empty graves and dug up scores of badgers and turtles without curing her.

sentences.zh: 友筮之，命作布囊，依女發時，張囊著窗牖間，友閉戶作氣，若有所驅。

translations.literal: You divined, ordered a cloth bag made, and when the woman's hair rose, spread the bag at the window; You closed the door and made qi as if driving something.
translations.idiomatic: Han You had a linen sack hung in the window when her fits began, then shut the door and performed a breath ritual as though expelling a thing.

sentences.zh: 斯須之間，見囊大脹如吹，因決敗之，女仍大發。

translations.literal: In a moment the bag was seen to swell greatly as if blown; they therefore slit and broke it open, and the woman still had a great outbreak.
translations.idiomatic: The sack suddenly ballooned; they ripped it open, and the girl convulsed worse than ever.

sentences.zh: 友乃更作皮囊二枚，遝張之，施張如前，囊復脹滿。

translations.literal: You then made two leather bags, stacked them, spread them as before; the bags again swelled full.
translations.idiomatic: He made two leather bags, layered them as before, and again they bulged tight.

sentences.zh: 因急縛囊口，懸著樹二十許日，漸消，開視有二斤狐毛，女遂差。

translations.literal: Thereupon he urgently bound the bag mouths, hung them on a tree for about twenty days; they gradually shrank; opening and looking, there were two jin of fox fur, and the girl then recovered.
translations.idiomatic: He lashed the mouths shut and hung them in a tree for twenty days until they deflated, revealing two jin of fox fur inside—after which the girl healed.

sentences.zh: 宣城邊洪以四月中就友卜家中安否，友曰：「卿家有兵殃，其禍甚重。

translations.literal: Bian Hong of Xuancheng in the fourth month came to You to divine whether his household would be safe; You said, "Your household has the misfortune of arms; the disaster is very heavy."
translations.idiomatic: Bian Hong of Xuancheng asked Han You about domestic safety; the diviner warned of violent disaster looming over the house.

sentences.zh: 可伐七十束柴，積於庚地，至七月丁酉放火燒之，咎可消也。

translations.literal: You may cut seventy bundles of firewood, pile them on the geng ground, and on dingyou of the seventh month set fire and burn them—the blame can be dispelled."
translations.idiomatic: He told him to stack seventy faggots on geng soil and burn them on dingyou in the seventh month to lift the curse."

sentences.zh: 不爾，其凶難言。

translations.literal: If not, its ill is hard to speak of."
translations.idiomatic: If he refused, Han You said, the harm would be beyond words."

sentences.zh: 」洪即聚柴。

translations.literal: " Hong immediately gathered firewood.
translations.idiomatic: Bian Hong collected the wood.

sentences.zh: 至日，大風，不敢發火。

translations.literal: When the day came, there was a great wind; he did not dare set the fire.
translations.idiomatic: On the appointed day a gale rose and he dared not light the pyre.

sentences.zh: 洪後為廣陽領校，遭母喪歸家，友來投之，時日已暮，出告從者，速裝束，吾當夜去。

translations.literal: Later Hong became colonel of Guangyang, met his mother's mourning and returned home; You came to visit him; the sun was already low when he went out and told his followers, "Pack quickly—I must leave this night."
translations.idiomatic: Later, as Bian Hong mourned his mother at home, Han You visited, then suddenly ordered his escort to saddle up for a midnight flight.

sentences.zh: 從者曰：「今日已暝，數十里草行，何急復去？

translations.literal: The followers said, "The day is already dark; a grass road of several dozen li—why urgently leave again?"
translations.idiomatic: His men protested that night had fallen and the road was long.

sentences.zh: 」友曰：「非汝所知也。

translations.literal: You said, "It is not something you would understand."
translations.idiomatic: Han You said they could not understand what he saw.

sentences.zh: 此間血覆地，寧可復住！

translations.literal: Blood will cover this ground—how can one stay again!"
translations.idiomatic: "Blood will soak this yard," he said; "we cannot stay."

sentences.zh: 」苦留之，不待食而去。

translations.literal: " They bitterly detained him; he did not wait for food but departed.
translations.idiomatic: Hosts pressed him to stay, but he rode off unfed.

sentences.zh: 其夜洪欻發狂，絞殺兩子，並殺婦，又斫父妾二人，皆被創，因出亡走。

translations.literal: That night Hong suddenly went mad, strangled two sons, also killed his wife, and hacked two of his father's concubines, all wounded; then he fled.
translations.idiomatic: That night Bian Hong ran amok, throttled two sons, murdered his wife, wounded two concubines, and bolted.

sentences.zh: 明日，其宗族往收殯亡者，尋索洪，數日，于宅前林中得之，已自經死。

translations.literal: The next day his lineage kin went to gather the dead and search for Hong; after several days they found him in the wood before the house—he had already hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: Next day kinsmen came to bury the dead and found Bian Hong hanged in the grove before his gate.

sentences.zh: 宣城太守殷祐有病，友筮之，曰：「七月晦日，將有大鸜鳥來集廳事上，宜勤伺取，若獲者為善，不獲將成禍。

translations.literal: Yin You, governor of Xuancheng, was ill; You divined and said, "On the last day of the seventh month a great guisu bird will come and alight in the hall—you ought diligently to try to catch it; if you obtain it, that is good; if you do not obtain it, it will become calamity."
translations.idiomatic: Governor Yin You of Xuancheng fell ill; Han You foretold a giant guisu bird on the hall on the seventh month's last day and urged him to capture it or suffer woe.

sentences.zh: 」祐乃謹為其備。

translations.literal: " You thereupon carefully made preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Yin You made every preparation.

sentences.zh: 至日，果有大鸜垂尾九尺，來集廳事上，掩捕得之，祐乃遷石頭督護，後為吳郡太守。

translations.literal: When the day came, there was indeed a great gui with a nine-chi tail that came and alighted in the hall; they covered and caught it; You thereupon was promoted protector at Stone Rampart, and later became governor of Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The bird appeared as foretold; they seized it, and Yin You rose to Stone Rampart protector and later governor of Wu.

sentences.zh: 友卜占神效甚多，而消殃轉禍，無不皆驗。

translations.literal: Han You's divinations were very many and spirit-like, and in dispelling disaster and turning ill fortune there was none that did not prove true.
translations.idiomatic: Han You's divinations were uncannily accurate, and his rites to turn away calamity never failed.

sentences.zh: 于寶問其故，友曰：「筮封用五行相生殺，如案方投藥治病，以冷熱相救。

translations.literal: Yu Bao asked him the reason; You said, "Divination by hexagram uses the five phases' mutual overcoming and killing, like examining a case and applying medicine to cure illness, using cold and hot to rescue each other."
translations.idiomatic: Yu Bao asked how it worked; Han You compared yarrow work to prescribing medicine by pattern—warming or cooling the patient according to need.

sentences.zh: 其差與不差，不可必也。

translations.literal: Whether it improves or not cannot be certain."
translations.idiomatic: Whether the patient mends, he added, can never be guaranteed."

sentences.zh: 」友以舉賢良，元帝渡江，以為廣武將軍，永嘉末卒。

translations.literal: " You was recommended worthy and good; when Emperor Yuan crossed the Yangzi he made him General Who Extends Martiality, and he died at the end of the Yongjia reign.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended as worthy, he became General Who Extends Martiality after the court crossed the river, and died late in Yongjia.

sentences.zh: 淳于智

translations.literal: Chunyu Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Chunyu Zhi

sentences.zh: 淳于智，字叔平，濟北盧人也。

translations.literal: Chunyu Zhi, style name Shuping, was a man of Lu in Jibei.
translations.idiomatic: Chunyu Zhi, courtesy name Shuping, was a native of Lu in Jibei commandery.

sentences.zh: 有思義，能《易》筮，善厭勝之術。

translations.literal: He had thoughtful integrity, could divine by the Changes, and was skilled in apotropaic "victory" arts.
translations.idiomatic: He was principled, divined with the Zhouyi, and mastered apotropaic rites.

sentences.zh: 高平劉柔夜臥，鼠齧其左手中指，以問智。

translations.literal: Liu Rou of Gaoping lay down at night; a rat gnawed his left middle finger; he asked Zhi about it.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Rou of Gaoping awoke to find a rat had chewed his left middle finger and consulted Chunyu Zhi.

sentences.zh: 智曰：「是欲殺君而不能，當為君使其反死。

translations.literal: Zhi said, "It wishes to kill you but cannot; I ought to make it die in your stead."
translations.idiomatic: Chunyu Zhi said the beast meant murder but lacked power—and he would turn the death back on the rat.

sentences.zh: 」乃以硃書手腕橫文後三寸作田字，辟方一寸二分，使露手以臥。

translations.literal: " Thereupon with cinnabar he wrote on the transverse crease three cun behind the wrist the character "field," one cun two fen square, and had him expose the hand and lie down.
translations.idiomatic: He painted a vermilion "field" glyph on the wrist crease and bade Liu sleep with the hand uncovered.

sentences.zh: 明旦，有大鼠伏死手前。

translations.literal: At dawn a great rat was found lying dead before the hand.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn a large rat lay dead before that hand.

sentences.zh: 譙人夏侯藻母病困，詣智卜，忽有一狐當門向之嗥。

translations.literal: Xia Hou Zao of Qiao, his mother being gravely ill, went to Zhi to divine; suddenly a fox stood at the gate howling toward him.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Hou Zao of Qiao sought a reading for his dying mother; a fox stood howling across his gateway.

sentences.zh: 藻怖愕，馳見智。

translations.literal: Zao was frightened and alarmed and galloped to see Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Zao raced to Chunyu Zhi.

sentences.zh: 智曰：「其禍甚急，君速歸，在狐嗥處拊心啼哭，令家人驚怪，大小必出，一人不出，哭勿止，然後其禍可救也。

translations.literal: Zhi said, "The misfortune is very urgent—you should hurry home, clap your heart and weep at the place where the fox howled, make the household startled so that surely all sizes come out; if one person does not come out, do not stop weeping—then the misfortune can be saved."
translations.idiomatic: Chunyu Zhi told him to rush home, wail beneath the fox until every member of the household ran outdoors—if one stayed inside, keep crying—and thus avert the blow.

sentences.zh: 」藻還，如其言，母亦扶病而出。

translations.literal: " Zao returned and acted as he said; his mother also supported her illness and came out.
translations.idiomatic: Zao did so, and even his ailing mother stumbled out.

sentences.zh: 家人既集，堂屋五間拉然而崩。

translations.literal: When the household had assembled, the five bays of the main hall suddenly collapsed with a roar.
