translations.idiomatic: Once they were all outside, the five-bay hall crashed down.

sentences.zh: 護軍張劭母病篤，智筮之，使西出市沐猴，系母臂，令傍人捶拍，恆使作聲，三日放去。

translations.literal: Zhang Shao the protector's mother was gravely ill; Zhi divined, had him go west into the market to buy a bathing monkey, tie it on his mother's arm, order someone beside to beat and pat it so it constantly made noise, and on the third day release it.
translations.idiomatic: Protector Zhang Shao's mother lay dying; Chunyu Zhi sent him west to buy a macaque, bind it on her arm, keep it squealing under patting for three days, then release it.

sentences.zh: 劭從之。

translations.literal: Shao followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shao obeyed.

sentences.zh: 其猴出門即為犬所咋死，母病遂差。

translations.literal: The monkey, once out the gate, was bitten to death by a dog; his mother's illness then recovered.
translations.idiomatic: The monkey was killed by dogs at the door; the mother recovered.

sentences.zh: 上党鮑瑗家多喪病貧苦，或謂之曰：「淳于叔平神人也，君何不試就卜，知禍所在？

translations.literal: Bao Yuan of Shangdang had many deaths and illness in the family and was poor and bitter; someone said to him, "Chunyu Shuping is a spirit man—why not try going to him for divination and learn where the misfortune lies?"
translations.idiomatic: Bao Yuan of Shangdang suffered repeated deaths, sickness, and poverty; neighbors urged him to consult the "spirit man" Chunyu Zhi.

sentences.zh: 」瑗性質直，不信卜筮，曰：「人生有命，豈卜筮所移！

translations.literal: " Yuan was by nature straightforward and did not believe in divination, saying, "Human life has fate—how can divination shift it!"
translations.idiomatic: Bao Yuan, blunt and skeptical, said fate ruled life—not yarrow.

sentences.zh: 」會智來，應詹謂曰：「此君寒士，每多屯虞，君有通靈之思，可為一卦。

translations.literal: " When Zhi came, Ying Zhan said to him, "This gentleman is a poor scholar who often meets obstruction; you have a penetrating mind—cast one hexagram for him."
translations.idiomatic: When Chunyu Zhi arrived, Ying Zhan begged a reading for the hard-pressed scholar.

sentences.zh: 」智乃為卦，卦成，謂瑗曰：「君安宅失宜，故令君困。

translations.literal: " Zhi thereupon cast the hexagram; when the hexagram was complete he said to Yuan, "Your dwelling is out of alignment with the site, and therefore makes you destitute."
translations.idiomatic: Chunyu Zhi cast the lines and said Bao Yuan's house sat on ill-oriented ground that beggared him.

sentences.zh: 君舍東北有大桑樹，君徑至市，入門數十步，當有一人持荊馬鞭者，便就買以懸此樹，三年當暴得財。

translations.literal: " There is a great mulberry northeast of your house; go straight to the market, enter the gate several dozen paces, and there ought to be a man holding a thorn horsewhip—buy it from him and hang it on this tree, and in three years you will suddenly obtain wealth."
translations.idiomatic: He told him to buy a thorn switch in the market and hang it on a great mulberry northeast of the house to draw sudden fortune within three years.

sentences.zh: 」瑗承言詣市，果得馬鞭，懸之三年，浚井，得錢數十萬，銅鐵器復二十餘萬，於是致贍，疾者亦愈。

translations.literal: " Yuan followed the words and went to the market, indeed obtained a horsewhip, hung it three years, dredged the well, obtained several hundred thousand cash, and more than two hundred thousand in bronze and iron vessels; thereupon he became well provided, and the sick also recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Yuan obeyed, found the whip, hung it, and three years later dredged tens of thousands of cash and bronze from his well—ending want and sickness in the household.

sentences.zh: 其消災轉禍，不可勝紀，而卜筮所占，千百皆中。

translations.literal: His dispelling disaster and turning ill fortune cannot be fully recorded, yet divinations were in the hundreds and thousands and all hit.
translations.idiomatic: His turnings of ill luck are beyond counting, and every yarrow reading struck true.

sentences.zh: 應詹少亦多病，智乃為符使詹佩之，誦其文，既而皆驗，莫能學也。

translations.literal: Ying Zhan in youth also often fell ill; Zhi then made talismans for Zhan to wear and recite their text—afterward all were verified, yet none could learn his method.
translations.idiomatic: Ying Zhan had been sickly in youth until Chunyu Zhi gave him talismans to wear and chant—cures that worked but could not be taught.

sentences.zh: 性深沈，常自言短命，曰：「辛亥歲天下有事，當有巫醫挾道術者死。

translations.literal: His nature was deep and still; he often said he would die young: "In the xinhai year there will be affairs under Heaven; there will then die a shaman or doctor who wields the Dao arts."
translations.idiomatic: Brooding and self-aware, he predicted a xinhai-year purge that would kill occult healers.

sentences.zh: 吾守《易》義以行之，猶當不應此乎！

translations.literal: I uphold the meaning of the Changes to practice them—should I still not meet this!"
translations.idiomatic: "I live by the Changes," he said, "yet even I cannot escape that fate!"

sentences.zh: 」太康末，為司馬督，有寵于楊駿，故見殺。

translations.literal: " At the end of the Taikang reign he was marshal-in-attendant and had favor with Yang Jun, and therefore was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Taikang he served as marshal under Yang Jun's patronage and was executed in the coup.

sentences.zh: 步熊

translations.literal: Bu Xiong.
translations.idiomatic: Bu Xiong

sentences.zh: 步熊，字叔羆，陽平發幹人也。

translations.literal: Bu Xiong, style name Shupi, was a man of Fagan in Yangping.
translations.idiomatic: Bu Xiong, courtesy name Shupi, came from Fagan in Yangping commandery.

sentences.zh: 少好卜筮數術，門徒甚盛。

translations.literal: In youth he loved divination and numerological arts; his disciples were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he loved yarrow and number lore and gathered many pupils.

sentences.zh: 熊學舍側有一人燒死，吏持熊諸生，謂為失火。

translations.literal: Beside Xiong's study hall a man burned to death; the clerk seized Xiong's students, deeming it a fire they had let spread.
translations.idiomatic: When a man burned to death beside his school, the magistrate seized Bu Xiong's disciples as arsonists.

sentences.zh: 熊曰：「已為卿卜得其人矣。

translations.literal: Xiong said, "I have already divined for you and obtained the man."
translations.idiomatic: Bu Xiong said he had already identified the culprit by divination.

sentences.zh: 使從道南行，當有一人來問得火主未者，便縛之。

translations.literal: Have him go south on the road; there ought to be a man who comes asking whether the master of the fire has been found—then bind him."
translations.idiomatic: He told the clerk to walk south until someone asked about the "fire's master," then seize him.

sentences.zh: 」吏如熊言，果是耕人，自言草惡難耕，故燒之，忽風起延燒遠近，實不知草中有人。

translations.literal: " The clerk acted as Xiong said; it was indeed a ploughman who said of himself that the grass was bad and hard to plough, therefore he burned it; suddenly wind rose and the fire spread far and near; in truth he did not know there was a man in the grass.
translations.idiomatic: The man was a farmer who had torched stubble for clearing; a gust spread the blaze and he never knew someone lay hidden in the weeds.

sentences.zh: 又鄰人兒遠行，或告已死，其父母號哭制服，熊為之卜，克日當還，如期果至。

translations.literal: Moreover a neighbor's son went far away; someone reported he had died; his parents wailed and donned mourning; Xiong divined for them that on the appointed day he ought to return, and at the term he indeed arrived.
translations.idiomatic: When neighbors thought a boy dead abroad, Bu Xiong set a return date—and the youth walked home on that very day.

sentences.zh: 趙王倫聞其名，召之。

translations.literal: Prince Zhao Lun heard his name and summoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Sima Lun of Zhao summoned him to court.

sentences.zh: 熊謂諸生曰：「倫死不久，不足應也。

translations.literal: Xiong said to the students, "Lun will not long survive—it is not worth answering."
translations.idiomatic: Bu Xiong told his pupils Sima Lun was doomed and the summons was beneath their notice.

sentences.zh: 」倫怒，遣兵圍之數重。

translations.literal: " Lun raged and sent troops to surround them in many layers.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Lun ringed the school with soldiers.

sentences.zh: 熊乃使諸生著其裘南走，倫兵悉赴捉之，熊密從北出，得脫。

translations.literal: Xiong then had the students put on his furs and run south; Lun's soldiers all rushed to seize them; Xiong secretly went out from the north and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: He dressed disciples in his own robes as decoys while he slipped out the north side.

sentences.zh: 後為成都王穎所辟，穎使熊射覆，物無所失。

translations.literal: Later he was recruited by Prince Chengdu Ying; Ying had Xiong shoot the covered vessel—nothing was ever missed.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Ying of Chengdu employed him for "cover-shoot" divination, and he never failed to name the hidden object.

sentences.zh: 後穎奔關中，平昌公模鎮鄴，以熊穎黨，誅之。

translations.literal: Later Ying fled into the passes; the Duke of Pingchang, Mo, garrisoned Ye; because Xiong was Ying's partisan, he executed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Ying fled to Guanzhong and Sima Mo held Ye, Mo executed Bu Xiong as a partisan of the prince.

sentences.zh: 杜不愆

translations.literal: Du Buqian.
translations.idiomatic: Du Buqian

sentences.zh: 杜不愆，廬江人也。

translations.literal: Du Buqian was a man of Lujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Du Buqian came from Lujiang commandery.

sentences.zh: 少就外祖郭璞學《易》卜。

translations.literal: In youth he studied the Changes and divination with his maternal grandfather Guo Pu.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he learned the Zhouyi and yarrow lore under his grandfather Guo Pu.

sentences.zh: 屢有驗。

translations.literal: Repeatedly there were verifications.
translations.idiomatic: His readings proved true again and again.

sentences.zh: 高平郗超年二十餘，得重疾，試令筮之。

translations.literal: Xi Chao of Gaoping, over twenty years of age, contracted a grave illness; they tried having him cast the yarrow.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Chao of Gaoping, barely twenty, fell dangerously ill; his household asked Du Buqian to cast.

sentences.zh: 不愆曰：「案卦言之，卿所苦尋除。

translations.literal: Buqian said, "According to the hexagram what you suffer will soon be removed.
translations.idiomatic: Du Buqian said the lines showed the ailment lifting soon.

sentences.zh: 然宜於東北三十里上宮姓家索其所養雄雉，籠盛置東簷下，卻後九日丙午日午時，必當有雌雉飛來與交，既而雙去。

translations.literal: Yet you ought to go to a family surnamed Shang on the high ground thirty li northeast and seek the cockerel they raise, put it in a cage and place it under the east eaves; afterward on the ninth day, bingwu day, at the wu double-hour, there ought surely to be a hen that flies in and mates with it; when both have gone away—
translations.idiomatic: He prescribed a ritual: fetch a rooster from a Shang family on a rise thirty li northeast, cage it under the east eaves, and on the ninth day at noon a hen would arrive to mate—

sentences.zh: 若如此，不出二十日病都除，又是休應，年將八十，位極人臣。

translations.literal: if so, within twenty days the illness will entirely be gone; moreover it is a sign of rest; the years will approach eighty, and rank will reach the utmost of human ministers.
translations.idiomatic: if that happened, the sickness would vanish within twenty days, he would live toward eighty, and rise to the highest ministerial rank.

sentences.zh: 若但雌逝雄留者，病一周方差，年半八十，名位亦失。

translations.literal: If only the hen departs and the cock remains, the illness will improve after one week, the years half of eighty, and name and rank likewise lost."
translations.idiomatic: If the hen left while the cock stayed, he would mend after a week but lose half his years and his career prospects.

sentences.zh: 」超時正羸篤，慮命在旦夕，笑而答曰：「若保八十之半，便有餘矣。

translations.literal: " Chao at the time was just emaciated and gravely ill, worried his life was at dawn and dusk; smiling he answered, "If it secures half of eighty, that is already more than enough.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Chao, wasted and near death, laughed that half of eighty would be plenty.

sentences.zh: 一周病差，何足為淹！

translations.literal: One week's illness mended—what is worth calling a delay!"
translations.idiomatic: A week's convalescence seemed a trifle.

sentences.zh: 」然未之信。

translations.literal: " Yet he did not believe it.
translations.idiomatic: Still he doubted the oracle.

sentences.zh: 或勸依其言，索雉果得。

translations.literal: Someone urged him to follow the words; he sought the cocks and indeed obtained them.
translations.idiomatic: Friends pressed him to obey; he found the birds as directed.

sentences.zh: 至丙午日，超臥南軒之下觀之，至日晏，果有雌雉飛入籠，與雄雉交而去，雄雉不動。

translations.literal: On the bingwu day Chao lay under the south gallery watching; by the time the sun was low, indeed a hen flew into the cage, mated with the cock, and departed; the cock did not move.
translations.idiomatic: At noon on bingwu he watched from the south loggia until a hen flew in, coupled, and flew off while the rooster stayed.

sentences.zh: 超歎曰：「雖管郭之奇，何以尚此！

translations.literal: Chao sighed, "Though Guan and Guo were marvelous, how could they surpass this!"
translations.idiomatic: Xi Chao marveled that even Guan Lu and Guo Pu could not match such precision.

sentences.zh: 」超病彌年乃起，至四十，卒于中書郎。

translations.literal: " Chao's illness lasted a full year before he rose; at forty he died as Palace Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: His illness lingered a year before he rose; he died at forty as a secretary at the palace bureau.

sentences.zh: 不愆後占筮轉疏，無復此類。

translations.literal: Afterward Buqian's divinations grew cruder and there were no more cases of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: Later Du Buqian's casts grew rougher, and nothing so striking happened again.

sentences.zh: 後為桓嗣建威參軍。

translations.literal: Later he became adjutant to Huan Si's General Who Establishes Might.
translations.idiomatic: He ended as staff officer to Huan Si, general who establishes might.

sentences.zh: 嚴卿

translations.literal: Yan Qing.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Qing

sentences.zh: 嚴卿，會稽人也。

translations.literal: Yan Qing was a man of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Qing was a native of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 善卜筮。

translations.literal: He was skilled at divination by yarrow.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at yarrow divination.

sentences.zh: 鄉人魏序欲暫東行，荒年多抄盜，令卿筮之。

translations.literal: Fellow townsman Wei Xu wished to go east for a time; in famine years there was much banditry; he ordered Qing to divine it.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xu of his village planned an eastern journey in a year of famine and robbers, and asked Yan Qing to cast.

sentences.zh: 卿筮曰：「君慎不可東行，必遭暴害之氣，而非劫也。

translations.literal: Qing divined and said, "You must be careful not to go east—you will meet the qi of sudden violence, yet it will not be robbery."
translations.idiomatic: Yan Qing warned him not to travel east: violent qi awaited him, though not common bandits.

sentences.zh: 」序不之信。

translations.literal: " Xu did not believe him.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xu ignored the warning.

sentences.zh: 卿曰：「既必不停，宜以禳之，可索西郭外獨母家白雄狗系著船前。

translations.literal: Qing said, "Since you will surely not stop, you ought to exorcise it: seek west of the outer wall the lone widow's house for a white cockerel and tie it at the prow of the boat."
translations.idiomatic: Yan Qing said if he insisted, he must tie a white rooster from a widow west of the wall to the bow as a ward.

sentences.zh: 」求索止得駁狗，無白者。

translations.literal: " He searched and obtained only a piebald dog—there was no white one.
translations.idiomatic: They could only find a spotted dog, no pure white fowl.

sentences.zh: 卿曰：「駁者亦足，然猶恨其色不純，當餘小毒，正及六畜輩耳，無所復憂。

translations.literal: Qing said, "Piebald is also enough, yet I still regret that its color is not pure—there will remain a small poison, reaching only the six domestic animals; there is nothing further to worry about."
translations.idiomatic: Yan Qing said piebald would serve but hinted at leftover venom limited to livestock.

sentences.zh: 」序行半路，狗忽然作聲甚急，有如人打之者。

translations.literal: " When Xu was halfway on the road, the dog suddenly made a very urgent noise as if someone were beating it.
translations.idiomatic: Mid-voyage the dog yelped as if flogged.

sentences.zh: 比視，已死，吐黑血鬥餘。

translations.literal: When they looked, it was already dead, vomiting more than a dou of black blood.
translations.idiomatic: They found it dead, having spewed more than a dou of black blood.

sentences.zh: 其夕，序墅上白鵝數頭無故自死，而序家無恙。

translations.literal: That evening several white geese on Xu's manor died for no reason, yet Xu's household had no harm.
translations.idiomatic: That night his white geese dropped dead, yet every human under his roof was spared.

sentences.zh: 隗炤

translations.literal: Wei Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhao

sentences.zh: 隗炤，汝陰人也。

translations.literal: Wei Zhao was a man of Ruyin.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhao came from Ruyin.

sentences.zh: 善於《易》。

translations.literal: He was skilled in the Changes.
translations.idiomatic: He was a master of the Zhouyi.

sentences.zh: 臨終，書版授其妻曰：「吾亡後當大荒窮，雖爾慎莫賣宅也。

translations.literal: At the end of life he wrote on a board and handed it to his wife, saying, "After my death there will be great famine and poverty; though it be so, be careful not to sell the house."
translations.idiomatic: Dying, he gave his wife a wooden slip: after his death famine would strike, yet she must never sell the house.

sentences.zh: 卻後五年春，當有詔使來頓此亭，姓龔，此人負吾金，即以此版往責之，勿違言也。

translations.literal: After five years, in spring, there will be an imperial messenger who stops at this post, surnamed Gong—this man owes me gold; take this board to him to collect; do not disobey my words."
translations.idiomatic: In five years a courier surnamed Gong would lodge at their post owing him gold—she must present the slip to collect.

sentences.zh: 」炤亡後，其家大困乏，欲賣宅，憶夫言輒止。

translations.literal: " After Zhao died, his household was greatly destitute and wished to sell the house; remembering her husband's words they always stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When want tempted her to sell, she remembered his charge and held the property.

sentences.zh: 期日，有龔使者止亭中，妻遂齎版往責之。

translations.literal: On the appointed day there was indeed an envoy Gong who halted in the post; the wife then carried the board to demand payment.
translations.idiomatic: On the day foretold a Mr. Gong arrived; she brought him the tally for the debt.

sentences.zh: 使者執版惘然，不知所以。

translations.literal: The envoy held the board, dazed, not knowing why.
translations.idiomatic: The messenger stared at the slip, baffled.

sentences.zh: 妻曰：「夫臨亡，手書版見命如此，不敢妄也。

translations.literal: The wife said, "At death my husband hand-wrote the board and charged me thus—I dare not be rash."
translations.idiomatic: She explained her husband's dying instructions.

sentences.zh: 」使者沈吟良久而悟，謂曰：「賢夫何善？

translations.literal: " The messenger pondered long and understood; he said to her, "In what was your worthy husband skilled?"
translations.idiomatic: After long thought he asked what arts Wei Zhao had practiced.

sentences.zh: 」妻曰：「夫善於《易》，而未會為人卜也。

translations.literal: " The wife said, "He was skilled in the Changes, yet never divined for others."
translations.idiomatic: She said he knew the Zhouyi but never read for clients.

sentences.zh: 」使者曰：「噫，可知矣！

translations.literal: " The envoy said, "Ah, I can know!"
translations.idiomatic: The envoy exclaimed that he now understood.

sentences.zh: 」乃命取蓍筮之，卦成，撫掌而歎曰：「妙哉隗生！

translations.literal: " He ordered yarrow brought and divined; when the hexagram was complete, he clapped his palm and sighed, "Wonderful, Master Wei!"
translations.idiomatic: He cast the yarrow himself, then cried out in admiration for Wei Zhao's craft.

sentences.zh: 含明隱跡，可謂鏡窮達而洞吉凶者也。

translations.literal: Holding brightness yet hiding his traces—he may be called one who mirrors fortune and privation and pierces good and ill."
translations.idiomatic: He praised Wei for hiding brilliance while reading rise and fall with perfect clarity.

sentences.zh: 」於是告炤妻曰：「吾不相負金也，賢夫自有金耳，知亡後當暫窮，故藏金以待太平，所以不告兒婦者，恐金盡而困無已也。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he told Zhao's wife, "I do not owe your worthy husband gold; your worthy husband had gold himself—knowing that after death there would be temporary poverty, he hid gold to await peace; the reason he did not tell sons and wives was fear that when the gold was exhausted hardship would have no end."
translations.idiomatic: He explained Wei had buried five hundred jin of gold for the lean years, telling no kin lest they spend it and starve.

sentences.zh: 知吾善《易》，故書版以寄意耳。

translations.literal: Knowing I am skilled in the Changes, therefore he wrote the board to lodge his meaning."
translations.idiomatic: Wei knew the envoy understood the Changes, so he used the slip as cipher.

sentences.zh: 金有五百斤，盛以青甕，覆以銅柈，埋在堂屋東頭，去壁一丈，入地九尺。

translations.literal: The gold is five hundred jin, stored in green jars, covered with bronze platters, buried east of the main hall's head, one zhang from the wall, nine chi into the earth."
translations.idiomatic: He directed her to green jars under bronze lids, one zhang from the east wall and nine chi down.

sentences.zh: 」妻還掘之，皆如卜焉。

translations.literal: " The wife returned and dug; all was as divined.
translations.idiomatic: She dug and found every coin exactly as foretold.

sentences.zh: 卜珝

translations.literal: Bu Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Bu Xu

sentences.zh: 卜珝，字子玉，匈奴後部人也。

translations.literal: Bu Xu, style name Ziyu, was a man of the rear section of the Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: Bu Xu, courtesy name Ziyu, belonged to the Xiongnu rear division.

sentences.zh: 少好讀《易》，郭璞見而歎曰：「吾所弗如也，柰何不免兵厄！

translations.literal: In youth he loved reading the Changes; Guo Pu saw him and sighed, "What I cannot match—yet how can you avoid the misfortune of arms!"
translations.idiomatic: While Bu Xu was still a youth poring over the Zhouyi, Guo Pu met him and marveled, "I am not his equal—yet how will he escape dying by the sword?"

sentences.zh: 」珝曰：「然。

translations.literal: " Xu said, "So it is.
translations.idiomatic: Bu Xu calmly replied, "It is as you say."

sentences.zh: 吾大厄在四十一，位為卿將，當受禍耳。

translations.literal: My great misfortune is at forty-one; my rank will be minister-general—I shall then meet disaster.
translations.idiomatic: He foretold his own doom at forty-one as a minister-general.

sentences.zh: 不爾者，亦為猛獸所害。

translations.literal: If not that, I will likewise be harmed by a fierce beast.
translations.idiomatic: If not that, a savage beast would kill him.

sentences.zh: 吾亦未見子之令終也。

translations.literal: I likewise have not seen your propitious end."
translations.idiomatic: He added that he did not see a peaceful end for Guo Pu either.

sentences.zh: 」璞曰：「吾禍在江南，甚營之，未見免兆。

translations.literal: " Pu said, "My misfortune lies south of the Yangzi—I greatly worry about it and have not yet seen an omen of escape.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Pu said his peril lay in the south, with no sign of escape.

sentences.zh: 雖然，在南猶可延期，住此不過時月。

translations.literal: Even so, in the south the term may still be extended; staying here will not exceed months."
translations.idiomatic: Bu Xu replied that the south might delay fate, but staying north bought only a few months.

sentences.zh: 」珝曰：「子勿為公吏，可以免諸。

translations.literal: " Xu said, "Do not become a public clerk and you can avoid the various ills."
translations.idiomatic: He urged Guo Pu never to take a clerk's post if he wished to live.

sentences.zh: 」璞曰：「吾不能免公吏，猶子之不能免卿將也。

translations.literal: " Pu said, "I cannot avoid being a public clerk—just as you cannot avoid being minister-general."
translations.idiomatic: Guo Pu answered that neither could escape the roles fate assigned.

sentences.zh: 」珝曰：「吾此雖當有帝王子，終不復奉二京矣。

translations.literal: " Xu said, "Though here there ought to be an imperial son, in the end we will not again serve the two capitals.
translations.idiomatic: Bu Xu predicted an imperial scion would rise yet the two capitals would never be restored under them.

sentences.zh: 琅邪可奉，卿謹奉之，主晉祀者必此人也。

translations.literal: Langye may be served—serve him carefully; the one who will uphold the Jin sacrifices must be this man."
translations.idiomatic: He told Guo to cleave to the prince of Langye—the man who would carry the Jin rites.

sentences.zh: 」珝遂隱于龍門山。

translations.literal: " Xu thereupon hid on Mount Longmen.
translations.idiomatic: Bu Xu then withdrew to Mount Longmen.

sentences.zh: 劉元海僭號，徵為大司農、侍中，固以疾辭。

translations.literal: When Liu Yuanhai arrogated the title, he summoned him as Grand Minister of Agriculture and palace attendant; he firmly pleaded illness and declined.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuan summoned him as grand minister of agriculture; he feigned illness and refused.

sentences.zh: 元海曰：「人各有心，卜珝不欲在吾朝，何異高祖四公哉！

translations.literal: Yuanhai said, "Each man has his mind—Bu Xu not wishing to be in my court, how does he differ from the Four Lords of the High Ancestor!"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuan compared his refusal to the recluses Han Gaozu could not compel.

sentences.zh: 可遂其高志。

translations.literal: Let his lofty will be followed."
translations.idiomatic: He let Bu Xu keep his hermit pride.

sentences.zh: 」後復徵為光祿大夫，珝謂使者曰：「非吾死所也。

translations.literal: " Later he was again summoned as Supernumerary Palace Grandee; Xu said to the messenger, "That is not the place where I shall die."
translations.idiomatic: When summoned as supernumerary grandee, he told the envoy that office was not where he would perish.

sentences.zh: 」及劉聰嗣偽位，徵為太常。

translations.literal: " When Liu Cong succeeded to the false throne, he summoned him as Grand Master of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liu Cong he was called to be grand master of ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 時劉琨據并州，聰問何時可平，珝答曰：「并州陛下之分，今茲克之必矣。

translations.literal: At that time Liu Kun held Bing Province; Cong asked when it could be pacified; Xu answered, "Bing Province is Your Majesty's allotted share—this year taking it is certain."
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Cong asked when Liu Kun's Bingzhou would fall, Bu Xu said the stars marked it for the barbarian house that very year.

sentences.zh: 」聰戲曰：「朕欲勞先生一行可乎？

translations.literal: " Cong jested, "I would trouble the master to go on one journey—may it be done?"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong teasingly asked him to lead the campaign himself.

sentences.zh: 」珝曰：「臣所以來不及裝者，正為是行也。

translations.literal: " Xu said, "The reason I came without finishing my gear was precisely for this journey."
translations.idiomatic: Bu Xu replied he had hurried north unprepared precisely to accept that march.

sentences.zh: 」聰大悅，署珝使持節、平北將軍。

translations.literal: " Cong was greatly pleased and appointed Xu commissioner on campaign with credentials, General Who Pacifies the North.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted, Liu Cong named him credential-bearing commissioner and general who pacifies the north.

sentences.zh: 將行，謂其妹曰：「此行也，死自吾分，後慎勿紛紜。

translations.literal: About to depart, he told his younger sister, "This journey—death is my lot; afterward be careful not to fuss."
translations.idiomatic: Before leaving he told his sister the campaign meant his death and bade her not to mourn loudly.

sentences.zh: 」及攻晉陽，為琨所敗，珝卒先奔，為其元帥所殺。

translations.literal: When they attacked Jinyang he was defeated by Kun; Xu was the first to flee in panic and was killed by his commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: At the assault on Jinyang he broke before Liu Kun and was cut down by his own commander for cowardice.

sentences.zh: 鮑靚

translations.literal: Bao Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Jing

sentences.zh: 鮑靚，字太玄，東海人也。

translations.literal: Bao Jing, style name Taixuan, was a man of Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Jing, courtesy name Taixuan, came from Donghai commandery.

sentences.zh: 年五歲，語父母云：「本是曲陽李家兒，九歲墜井死。

translations.literal: At age five he told his parents, "Originally I was a Li-family child of Quyang; at nine I fell into a well and died."
translations.idiomatic: At five he told his parents he had been a Li boy in Quyang who drowned in a well at nine.

sentences.zh: 」其父母尋訪得李氏，推問皆符驗。

translations.literal: " His parents searched and found the Li family; pushing the inquiry, everything matched verification.
translations.idiomatic: They traced the Li household and every detail matched his tale.

sentences.zh: 靚學兼內外，明天文河洛書，稍遷南陽中部都尉，為南海太守。

translations.literal: Jing's learning embraced inner and outer; he understood astronomy and the River Chart and Luo Writings; he gradually rose to metropolitan commandant of the middle division of Nanyang and became governor of Nanhai.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered Confucian and occult lore, astrology, and Hetu-Luoshu numerology, rising to Nanyang commandant and Nanhai governor.

sentences.zh: 嘗行部入海，遇風，饑甚，取白石煮食之以自濟。

translations.literal: Once on inspection he entered the sea, met wind, and was extremely hungry; he took white stones, boiled and ate them to save himself.
translations.idiomatic: Caught in a gale at sea on tour, he boiled white flints for food and survived.

sentences.zh: 王機時為廣州刺史，入廁，忽見二人著烏衣，與機相捍，良久擒之，得二物似烏鴨。

translations.literal: Wang Ji at the time was governor of Guangzhou; entering the privy he suddenly saw two men in black clothes grappling with Ji; after a long while he seized them and obtained two things like crows.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Ji was governor of Guangzhou, he seized two crow-shaped imps that attacked him in the latrine.

sentences.zh: 靚曰：「此物不祥。

translations.literal: Jing said, "These things are inauspicious."
translations.idiomatic: Bao Jing called them ill omens.

sentences.zh: 」機焚之，徑飛上天，機尋誅死。

translations.literal: " Ji burned them; they flew straight to heaven; Ji soon was executed and died.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji burned them; they shot skyward; soon afterward he was executed.

sentences.zh: 靚嘗見仙人陰君，授道訣，百餘歲卒。

translations.literal: Jing once met the transcendent Lord Yin, who handed him the oral formulas of the Dao; he died at over a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: He met the immortal Yin Jun, received Dao formulas, and died past the century mark.

sentences.zh: 吳猛

translations.literal: Wu Meng.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Meng

sentences.zh: 吳猛，豫章人也。

translations.literal: Wu Meng was a man of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Meng was a native of Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 少有孝行，夏日常手不驅蚊，懼其去己而噬親也。

translations.literal: In youth he had filial conduct; in summer he commonly did not drive off mosquitoes with his hand, fearing they would leave him and bite his kin.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he let mosquitoes feed on his own flesh so they would not trouble his parents.

sentences.zh: 年四十，邑人丁義始授其神方。

translations.literal: At forty a townsman, Ding Yi, first handed him the divine formula.
translations.idiomatic: At forty Ding Yi of his town taught him an esoteric formula.

sentences.zh: 因還豫章，江波甚急，猛不假舟楫，以白羽扇畫水而渡，觀者異之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he returned to Yuzhang; the river waves were very swift; Meng used no boat or oar but with a white feather fan drew on the water and crossed; watchers marveled.
translations.idiomatic: Returning to Yuzhang he crossed a raging stream by fanning the water with a white feather fan, astonishing onlookers.

sentences.zh: 庾亮為江州刺史，嘗遇疾，聞猛神異，乃迎之，問己疾何如。

translations.literal: Yu Liang was governor of Jiang Province; once he fell ill; hearing Meng was spirit-like, he welcomed him and asked how his illness was.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Liang, as Jiangzhou governor, summoned him when ill to ask his fate.

sentences.zh: 猛辭以算盡，請具棺服。

translations.literal: Meng declined, saying the reckoning was exhausted, and asked to prepare a coffin and shroud.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Meng answered that Yu Liang's span was spent and asked him to ready coffin clothes.

sentences.zh: 旬日而死，形狀如生。

translations.literal: Within ten days he died; his form and appearance were as if alive.
translations.idiomatic: He died within ten days, yet his corpse looked as though he still lived.

sentences.zh: 未及大斂，遂失其屍。

translations.literal: Before they reached the great laying-in, thereupon his corpse was lost.
translations.idiomatic: Before the encoffining rites could begin, the body had vanished.

sentences.zh: 識者以為亮不祥之徵。

translations.literal: Those who understood deemed it an ill-omened sign for Yu Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Knowledgable onlookers read it as a dark portent for Yu Liang.

sentences.zh: 亮疾果不起。

translations.literal: Yu Liang's illness indeed did not recover—he could not rise.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Liang never rose from his sickbed.

sentences.zh: 幸靈

translations.literal: Xing Ling.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Ling

sentences.zh: 幸靈者，豫章建昌人也。

translations.literal: Xing Ling was a man of Jianchang in Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Ling came from Jianchang county in Yuzhang commandery.

sentences.zh: 性少言，與小人群居，見侵辱而無慍色，邑裏號之癡，雖其父母兄弟亦以為癡也。

translations.literal: By nature he spoke little; he dwelled among petty men; seeing insult and humiliation he had no angry color; the town called him foolish; though his parents and brothers likewise deemed him foolish.
translations.idiomatic: Taciturn, he lived among common folk, endured abuse without a scowl, and the whole hamlet mocked him as simple—even his kin thought him dull-witted.

sentences.zh: 嘗使守稻，群牛食之，靈見而不驅，待牛去乃往理其殘亂者。

translations.literal: Once they had him guard the rice; a herd of cattle ate it; Ling saw and did not drive them; waiting until the cattle departed he then went to set in order what was ruined and in disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Set to watch the paddies, he let the oxen finish grazing before he straightened the trampled stalks.

sentences.zh: 其父母見而怒之，靈曰：「夫萬物生天地之間，各欲得食。

translations.literal: His parents seeing it were angry at him; Ling said, "The myriad things born between heaven and earth each wish to obtain food.
translations.idiomatic: His parents scolded him; he answered that every creature under heaven hungered alike.

sentences.zh: 牛方食，柰何驅之！

translations.literal: The oxen are just feeding—how shall we drive them off!"
translations.idiomatic: "The herd is feeding—why chase them away?"

sentences.zh: 」其父愈怒曰：「即如汝言，復用理壞者何為？

translations.literal: " His father grew angrier and said, "If it is as you say, what use again is setting in order what is ruined?"
translations.idiomatic: His father snapped that if that were true, tidying ruined grain was pointless.

sentences.zh: 」靈曰：「此稻又欲得終其性，牛自犯之，靈可以不收乎！」

translations.literal: " Ling said, "This rice moreover wishes to complete its nature; the oxen on their own offended it—can Ling fail to gather it in!"
translations.idiomatic: Ling retorted that the grain still deserved its full growth, the cattle had wronged it, and he was bound to salvage what remained.

sentences.zh: 時順陽樊長賓為建昌令，發百姓作官船於建城山中，吏令人各作箸一雙。

translations.literal: At that time Fan Changbin of Shunyang was magistrate of Jianchang; he mobilized the common people to build official boats in the Jiancheng mountains; clerks ordered each man to make one pair of chopsticks.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Changbin of Shunyang, then magistrate of Jianchang, conscripted villagers to build government vessels in the Jiancheng hills and required every laborer to turn in one pair of chopsticks.

sentences.zh: 靈作而未輸，或竊之焉。

translations.literal: Ling made them but had not yet delivered them; someone stole them.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Ling finished his pair, yet before he could hand them in someone stole them.

sentences.zh: 俄而竊者心痛欲死，靈謂之曰：「爾得無竊我箸乎？

translations.literal: Before long the thief's heart ached as if he would die; Ling said to him, "Could it be you stole my chopsticks?"
translations.idiomatic: The thief doubled over with chest pain until Ling asked whether he had lifted the chopsticks.

sentences.zh: 」竊者不應。

translations.literal: " The thief did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: The culprit kept silent.

sentences.zh: 有頃，愈急，靈曰：「若爾不以情告我者，今真死矣。

translations.literal: After a while it grew more urgent; Ling said, "If thus you do not tell me the truth in earnest, now you will truly die."
translations.idiomatic: As the agony mounted, Ling warned that only a frank confession would spare him.

sentences.zh: 」竊者急遽，乃首出之。

translations.literal: " The thief, pressed and hurried, then confessed and produced them.
translations.idiomatic: Panicked, the thief owned up and produced them.

sentences.zh: 靈於是飲之以水，病即立愈。

translations.literal: Ling thereupon gave him to drink of water; the ailment at once was cured on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Ling gave him water and the pain vanished instantly.

sentences.zh: 行人由此敬畏之。

translations.literal: Wayfarers from this feared and revered him.
translations.idiomatic: Travelers thereafter stood in awe of him.

sentences.zh: 船成，當下，吏以二百人引一艘，不能動，方請益人。

translations.literal: When the boats were finished and were to go downstream, clerks used two hundred men to pull one vessel and could not move it; they were about to request more men.
translations.idiomatic: On launch day two hundred haulers could not budge a single hull, so the bailiffs begged for more hands.

sentences.zh: 靈曰：「此以過足，但部分未至耳。

translations.literal: Ling said, "In this the manpower already exceeds what is needed; only the allotments have not yet arrived."
translations.idiomatic: Ling said the crews were already ample but badly deployed.

sentences.zh: 靈請自牽之。

translations.literal: Ling asked to lead the hauling himself.
translations.idiomatic: He volunteered to marshal the tow-ropes himself.

sentences.zh: 」乃手執箸，惟用百人，而船去如流。

translations.literal: " Thereupon with his hand he grasped the chopsticks; using only a hundred men, the boat went away like a current.
translations.idiomatic: Chopsticks in hand, he redeployed a hundred men and the barge glided downstream like swift water.

sentences.zh: 眾大驚怪，咸稱其神，於是知名。

translations.literal: The crowd greatly marveled; all called him divine; from this he became known.
translations.idiomatic: The throng gasped, hailed him a wonder-worker, and his fame spread.

sentences.zh: 有龔仲儒女病積年，氣息財屬，靈使以水含之，已而強起，應時大愈。

translations.literal: There was the daughter of Gong Zhongru ill many years; her breath only just hung on; Ling had her hold water in the mouth; afterward she rose with strength and at the moment was greatly cured.
translations.idiomatic: Gong Zhongru's daughter had lain at death's door for years until Ling had her rinse with water; she sat up vigorously and recovered at once.

sentences.zh: 又呂猗母皇氏得痿痹病，十有餘年，靈療之，去皇氏數尺而坐，冥目寂然，有頃，顧謂猗曰：「扶夫人令起。

translations.literal: Also Lü Yi's mother Lady Huang contracted paralysis-numbness illness more than ten years; Ling treated her; removing several chi from Lady Huang he sat; closing his eyes in silent stillness; after a moment, turning his gaze he said to Yi, "Support the lady and order her to rise."
translations.idiomatic: He also healed Lü Yi's mother, crippled by palsy for a decade, by sitting yards away in trance until he told Lü Yi to help her stand.

sentences.zh: 」猗曰：「老人得病累年，奈何可倉卒起邪？

translations.literal: " Yi said, "The old woman has been ill cumulative years—how can one hastily make her rise?"
translations.idiomatic: Lü Yi protested that an aged invalid could not be roused in haste.

sentences.zh: 」靈曰：「但試扶起。

translations.literal: " Ling said, "Only try supporting her to rise."
translations.idiomatic: Ling bade him simply try.

sentences.zh: 」於是兩人夾扶以立。

translations.literal: " Thereupon two men flanked and supported her to stand.
translations.idiomatic: Two servants braced her upright.

sentences.zh: 少選，靈又令去扶，即能自行，由此遂愈。

translations.literal: In a short while Ling again ordered them to remove the support; she was then able to walk by herself; from this she was cured.
translations.idiomatic: Moments later he had them let go, and she walked unaided thereafter.

sentences.zh: 於是百姓奔趣，水陸輻輳，從之如雲。

translations.literal: Thereupon the hundred surnames ran to join him; by water and land hubs converged; those who followed him were like clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners flocked by river and road until his train swelled like clouds.

sentences.zh: 皇氏自以病久，懼有發動，靈乃留水一器令食之，每取水，輒以新水補處，二十餘年水清如新，塵垢不能加焉。

translations.literal: Lady Huang, deeming herself ill long, feared there would be a relapse; Ling then left one vessel of water and ordered her to take of it; whenever she drew water he always had new water replenish the place; more than twenty years the water was clear as new; dust and filth could not adhere to it.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing relapse, she kept his jar; each draught was topped with fresh water, and for over twenty years the liquid stayed crystal-clear, untainted by grime.

sentences.zh: 時高悝家有鬼怪，言語訶叱，投擲內外，不見人形，或器物自行，再三發火，巫祝厭劾而不能絕。

translations.literal: At that time in Gao Kui's house there were ghosts and goblins; they spoke and scolded; they threw things inside and outside; human form was not seen; at times implements moved of themselves; repeatedly fire broke out; shamans suppressed and cursed yet could not stop it.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Kui's mansion was plagued by bodiless voices, flying crockery, self-moving tools, and fires no exorcist could quell.

sentences.zh: 適值靈，乃要之。

translations.literal: They happened to meet Ling and therefore invited him.
translations.idiomatic: Meeting Xing Ling by chance, they pressed him to help.

sentences.zh: 靈於陌頭望其屋，謂悝曰：「此君之家邪？

translations.literal: Ling at the lane's end looked at their house and said to Kui, "Is this your lord's home?"
translations.idiomatic: From the lane mouth he studied the roofline and asked if it was Gao Kui's house.

sentences.zh: 」悝曰：「是也。

translations.literal: " Kui said, "It is so."
translations.idiomatic: Gao Kui confirmed it.

sentences.zh: 」靈曰：「知之足矣。

translations.literal: " Ling said, "Knowing suffices."
translations.idiomatic: Ling said knowing that was enough.

sentences.zh: 」悝固請之，靈不得已，至門，見符索甚多，謂悝曰：「當以正止邪，而以邪救邪，惡得已乎！

translations.literal: " Kui firmly pressed him; Ling had no choice; arriving at the gate he saw many talisman cords; he said to Kui, "One ought to use the upright to stop the deviant—yet using the deviant to save the deviant—how can that be right!"
translations.idiomatic: Dragged to the gate, he saw charms papering the lintel and scolded that chasing fiends with more sorcery could never set things right.

sentences.zh: 」並使焚之，惟據軒小坐而去，其夕鬼怪即絕。

translations.literal: " He together ordered them burned; only leaning on the veranda gallery he sat a little and departed; that night the ghosts and goblins at once ceased.
translations.idiomatic: He made them burn every charm, lingered briefly on the porch, and left; the haunting ended that very night.

sentences.zh: 靈所救愈多此類，然不取報謝。

translations.literal: Of those Ling saved and healed many were of this kind, yet he did not take reward or thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Most of his cures followed this pattern, yet he accepted no fee.

sentences.zh: 行不騎乘，長不娶妻，性至恭，見人即先拜，言輒自名。

translations.literal: In travel he did not ride mounts; grown he did not take a wife; his nature was utmost deferential; seeing a person he at once bowed first; in speech he always gave his own name.
translations.idiomatic: He walked everywhere, never wed, bowed before any interlocutor, and introduced himself by name.

sentences.zh: 凡草木之夭傷于山林者，必起理之，器物之傾覆于途路者，必舉正之。

translations.literal: Whatever grasses and trees prematurely injured in mountain forest—he invariably rose and set them right; whatever vessels overturned on roads—he invariably raised and righted them.
translations.idiomatic: He straightened wind-snapped saplings in the wild and righted overturned gear on the highway.

sentences.zh: 周旋江州間，謂其士人曰：「天地之於人物，一也，咸欲不失其情性，奈何制服人以為奴婢乎！

translations.literal: Moving back and forth amid Jiang Province he said to its gentlemen, "Heaven and earth toward people and things are one; all wish not to lose their essential nature—why compel and subdue people to make slaves and maids!"
translations.idiomatic: Ranging Jiangzhou, he lectured local scholars that heaven treated all beings alike and reproached those who enserfed others.

sentences.zh: 諸君若欲享多福以保性命，可悉免遣之。

translations.literal: " If you gentlemen wish to enjoy much fortune and preserve life and body, you may entirely dismiss and send them away freely."
translations.idiomatic: He urged them to free every bond servant if they valued long life.

sentences.zh: 」十餘年間，賴其術以濟者極多。

translations.literal: " In more than ten years those who relied on his art to be helped were extremely many.
translations.idiomatic: For a decade multitudes credited his teaching with deliverance.

sentences.zh: 後乃娶妻，畜車以奴婢，受貨賂致遺，於是其術稍衰，所療得失相半焉。

translations.literal: Only afterward did he wed and keep carts with slave maids; receiving goods, bribes, and bestowed gifts; from this his arts slightly declined; of those he treated, gain and loss were half and half.
translations.idiomatic: Later he married, kept carriages and bondsmen, and took bribes; his powers waned and his cures became hit or miss.

sentences.zh: 佛圖澄

translations.literal: Fotucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Fotucheng

sentences.zh: 佛圖澄，天竺人也。

translations.literal: Fotucheng was a man of Tianzhu.
translations.idiomatic: The monk Fotucheng hailed from India (Tianzhu).

sentences.zh: 本姓帛氏。

translations.literal: Originally his surname was the Bo clan.
translations.idiomatic: His clan name had been Bo.

sentences.zh: 少學道，妙通玄術。

translations.literal: In youth he studied the Dao and wondrously penetrated arcane arts.
translations.idiomatic: Trained in Daoist practice from boyhood, he mastered occult skills.

sentences.zh: ，來適洛陽，自雲百有餘歲，常服氣自養，能積日不食。

translations.literal: , coming he arrived at Luoyang; he declared himself more than a hundred years; constantly ingested qi to nurture himself; he could accumulate days without eating.
translations.idiomatic: He reached Luoyang claiming to exceed a century in age, nourished himself on breath discipline, and could fast for many successive days.

sentences.zh: 善誦神咒，能役使鬼神。

translations.literal: He was good at chanting divine spells; he could conscript and employ ghosts and spirits.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at spirit mantras and could bind ghosts to his will.

sentences.zh: 腹旁有一孔，常以絮塞之，每夜讀書，則拔絮，孔中出光，照於一室。

translations.literal: Beside his belly there was one hole; he constantly plugged it with cotton wadding; every night when reading books he then pulled the wadding; from the hole light issued, illuminating one room.
translations.idiomatic: A cotton-plugged aperture in his flank, uncorked at study time, cast enough radiance to light a chamber.

sentences.zh: 又嘗齋時，平旦至流水側，從腹旁孔中引出五藏六府洗之，訖，還內腹中。

translations.literal: Also once during fast days at dawn he went to the side of running water; from the hole beside his belly he drew out the five depots and six bowels and washed them; when finished he returned them inside the belly.
translations.idiomatic: At fasting dawn he once drew his viscera through that opening to rinse them in a stream, then tucked them back inside.

sentences.zh: 又能聽鈴音以言吉凶，莫不懸驗。

translations.literal: Also he could listen to bell sound to speak auspicious and inauspicious; none missed verification beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: He divined by temple bells, and every omen proved true beforehand.

sentences.zh: 及洛中寇亂，乃潛草野以觀變。

translations.literal: When there was bandit chaos in Luoyang he hid in grass and wilds to observe the changes.
translations.idiomatic: As Luoyang fell to rebels he withdrew to the wilderness to watch how events would turn.

sentences.zh: 石勒屯兵葛陂，專行殺戮，沙門遇害者其眾。

translations.literal: Shi Le encamped troops at Gebei; he exclusively practiced killing; Buddhist monks who met harm were very many.
translations.idiomatic: At Gebei Shi Le's army slaughtered mercilessly, and countless monks perished.

sentences.zh: 澄投勒大將軍郭黑略家，黑略每從勒征伐，輒豫克勝負，勒疑而問曰：「孤不覺卿有出眾智謀，而每知軍行吉凶何也？

translations.literal: Cheng threw himself on Shi Le's great general Guo Heilüe's household; Heilüe every time followed Shi Le on campaigns always beforehand divined victory and defeat; Le suspected and asked, saying, "I do not myself perceive you having surpassing wit and schemes—yet you always know the army's march auspicious and inauspicious—why is it?"
translations.idiomatic: Fotucheng took refuge with Shi Le's general Guo Heilüe, whose uncanny battlefield forecasts drew Shi Le's question: he saw no genius in Guo—so how did he always read every march?

sentences.zh: 」黑略曰：「將軍天挺神武，幽靈所助，有一沙門智術非常，雲將軍當略有區夏，己應為師。

translations.literal: " Heilüe said, "The general is heaven-born divine martial; hidden spirits assist; there is one Buddhist monk whose wisdom and arts are extraordinary; he says the general ought broadly to seize the Central Xia; I ought to be teacher."
translations.idiomatic: Guo Heilüe credited a strange monk who foretold Shi Le's conquest of the Central Plain and named himself disciple.

sentences.zh: 臣前後所白，皆其言也。

translations.literal: " What your servant before and after reported—all were his words."
translations.idiomatic: Every report Guo had made came from the monk.

sentences.zh: 」勒召澄，試以道術。

translations.literal: " Le summoned Cheng and tested him with Dao arts.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le summoned Fotucheng and put his thaumaturgy to trial.

sentences.zh: 澄即取缽盛水，燒香咒之，須臾缽中生青蓮花，光色曜日，勒由此信之。

translations.literal: Cheng then took a bowl filled with water, burned incense and chanted over it; in a moment in the bowl green lotus flowers were born; light and color dazzled the sun; from this Le believed him.
translations.idiomatic: He filled an alms bowl with water, cursed over incense, and raised azure lotuses whose glare outshone the sun—convincing Shi Le.

sentences.zh: 勒自葛陂還河北，過枋頭，枋頭人夜欲斫營，澄謂黑略曰：「須臾賊至，可令公知。

translations.literal: When Shi Le returned from Gebei to north of the river, passing Fangtou, Fangtou people by night wished to raid the camp; Cheng said to Heilüe, "In a moment bandits will arrive—may you make the duke know."
translations.idiomatic: Marching homeward past Fangtou, Fotucheng warned Guo Heilüe of a night strike so the warlord could brace his lines.

sentences.zh: 」果如其言，有備，故不敗。

translations.literal: " It was indeed as he said; there was preparedness; therefore they did not lose.
translations.idiomatic: The raid came as foretold, but preparedness averted defeat.

sentences.zh: 勒欲試澄，夜冠胄衣甲，執刀而坐，遣人告澄云：「夜來不知大將軍何所在。

translations.literal: Shi Le wished to test Cheng; by night he donned helmet and armor, grasped a sword and sat; he sent a man to tell Cheng saying, "In the night we do not know where the great general is."
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le staged a midnight alert in full armor to test the monk, sending a runner to claim the commander could not be found.

sentences.zh: 」使人始至，未及有言，澄逆問曰：「平居無寇，何故夜嚴？

translations.literal: " The messenger had just arrived; before there was speech, Cheng counter-asked saying, "In ordinary dwelling there is no raider—why by night are you on strict alert?"
translations.idiomatic: Before the envoy could speak, Fotucheng demanded why the camp stood battle-ready when no enemy threatened.

sentences.zh: 」勒益信之。

translations.literal: " Le all the more believed him.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le's trust only deepened.

sentences.zh: 勒後因忿，欲害諸道士，並欲苦澄。

translations.literal: Later Le because of rage wished to harm the various Daoist masters, and also wished to torment Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: In a fury Shi Le resolved to massacre Daoist adepts and torture Fotucheng too.

sentences.zh: 澄乃潛避至黑略舍，語弟子曰：「若將軍信至，問吾所在者，報雲不知所之。

translations.literal: Cheng thereupon secretly fled to Heilüe's lodging; he told disciples, "If the general's messenger arrives asking where I am, answer saying one does not know whither he has gone."
translations.idiomatic: Fotucheng hid with Guo Heilüe and ordered disciples, if messengers asked, to swear they did not know his whereabouts.

sentences.zh: 」既而勒使至，覓澄不得。

translations.literal: " Before long Le's messenger arrived; searching they could not obtain Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le's men arrived and found him gone.

sentences.zh: 使還報勒，勒驚曰：「吾有惡意向澄，澄舍我去矣。

translations.literal: " The messenger returned and reported to Le; Le startled said, "I had evil intent toward Cheng—Cheng abandoned me and left."
translations.idiomatic: The envoy's report left Shi Le thunderstruck that malice had driven the monk away.

sentences.zh: 」通夜不寢，思欲見澄。

translations.literal: " Through the night he did not sleep; he thought wanting to see Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: He lay awake the night through, longing for Fotucheng.

sentences.zh: 澄知勒意悔，明旦造勒。

translations.literal: Cheng knew Le's mind repented; at dawn next day he visited Le.
translations.idiomatic: Sensing the warlord's remorse, Fotucheng appeared at dawn.

sentences.zh: 勒曰：「昨夜何行？

translations.literal: Le said, "Last night where did you go?"
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le asked where he had been the night before.

sentences.zh: 」澄曰：「公有怒心，昨故權避公。

translations.literal: " Cheng said, "Your lordship had a heart of anger; yesterday I therefore temporarily avoided your lordship."
translations.idiomatic: The monk answered that Shi Le's wrath had forced him to step aside.

sentences.zh: 今改意，是以敢來。

translations.literal: Now you have changed your mind; therefore I dare to come.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the temper had cooled, he dared return.

sentences.zh: 勒大笑曰：「道人謬矣。」

translations.literal: Le greatly laughed saying, "The Daoist man errs."
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le roared with laughter and called him mistaken.

sentences.zh: 襄國城塹水源在城西北五里，其水源暴竭，勒問澄何以致水。

translations.literal: In Xiangguo city the moat's water source was five li northwest of the wall; its water source suddenly dried up utterly; Le asked Cheng how thereby to obtain water.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiangguo's ditch-fed spring five li northwest ran dry, Shi Le asked how to refill the works.

sentences.zh: 澄曰：「今當敕龍取水。

translations.literal: Cheng said, "Now ought to command the dragon to fetch water."
translations.idiomatic: Fotucheng said he would command a dragon to restore the flow.

sentences.zh: 」乃與弟子法首等數人至故泉源上，坐繩床，燒安息香，咒願數百言。

translations.literal: " Thereupon with disciples Fashou and others, several persons, he went to the old spring head above; sat rope bed; burned benzoin incense; chanted vows several hundred words.
translations.idiomatic: He led Fashou and a few disciples to the old spring, sat a rope cot, burned frankincense, and recited vows for hundreds of lines.

sentences.zh: 如此三日，水泫然微流，有一小龍長五六寸許，隨水而來，諸道士競往觀之。

translations.literal: Thus three days; water trickled faintly and flowed slightly; there was one small dragon five or six cun in length, following the water and coming; the various Daoists competed to go observe it.
translations.idiomatic: After three days a thin rivulet appeared bearing a dragonlet a few inches long that curious Daoists rushed to see.

sentences.zh: 有頃，水大至，隍塹皆滿。

translations.literal: After a moment water greatly arrived; moats and ditches all filled.
translations.idiomatic: Soon torrents refilled every moat and trench.

sentences.zh: 鮮卑段末波攻勒，眾甚盛。

translations.literal: Xianbei Duan Mobo attacked Shi Le; the host was very great.
translations.idiomatic: The Xianbei chief Duan Mobo assailed Shi Le with overwhelming numbers.

sentences.zh: 勒懼，問澄。

translations.literal: Le feared and asked Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le, daunted, consulted Fotucheng.

sentences.zh: 澄曰：「昨日寺鈴鳴雲，明旦食時，當擒段末波。

translations.literal: Cheng said, "Yesterday the monastery bell rang saying; tomorrow at the breakfast hour ought to capture Duan Mobo."
translations.idiomatic: Fotucheng cited the monastery bells: by tomorrow's mealtime Duan Mobo would be taken.

sentences.zh: 」勒登城望末波軍，不見前後，失色曰：「末波如此，豈可獲乎！

translations.literal: " Le climbed the wall to gaze at Mobo's army; he could not see front or rear; his color changed and he said, "Mobo like this—how can he be captured!"
translations.idiomatic: From the battlements the host stretched beyond sight, and Shi Le blanched—how could such a multitude yield their leader?

sentences.zh: 」更遣夔安問澄。

translations.literal: " He again sent Kui An to ask Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Kui An back to the monk for reassurance.

sentences.zh: 澄曰：「已獲末波矣。

translations.literal: Cheng said, "Already Mobo has been captured."
translations.idiomatic: Fotucheng insisted Duan Mobo was already taken.

sentences.zh: 」時城北伏兵出，遇末波，執之。

translations.literal: " At that time ambush troops north of the city emerged; they encountered Mobo and seized him.
translations.idiomatic: Northern ambushers sprang up and seized Mobo in the same stroke.

sentences.zh: 澄勸勒宥末波，遣還本國，勒從之，卒獲其用。

translations.literal: Cheng urged Shi Le to spare Duan Mobo and send him back to his native country; Shi Le followed him; finally he obtained his usefulness.
translations.idiomatic: Fotucheng persuaded Shi Le to spare Mobo and repatriate him, a mercy that later paid strategic dividends.

sentences.zh: 劉曜遣從弟岳攻勒，勒遣石季龍距之。

translations.literal: Liu Yao sent his cousin Yue to attack Shi Le; Shi Le sent Shi Jilong to oppose him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao dispatched Liu Yue while Shi Le countered with Shi Hu (Shi Jilong).

sentences.zh: 嶽敗，退保石梁塢，季龍堅柵守之。

translations.literal: Yue was defeated; withdrew defending Shiliang wu; Jilong firmly palisaded and guarded him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yue retreated to the Shiliang stockade ringed by Shi Hu's palisade.

sentences.zh: 澄在襄國，忽歎曰：「劉嶽可憫！

translations.literal: Cheng in Xiangguo suddenly sighed saying, "Liu Yue is pitiable!"
translations.idiomatic: Fotucheng in Xiangguo cried out in pity for Liu Yue.

sentences.zh: 」弟子法祚問其故，澄曰「昨日亥時，嶽已敗被執。

translations.literal: " Disciple Fazuo asked the reason; Cheng said, "Yesterday at the hai double-hour Yue already was defeated and taken."
translations.idiomatic: Asked why, he said Liu Yue had already fallen captive at the previous night's hai watch.

sentences.zh: 」果如所言。

translations.literal: " It was indeed as he spoke.
translations.idiomatic: Scouts confirmed every word.

sentences.zh: 及曜自攻洛陽，勒將救之，其群下咸諫以為不可。

translations.literal: When Yao himself attacked Luoyang, Shi Le was about to go save it; his host of subordinates all remonstrated deeming it not permissible.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yao besieged Luoyang, Shi Le prepared a relief march but every minister called it folly.

sentences.zh: 勒以訪澄，澄曰：「相輪鈴音云：'秀支替戾岡，僕穀劬禿當。

translations.literal: Shi Le consulted Cheng; Cheng said, "The reliquary-ring bell's sound says: 'Xiuzhi tiligang, pugu qutu dang.
translations.idiomatic: Consulting Fotucheng, he quoted the stupa bell: "Xiuzhi tiligang, pugu qutu dang."

sentences.zh: 」此羯語也，秀支，軍也。

translations.literal: " This is Jie language; xiuzhi, army.
translations.idiomatic: He glossed the phrase as Jie speech: xiuzhi meant "army."

sentences.zh: 替戾岡，出也。

translations.literal: Tiligang, going forth.
translations.idiomatic: The compound tiligang glossed the word for "sally forth" or "issue out."

sentences.zh: 僕谷，劉曜胡位也。

translations.literal: Pugu—Liu Yao's barbarian title.
translations.idiomatic: Pugu was the Jie-style epithet for Liu Yao's rank.

sentences.zh: 劬禿當，捉也。

translations.literal: Qutu dang—capture.
translations.idiomatic: The phrase qutu dang meant "to seize" or "to take captive."

sentences.zh: 此言軍出捉得曜也。

translations.literal: This saying is: the army goes forth and captures Yao.
translations.idiomatic: Taken together, the oracle meant the host would march out and take Liu Yao alive.

sentences.zh: 」又令一童子潔齋七日，取麻油合胭脂，躬自研於掌中，舉手示童子，粲然有輝。

translations.literal: He further ordered one boy to purify in fast seven days, take sesame oil and mix rouge, personally grind it in his palm, raise his hand and show the boy—it blazed with radiance.
translations.idiomatic: He had a novice fast seven days, blend sesame oil with rouge in his own palm, then lift his hand before the boy until it shone dazzling bright.

sentences.zh: 童子驚曰：「有軍馬甚眾，見一人長大白晳，以硃絲縛其肘。

translations.literal: The boy startled said, "There are very many troops and horses; I see one man, tall, large, fair and white, with vermilion silk binding his elbow.
translations.idiomatic: The boy cried out that he saw endless squadrons and a towering, pale figure with crimson cords about his forearm.

sentences.zh: 」澄曰：「此即曜也。

translations.literal: " Cheng said, "This is Yao.
translations.idiomatic: Fotucheng said, "That man is Liu Yao."

sentences.zh: 」勒其悅，遂赴洛距曜，生擒之。

translations.literal: " Le was greatly pleased; thereupon he hastened to Luoyang to oppose Yao and seized him alive.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le rejoiced, marched on Luoyang to meet Liu Yao, and took him prisoner alive.

sentences.zh: 勒僭稱趙天王，行皇帝事，敬澄彌篤。

translations.literal: Le usurped the title Heavenly King of Zhao and conducted the business of an emperor; his reverence for Cheng grew ever deeper.
translations.idiomatic: Having arrogated the style Heavenly King of Zhao while wielding imperial power, Shi Le honored Fotucheng more devotedly than before.

sentences.zh: 時石蔥將叛，澄誡勒曰：「今年蔥中有蟲，食必害人，可令百姓無食蔥也。

translations.literal: At the time Shi Cong was about to rebel; Cheng admonished Le saying, "This year within cong there are worms—eating it will surely harm people; you may order the hundred surnames not to eat cong.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Cong plotted revolt, Fotucheng punned on the word "scallion" (cong) and warned Shi Le that "scallions" harbored worms—so the realm should shun them.

sentences.zh: 」勒班告境內，慎無食蔥。

translations.literal: " Le promulgated notice within the borders: be careful not to eat cong.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le issued an edict forbidding the people to touch scallions.

sentences.zh: 俄而石蔥果走。

translations.literal: Before long Shi Cong indeed fled.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Shi Cong bolted, as foretold.

sentences.zh: 勒益重之，事必諮而後行，號曰大和尚。

translations.literal: Le esteemed him the more; for affairs he invariably consulted him before acting, and styled him Great Monk.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le weighted him still higher, took counsel before every move, and addressed him as the Great Monk.

sentences.zh: 勒愛子斌暴病死，將殯，勒歎曰：「朕聞虢太子死，扁鵲能生之，今可得效乎？

translations.literal: Le's beloved son Bin died suddenly of illness; about to lay him out for burial, Le sighed, "We have heard that when the crown prince of Guo died, Bian Que could restore life—may we now obtain such efficacy?"
translations.idiomatic: When his favorite son Shi Bin died suddenly on the eve of obsequies, Shi Le mourned aloud whether any healer could work Bian Que's miracle for the dead.

sentences.zh: 」乃令告澄。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he ordered that Cheng be informed.
translations.idiomatic: He sent word to Fotucheng.

sentences.zh: 澄取楊枝沾水，灑而咒之。

translations.literal: Cheng took a poplar twig, dipped it in water, sprinkled and chanted over him.
translations.idiomatic: Fotucheng dipped a willow spray in water, sprinkled the corpse, and intoned spells.

sentences.zh: 就執斌手曰：「可起矣！

translations.literal: He went and grasped Bin's hand saying, "You may rise!"
translations.idiomatic: He seized Shi Bin's hand and commanded him to rise.

sentences.zh: 」因此遂蘇，有頃，平復。

translations.literal: " From this he then revived; after a moment he was fully restored.
translations.idiomatic: The prince stirred and within moments seemed wholly recovered.

sentences.zh: 自是勒諸子多在澄寺中養之。

translations.literal: From this Le's various sons for the most part were reared in Cheng's monastery.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward most of Shi Le's sons were raised inside Fotucheng's temple.

sentences.zh: 勒死之年，天靜無風，而塔上一鈴獨鳴，澄謂眾曰：「鈴音雲，國有大喪，不出今年矣。

translations.literal: In the year Le died, heaven was still and without wind, yet on the pagoda one bell alone rang; Cheng told the assembly, "The bell's sound declares: the state has a great mourning—it will not extend beyond this year."
translations.idiomatic: The year Shi Le died, though the air was breathless, a lone stupa bell tolled; Fotucheng told the monks it portended a court bereavement before year's end.

sentences.zh: 」既而勒果死。

translations.literal: " Before long Le indeed died.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le soon followed.

sentences.zh: 及季龍僭位，遷都於鄴，傾心事澄，有重於勒。

translations.literal: When Jilong usurped the throne, he moved the capital to Ye and poured his heart into Cheng—more heavily than Le had.
translations.idiomatic: After Shi Hu (Shi Jilong) seized the throne and shifted the seat to Ye, he lavished attention on Fotucheng beyond even Shi Le's devotion.

sentences.zh: 下書衣澄以綾錦，乘以雕輦，朝會之日，引之升殿，常侍以下悉助舉輿，太子諸公扶翼而上，主者唱大和尚，眾坐皆起，以彰其尊。

translations.literal: He issued an edict to clothe Cheng in damask and brocade, to mount him on an engraved palanquin; on court-conference days he led him up the hall—below regular attendant rank all helped lift the litter, while the heir apparent and dukes steadied him from the sides; the herald cried "Great Monk," every seated man rose, thereby displaying his honor.
translations.idiomatic: Edicts robed the monk in silk, gave him a carved litter, and on audience days convoked him to the dais with ministers hoisting his chair and princes flanking him while criers hailed the Great Monk so that every official stood.

sentences.zh: 又使司空李農旦夕親問，其太子諸公五日一朝，尊敬莫與為比。

translations.literal: He also had Minister of Works Li Nong inquire morning and evening in person; his heir apparent and dukes attended audience every five days—none matched such reverence.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Li Nong attended him daily, while the heir and nobles presented themselves every fifth day—no one else enjoyed such deference.

sentences.zh: 支道林在京師，聞澄與諸石遊，乃曰：「澄公其以季龍為海鷗鳥也。

translations.literal: Zhi Daolin was in the capital; hearing that Cheng consorted with the various Shi, he said, "Master Cheng surely takes Jilong for a sea-gull bird."
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Daolin in the capital, learning that Fotucheng walked among the Shi clan, remarked that the master must treat Shi Hu as the heedless gull of the fable.

sentences.zh: 百姓因澄故多奉佛，皆營造寺廟，相競出家，真偽混淆，多生愆過。

translations.literal: Because of Cheng the hundred surnames for the most part embraced Buddhism, all building temples, vying to leave home—true and false mingled, and very many faults arose.
translations.idiomatic: On his account the populace turned fervently Buddhist, racing to found cloisters and tonsure until authentic practice blurred with sham and abuses multiplied.

sentences.zh: 季龍下書料簡，其著作郎王度奏曰：「佛，外國之神，非諸華所應祠奉。

translations.literal: Jilong issued an edict to examine and sort; his editorial director Wang Du memorialized, "The Buddha is a god of foreign lands—not what the Hua Xia ought to worship."
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu ordered a review; Editorial Director Wang Du argued that the Buddha was a foreign deity unfit for Chinese state cult.

sentences.zh: 漢代初傳其道，惟聽西域人得立寺都邑，以奉其神，漢人皆不出家。

translations.literal: When the Han first transmitted his way, only Western Regions men were permitted to erect temples in the capitals to serve their god; Han men none left home.
translations.idiomatic: At the Han introduction only Westerners could build urban monasteries, while native Chinese were barred from ordination.

sentences.zh: 魏承漢制，亦循前軌。

translations.literal: Wei inherited Han institutions and likewise followed the former track.
translations.idiomatic: Wei continued Han precedent on the same footing.

sentences.zh: 今可斷趙人悉不聽詣寺燒香禮拜，以遵典禮，其百辟卿士下逮眾隸，例皆禁之，其有犯者，與淫祀同罪。

translations.literal: Now we may cut off Zhao people entirely from hearing them go to temples to burn incense and bow in worship, thereby observing canonical rites—from the hundred ministers and gentlemen down to the mass of bond servants, by rule all forbid it; those who violate shall share the guilt of illicit sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: He urged that Zhao subjects be forbidden temples, incense, and prostration to honor classical rites, extending the ban from high ministers to common laborers on pain of illicit-cult penalties.

sentences.zh: 其趙人為沙門者，還服百姓。

translations.literal: Those Zhao people who are shramanas—return them to commoner garb.
translations.idiomatic: Any Zhao monk should be laicized.

sentences.zh: 」朝士多同度所奏。

translations.literal: " Court gentlemen for the most part concurred with Du's memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Most courtiers sided with Wang Du.

sentences.zh: 季龍以澄故，下書曰：「朕出自邊戎，忝君諸夏，至於饗祀，應從本俗。

translations.literal: Jilong, because of Cheng, issued an edict saying, "We issue from border barbarians and disgracefully rule the Hua Xia; as to feasting sacrifice, we ought to follow our native customs.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Shi Hu, for Fotucheng's sake, proclaimed his barbarian origins and insisted ancestral rites follow steppe custom.

sentences.zh: 佛是戎神，所應兼奉，其夷趙百姓有樂事佛者，特聽之。」

translations.literal: The Buddha is a barbarian god whom one ought jointly to serve; among barbarian and Zhao commoners who delight in serving the Buddha, we specially permit it."
translations.idiomatic: The Buddha, he wrote, was a frontier deity worthy of joint worship, and any Zhao or tribesman who wished to serve him might do so.

sentences.zh: 澄時止鄴城寺中，弟子遍于郡國。

translations.literal: Cheng at the time lodged in Ye's monastery; disciples filled every commandery and state.
translations.idiomatic: Fotucheng resided in the Ye temple while disciples spread through every province.

sentences.zh: 嘗遣弟子法常北至襄國，弟子法佐從襄國還，相遇于梁基城下，對車夜談，言及和尚，比旦各去。

translations.literal: Once he sent disciple Fachang north to Xiangguo; disciple Fazuo returned from Xiangguo; they met beneath Liangji city's wall, faced their carts and talked through the night, speaking of the monk; at dawn each departed.
translations.idiomatic: He once dispatched Fachang north to Xiangguo while Fazuo returned south; the two met below Liangji, spoke in their carriages until dawn of their master, then parted.

sentences.zh: 佐始入，澄逆笑曰：「昨夜爾與法常交車共說汝師邪？

translations.literal: When Zuo had just entered, Cheng greeted him laughing, "Last night did you and Fachang halt carts together and speak of your teacher?"
translations.idiomatic: As Fazuo entered, Fotucheng laughed that he had overheard their midnight colloquy about him.

sentences.zh: 」佐愕然愧懺。

translations.literal: " Zuo was stunned and ashamed in repentance.
translations.idiomatic: Fazuo froze, then blushed with contrition.

sentences.zh: 於是國人每相語：「莫起噁心，和尚知汝。

translations.literal: From this the people whenever they spoke to each other said, "Do not harbor evil intent—the monk knows you.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth folk whispered that no ill thought escaped the monk's ken.

sentences.zh: 」及澄之所在，無敢向其方面涕唾者。

translations.literal: " Wherever Cheng dwelt, none dared toward his direction spit or weep.
translations.idiomatic: None dared face his quarters to spit or weep.

sentences.zh: 季龍太子邃有二字，在襄國，澄語邃曰：「小阿彌比當得疾，可往看之。

translations.literal: Jilong's heir Sui had two sons in Xiangguo; Cheng told Sui, "Little Amita presently will fall ill—you may go look on him.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu's heir Shi Sui had two boys in Xiangguo; Fotucheng warned him the younger would sicken and bade him visit.

sentences.zh: 」邃即馳信往視，果已得疾。

translations.literal: " Sui immediately galloped a messenger to look; indeed he had already fallen ill.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Sui sent riders at once and found the child already stricken.

sentences.zh: 太醫殷騰及外國道士自言能療之。

translations.literal: Court physician Yin Teng and foreign Daoists declared themselves able to cure it.
translations.idiomatic: Palace physician Yin Teng and foreign adepts claimed they could heal him.

sentences.zh: 澄告弟子法牙曰：「正使聖人復出，不愈此疾，況此等乎！

translations.literal: Cheng told disciple Faya, "Even if a sage again appeared, he would not cure this illness—how much less these!"
translations.idiomatic: Fotucheng told Faya that neither sages nor charlatans could save the boy.

sentences.zh: 」後三日果死。

translations.literal: " After three days he indeed died.
translations.idiomatic: Three days later the child was dead.

sentences.zh: 邃將圖為逆，謂內豎曰：「和尚神通，儻發吾謀。

translations.literal: Sui was about to plot treason; he told the inner attendants, "The monk has divine penetration—if he should disclose my plot, it will be exposed."
translations.idiomatic: Shi Sui plotted revolt and muttered to eunuchs that Fotucheng's clairvoyance might expose him.

sentences.zh: 明日來者，當先除之。

translations.literal: " Those who come tomorrow—you should first eliminate them."
translations.idiomatic: He ordered tomorrow's visitors killed beforehand.

sentences.zh: 」澄月望將入覲季龍，謂弟子僧慧曰：「昨夜天神呼我曰：'明日若入，還勿過人。

translations.literal: " Cheng on the full moon was about to enter audience with Jilong; he told disciple Seng Hui, "Last night a heavenly deity called me saying, 'If tomorrow you enter, again do not pass others.'"
translations.idiomatic: On the day of audience Fotucheng warned Seng Hui that a spirit had forbidden him to "pass others" inside the palace.

sentences.zh: 」我儻有所過，汝當止我。

translations.literal: " If I perhaps pass someone, you ought to stop me.
translations.idiomatic: If he should cross someone's path, the disciple must check him.

sentences.zh: 」澄常入，必過邃。

translations.literal: " Cheng whenever he entered invariably passed Sui.
translations.idiomatic: His usual route always crossed Shi Sui's quarters.

sentences.zh: 邃知澄入，要侯甚苦。

translations.literal: Sui knew Cheng would enter and waited in ambush with bitter urgency.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Sui lay in desperate wait along that corridor.

sentences.zh: 澄將上南台，僧慧引衣，澄曰：「事不得止。

translations.literal: Cheng was about to ascend the south terrace; Seng Hui pulled his robe; Cheng said, "The affair cannot be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: As he climbed the south terrace Seng Hui tugged his robe, but Fotucheng said the summons could not be refused.

sentences.zh: 」坐未安便起，邃固留不住，所謀遂差。

translations.literal: " Before he was seated securely he rose; Sui firmly could not detain him—the plot therefore missed.
translations.idiomatic: He barely sat down, then rose and slipped Shi Sui's grasp, foiling the ambush.

sentences.zh: 還寺，歎曰：「太子作亂，其形將成，欲言難言，欲忍難忍。

translations.literal: Returning to the monastery he sighed, "The heir is raising rebellion—its form is about to complete; to speak is hard, to endure is hard."
translations.idiomatic: Back at the cloister he groaned that the heir's mutiny was ripening yet could neither be told outright nor silently borne.

sentences.zh: 」乃因事從容箴季龍，季龍終不能解。

translations.literal: " Thereupon by affairs he leisurely admonished Jilong; Jilong to the end could not understand.
translations.idiomatic: He circled the warning obliquely, but Shi Hu never grasped it.

sentences.zh: 俄而事發，方悟澄言。

translations.literal: Before long the affair broke out; then he understood Cheng's words.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot erupted, Shi Hu finally saw his meaning.

sentences.zh: 後郭黑略將兵征長安北山羌，墮羌伏中。

translations.literal: Later Guo Heilüe led troops to campaign against the northern-shan Qiang of Chang'an and fell into a Qiang ambush.
translations.idiomatic: Later Guo Heilüe campaigned against the northern-shan Qiang near Chang'an and walked into an ambush.

sentences.zh: 時澄在堂上坐，慘然改容曰：「郭公今有厄。

translations.literal: At the time Cheng sat in the hall; grimly he changed countenance saying, "Lord Guo now has calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Fotucheng, seated in the refectory, blanched and cried that Guo Heilüe was in mortal peril.

sentences.zh: 」乃唱云：「眾僧祝願。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he intoned, "All monks pray blessing."
translations.idiomatic: He called for the community to pray.

sentences.zh: 」澄又自祝願。

translations.literal: " Cheng again personally prayed blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Then he prayed himself.

sentences.zh: 須臾，更曰：若東南出者活，余向者則困。

translations.literal: After a moment he changed again saying, "If one exits southeast he lives; if toward the remaining directions then peril.
translations.idiomatic: Moments later he amended the omen: escape southeast meant life; other headings meant doom.

sentences.zh: 」復更祝願。

translations.literal: " Again he changed praying blessing.
translations.idiomatic: He prayed again.

sentences.zh: 有頃，曰：「脫矣。

translations.literal: After a moment he said, "He has escaped."
translations.idiomatic: Soon he announced deliverance.

sentences.zh: 」後月餘，黑略還，自說墜羌圍中，東南走，馬乏，正遇帳下人，推馬與之曰：「公乘此馬，小人乘公馬，濟與不濟，命也。

translations.literal: " After more than a month Heilüe returned; himself narrated that he fell within the Qiang encirclement, fled southeast, horses exhausted, just then met a man of his tent who pushed a horse to him saying, "My lord ride this horse; your servant rides my lord's horse—whether we ford or not is fate."
translations.idiomatic: A month later Guo Heilüe returned, telling how he broke southeast, foundered, and a retainer swapped mounts, saying survival was heaven's whim.

sentences.zh: 」略得其馬，故獲免。

translations.literal: " Heilüe obtained that horse; therefore he obtained escape.
translations.idiomatic: That remount won him his life.

sentences.zh: 推檢時日，正是澄祝願時也。

translations.literal: Checking the times and days, it was exactly when Cheng prayed blessing.
translations.idiomatic: The timestamps matched Fotucheng's prayers exactly.

sentences.zh: 時天旱，季龍遣其太子詣臨漳西滏口祈雨，久而不降，乃令澄自行，即有白龍二頭降於祠所，其日大雨方數千里。

translations.literal: At the time heaven was drought; Jilong sent his heir to Fukou west of Linzhang to pray for rain; long it did not descend; then he ordered Cheng himself to go—immediately there were two white dragons that descended at the shrine site; that day great rain fell across several thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: During a drought Shi Hu first sent the heir to pray at Fukou west of Linzhang, then Fotucheng himself; two white dragons alighted on the altar and rain swept thousands of li.

sentences.zh: 澄嘗遣弟子向西域市香，既行，澄告余弟子曰：「掌中見買香弟子在某處被劫垂死。

translations.literal: Cheng once sent disciples to the Western Regions to market incense; after they had gone, Cheng told the remaining disciples, "In my palm I see the incense-buying disciple at such-and-such a place being robbed and on the verge of death."
translations.idiomatic: When monks went west for incense, Fotucheng told those behind that vision showed the buyer ambushed and dying.

sentences.zh: 」因燒香祝願，遙救護之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he burned incense, prayed blessing, and from afar rescued and protected him.
translations.idiomatic: He burned incense and sent a distant deliverance.

sentences.zh: 弟子後還，雲某月某日某處為賊所劫，垂當見殺，忽聞香氣，賊無故自驚曰：「救兵已至。

translations.literal: The disciple afterward returned, saying on such month such day at such-and-such a place he was robbed by bandits; about to be killed, suddenly he smelled incense fragrance; the bandits without cause themselves startled said, "Relief troops have already arrived."
translations.idiomatic: The monk returned reporting that robbers had stayed his execution until they smelled incense and fled, crying that reinforcements had come.

sentences.zh: 」棄之而走。

translations.literal: " They abandoned him and ran.
translations.idiomatic: They dropped him and bolted.

sentences.zh: 黃河中舊不生黿，時有得者，以獻季龍。

translations.literal: In the Yellow River of old soft-shelled turtles were not born; at the time there was one obtained and presented to Jilong.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow River turtles were unheard of until one was caught and sent to Shi Hu.

sentences.zh: 澄見而之曰：「桓溫入河，其不久乎！

translations.literal: Cheng seeing it said to him, "Huan Wen enters the river—will it not be soon!"
translations.idiomatic: Fotucheng declared the omen meant Huan Wen would soon ford the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 」溫字元子，後果如其言也。

translations.literal: " Wen's style was Yuanzi; afterward it indeed was as his words.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen, styled Yuanzi, did exactly as he foretold.

sentences.zh: 季龍嘗晝寢，夢見群羊負魚從東北來，寤以訪澄。

translations.literal: Jilong once napped by day and dreamed a flock of sheep bearing fish came from the northeast; waking he consulted Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu dreamed sheep laden with fish from the northeast and asked Fotucheng on waking.

sentences.zh: 澄曰：「不祥也，鮮卑其有中原乎！

translations.literal: Cheng said, "It is inauspicious—the Xianbei will possess the Central Plain!"
translations.idiomatic: Fotucheng called it ill-omened: the Xianbei would take the heartland.

sentences.zh: 」後亦皆驗。

translations.literal: " Later too all were verified.
