translations.idiomatic: Later events bore him out.

sentences.zh: 澄嘗與季龍升中台，澄忽驚曰：「變，變，幽州當火災。

translations.literal: Cheng once with Jilong ascended the middle terrace; Cheng suddenly startled said, "Change, change—Youzhou will have a fire disaster."
translations.idiomatic: On the central tower he suddenly cried that Youzhou faced a great blaze.

sentences.zh: 」乃取酒噀之，久而笑曰：「救已得矣。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he took wine and sprayed it; after a long while he laughed saying, "The rescue has already been obtained."
translations.idiomatic: He spat wine into the air, then laughed that the danger was averted.

sentences.zh: 」季龍遣驗幽州，雲爾日火從四門起，西南有黑雲來，驟雨滅之，雨亦頗有酒氣。

translations.literal: " Jilong sent to verify Youzhou; they reported that day fire rose from the four gates; from the southwest there came black clouds; sudden rain extinguished it; the rain too rather had the smell of wine.
translations.idiomatic: Inspectors reported flames bursting from Youzhou's gates until black clouds and a reeking downpour—almost vinous—doused them.

sentences.zh: 石宣將殺石韜，宣先到寺與澄同坐，浮屠一鈴獨鳴，澄謂曰：「解鈴音乎？

translations.literal: Shi Xuan was about to kill Shi Tao; Xuan first arrived at the temple and sat together with Cheng; one pagoda bell alone rang; Cheng told him, "Do you understand the bell's sound?"
translations.idiomatic: Before Shi Xuan murdered Shi Tao he sat with Fotucheng while a lone bell tolled; the monk asked if he grasped its message.

sentences.zh: 鈴雲鬍子洛度。

translations.literal: The bell declares: the bearded man crosses the river.
translations.idiomatic: The bell, he said, meant "the bearded man fords the river"—a Jie gloss on the plot.

sentences.zh: 」宣變色曰：「是何言歟？

translations.literal: " Xuan changed color saying, "What sort of talk is this!"
translations.idiomatic: Shi Xuan flushed and demanded what he meant.

sentences.zh: 」澄謬曰：「老胡為道，不能山居無言，重茵美服，豈非洛度乎！

translations.literal: " Cheng falsely said, "The old barbarian practices the Way—unable to dwell in mountains in silence, layered mats and fine robes—is that not crossing the river!"
translations.idiomatic: Fotucheng feigned to mock his own luxury as a monk who could not keep mountain silence.

sentences.zh: 」石韜後至，澄孰視良久。

translations.literal: " Shi Tao afterward arrived; Cheng stared fixedly a long while.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Tao entered, Fotucheng studied him at length.

sentences.zh: 韜懼而問澄，澄曰：「怪公血臭，故相視耳。

translations.literal: Tao feared and asked Cheng; Cheng said, "I marveled that lord's blood stank—therefore I gazed."
translations.idiomatic: Shi Tao quailed; Fotucheng said only that he smelled blood on him.

sentences.zh: 」季龍夢龍飛西南，自天而落，旦而問澄，澄曰：「禍將作矣，宜父子慈和，深以慎之。

translations.literal: " Jilong dreamed a dragon flew southwest, from heaven and fell; at dawn he asked Cheng; Cheng said, "Disaster is about to arise—you ought to be father-son kind and harmonious, deeply thereby be cautious."
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu dreamed a dragon plummet from the sky; Fotucheng warned of coming woe and urged father-son harmony.

sentences.zh: 」季龍引澄入東閣，與其後杜氏問訊之。

translations.literal: " Jilong led Cheng into the east pavilion and with his empress Du questioned him.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu brought him to the east gallery for Empress Du to question.

sentences.zh: 澄曰：「脅下有賊，不出十日，自浮圖以西，此殿以東，當有血流，慎勿東也。

translations.literal: Cheng said, "Beneath the ribs there is a bandit—within ten days, from west of the pagoda to east of this hall, there ought to be flowing blood—be careful not to go east."
translations.idiomatic: He warned of assassins within ten days, blood west of the stupa and east of the hall, and bade them shun the eastern precincts.

sentences.zh: 」杜後曰：「和尚耄邪！

translations.literal: " Empress Du said, "Monk, are you senile!"
translations.idiomatic: Empress Du sneered that the monk was senile.

sentences.zh: 何處有賊？

translations.literal: " Where would there be bandits?"
translations.idiomatic: She asked where brigands could hide.

sentences.zh: 」澄即易語云：「六情所受，皆悉是賊。

translations.literal: " Cheng immediately changed words saying, "The six emotions' receipts—all are entirely bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Fotucheng pivoted, saying every passion was a robber of the mind.

sentences.zh: 老自應耄，但使少者不昏即好耳。

translations.literal: The old naturally ought to be senile—but let it suffice that the young not be muddled."
translations.idiomatic: He granted his own dotage if only the young stayed clear-headed.

sentences.zh: 」遂便寓言，不復彰的。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he then spoke in allegory, no longer making it explicit.
translations.idiomatic: He dropped explicit prophecy and spoke in parables.

sentences.zh: 後二日，宣果遣人害韜於佛寺中，欲因季龍臨喪殺之。

translations.literal: After two days Xuan indeed sent men to harm Tao inside a Buddhist temple, wishing by Jilong's coming to the funeral to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Two days later Shi Xuan had Shi Tao murdered in a monastery, planning to strike Shi Hu at the obsequies.

sentences.zh: 季龍以澄先誡，故獲免。

translations.literal: Jilong because Cheng had beforehand warned therefore obtained escape.
translations.idiomatic: Forewarned by Fotucheng, Shi Hu escaped the trap.

sentences.zh: 及宣被收，澄諫季龍曰：「皆陛下之子也，何為重禍邪！

translations.literal: When Xuan was arrested, Cheng remonstrated Jilong saying, "They are all Your Majesty's sons—why double the calamity!"
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Xuan was seized, Fotucheng begged Shi Hu not to compound the tragedy among his sons.

sentences.zh: 陛下若含怒加慈者，尚有六十餘歲。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty will contain wrath and add kindness, still there are more than sixty years.
translations.idiomatic: Mercy, he said, could yet extend Shi Hu's life sixty-some years.

sentences.zh: 如必誅之，宣當為彗星下掃鄴宮。

translations.literal: If you must execute him, Xuan ought to become a broom-comet sweeping down the Ye palace.
translations.idiomatic: If Shi Xuan were put to death, a comet would scour the Ye palaces—so he warned.

sentences.zh: 」季龍不從。

translations.literal: " Jilong did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu refused the plea.

sentences.zh: 後月餘，有一妖馬，髦尾皆有燒狀，入中陽門，出顯陽門，東首東宮，皆不得入，走向東北，俄爾不見。

translations.literal: After more than a month there was one demon horse—mane and tail both had scorched marks—it entered Zhongyang Gate, exited Xianyang Gate, turned east toward the Eastern Palace, all could not enter, ran toward the northeast, before long disappeared.
translations.idiomatic: A month later a spectral horse with burnt mane and tail galloped from Zhongyang to Xianyang gate, wheeled toward the Eastern Palace yet could not enter, then fled northeast and vanished.

sentences.zh: 澄聞而歎曰：「災其及矣！

translations.literal: Cheng heard it and sighed, saying, "Calamity will reach us!
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the news, Fotucheng sighed, "Disaster is upon us!

sentences.zh: 」季龍大享群臣于太武前殿，澄吟曰：「殿乎，殿乎！

translations.literal: " Shi Hu gave a great feast to the host of ministers before the Hall of Martial Might; Cheng chanted, "Hall, O hall!
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu feasted his ministers before the Hall of Martial Might; Fotucheng chanted, "The hall—alas, the hall!

sentences.zh: 棘子成林，將壞人衣。

translations.literal: Thorns have grown into a forest—they will tear people's robes."
translations.idiomatic: Brambles have grown into a thicket—they will shred men's garments."

sentences.zh: 」季龍令發殿石下視之，有棘生焉。

translations.literal: " Shi Hu ordered the hall stones lifted to look beneath, and brambles were growing there.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu had workmen pry up the foundation stones and found thorns sprouting underneath.

sentences.zh: 冉閔小字棘奴。

translations.literal: Ran Min's childhood byname was Thorn-slave.
translations.idiomatic: Ran Min's pet name had been "Slave of the Thorns."

sentences.zh: 季龍造太武殿初成，圖畫自古賢聖、忠臣、孝子、烈士、貞女，皆變為胡狀，旬餘，頭悉縮入肩中，惟冠䯰仿佛微出，季龍大惡之，秘而不言也。

translations.literal: When Shi Hu first completed the Hall of Martial Might, the painted images of ancient worthies, loyal ministers, filial sons, martyrs, and chaste women all changed into Hu features; after ten-odd days their heads all shrank into their shoulders, only the caps and topknots faintly showing; Shi Hu deeply loathed it but kept silent.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Hu finished the new Hall of Martial Might, every fresco of ancient sages, loyal ministers, filial sons, martyrs, and chaste wives morphed into steppe faces; within a fortnight the heads had sunk into the shoulders so that only the hats and hair-knots peeked forth. Shi Hu was revolted but told no one.

sentences.zh: 澄對之流涕，乃自啟塋墓於鄴西紫陌，還寺，獨語曰：「得三年乎？

translations.literal: Cheng wept at this, then personally selected a grave site west of Ye on Purple Lane, returned to the monastery, and spoke alone, saying, "May I have three years?
translations.idiomatic: Fotucheng wept at the sight, chose his own tomb west of Ye on Purple Road, returned to the cloister, and muttered, "Will I get three years?

sentences.zh: 」自答：「不得。

translations.literal: " He answered himself: "You may not."
translations.idiomatic: He answered himself: "No."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「得二年、一年、百日、一月乎？

translations.literal: " Again he said, "Two years, one year, one hundred days, one month—may I?
translations.idiomatic: "Two years? A year? A hundred days? A month?

sentences.zh: 」自答：「不得。

translations.literal: " Again he answered himself: "You may not."
translations.idiomatic: "No."

sentences.zh: 」遂無復言。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he said no more.
translations.idiomatic: He fell silent.

sentences.zh: 謂弟子法祚曰：「戊申歲禍亂漸萌，己酉石氏當滅。

translations.literal: He told his disciple Fazuo, "In the wushen year turmoil will gradually sprout; in the jiyou year the Shi clan shall perish.
translations.idiomatic: To his disciple Fazuo he said, "Strife will stir in the wushen year, and the House of Shi will fall in jiyou.

sentences.zh: 吾及其未亂，先從化矣。

translations.literal: Before it has yet erupted in chaos, I shall first go to transformation."
translations.idiomatic: I shall quit this life before the storm breaks."

sentences.zh: 」卒于鄴宮寺。

translations.literal: " He died at the Ye palace monastery.
translations.idiomatic: He passed away in the imperial monastery at Ye.

sentences.zh: 後有沙門從雍州來，稱見澄西入關，季龍掘而視之，惟有一石無屍。

translations.literal: Later a monk coming from Yongzhou claimed to have seen Cheng entering the pass westward; Shi Hu exhumed and looked, and there was only one stone, no corpse.
translations.idiomatic: Later a monk from Yongzhou swore he had seen Fotucheng riding west through the passes; Shi Hu opened the grave and found only a slab of stone—no body.

sentences.zh: 季龍惡之曰：「石者，朕也，葬我而去，吾將死矣。

translations.literal: Shi Hu detested it and said, "Stone—that is Us; burying Me and leaving—We are about to die!
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu took it ill: "'Stone' is me—he buried his token and walked away—I am dying!

sentences.zh: 」因而遇疾。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: He fell ill on the spot.

sentences.zh: 明年，季龍死，遂大亂。

translations.literal: The next year Shi Hu died, and great chaos ensued.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Shi Hu died, and the realm collapsed into chaos.

sentences.zh: 麻襦

translations.literal: Ma Ru.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Ru

sentences.zh: 麻襦者，不知何許人也，莫得其姓名。

translations.literal: The one called Ma Ru—none knew whence he came; his name could not be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: The man called "Hemp Cloak"—no one knew his origin or his real name.

sentences.zh: 石季龍時，在魏縣市中乞丐，恆著麻襦布裳，故時人謂之麻襦。

translations.literal: In the time of Shi Jilong, in the market of Wei county he begged; he always wore a hemp bodice and cloth skirt, so people of the time called him Ma Ru.
translations.idiomatic: Under Shi Hu he begged in the Wei county marketplace, always dressed in a homespun hemp jacket, hence the nickname.

sentences.zh: 言語卓越，狀如狂者，乞得米穀不食，輒散置大路，雲飴天馬。

translations.literal: His speech was outstanding; his mien was like a madman's; grain he begged he did not eat but scattered on the great road, saying he fed the heaven-sent steeds.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke in lofty riddles like a man possessed; the grain he received he never ate but strewed across the highway, claiming he was foddering heaven's horses.

sentences.zh: 趙興太守籍狀收送詣季龍。

translations.literal: The Zhao-xing prefect registered his particulars, seized him, and sent him to Shi Hu.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect of Zhao-xing had him arrested on the rolls and escorted him to Shi Hu.

sentences.zh: 先是，佛圖澄謂季龍曰：「國東二百里某月日當送一非常人，勿殺之也。

translations.literal: Earlier Fotucheng had told Shi Hu, "On a certain day two hundred li east of the capital an extraordinary man will be delivered—do not kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Fotucheng had warned Shi Hu, "On such-and-such a day, two hundred li east of your capital, an extraordinary man will arrive—do not execute him.

sentences.zh: 」如期果至。

translations.literal: " It came to pass as on that date.
translations.idiomatic: He arrived exactly as foretold.

sentences.zh: 季龍與共語，了無異言，惟道：「陛下當終一柱殿下。

translations.literal: Shi Hu conversed with him; he had no unusual words, only saying, "Your Majesty will end beneath a single-pillar hall.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu spoke with him; he offered nothing remarkable except: "Your Majesty will die beneath a one-pillar hall.

sentences.zh: 」季龍不解，送以詣澄。

translations.literal: " Shi Hu did not understand and sent him to Fotucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Puzzled, Shi Hu sent him on to Fotucheng.

sentences.zh: 麻襦謂澄曰：「昔在光和中會，奄至今日。

translations.literal: Ma Ru said to Cheng, "Formerly at the Zhonghui gathering of the Guanghe era—suddenly we have reached today.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Ru told Fotucheng, "We met at the Zhonghui assembly in the Guanghe era—now suddenly we stand in this age.

sentences.zh: 酉戎受玄命，絕曆終有期。

translations.literal: You-rong receives the dark mandate; cutting off the calendar—termination has its appointed time.
translations.idiomatic: The Shi host receives the hidden mandate; the dynasty's span is fixed and its end is timed.

sentences.zh: 金離消于壞，邊荒不能遵，驅除靈期跡，莫已已之懿。

translations.literal: Metal departs dissolving in ruin; the border wastes cannot be followed; driving off the tracks of spirit-destiny—none can exhaust the splendor.
translations.idiomatic: Metal melts in the ruin; the frontiers will not hold order; fate's footprints are swept away—nothing can halt its awful closure.

sentences.zh: 裔苗葉繁，其來方積。

translations.literal: Offshoots' leaves multiply abundantly; their advent is still piling up.
translations.idiomatic: Sprigs leaf thickly; the onrush has only begun to mass.

sentences.zh: 休期於何期，永以歎之。

translations.literal: When is the auspicious term—at what term? Forever thus I sigh.
translations.idiomatic: When rests the appointed time—if ever? I sigh without end.

sentences.zh: 」澄曰：「天回運極，否將不支，九木水為難，無可以術寧。

translations.literal: " Cheng said, "Heaven's wheel turns—fate is at its limit; decline will not hold up; nine, wood, and water form calamity; nothing by art can bring peace.
translations.idiomatic: Fotucheng replied, "The cosmic cycle has turned; decline cannot be propped up; wood and water among the stems spell disaster—no rite can quiet it.

sentences.zh: 玄哲雖存世，莫能基必莫能基必頹。

translations.literal: Though dark sages remain in the world, none can shore the inevitable, none can shore the inevitable collapse.
translations.idiomatic: Sages walk among us still, yet none can buttress what is bound to fall.

sentences.zh: 久游閻浮利，擾擾多此患。

translations.literal: Long wandering in Jambudvipa—restless, many are these cares.
translations.idiomatic: Long have we roamed Jambudvipa; turmoil heaps such grief upon us.

sentences.zh: 行登陵雲宇，會于虛遊間。

translations.literal: Walk and ascend the cloud-scraping tower; meet in the void-roaming expanse.
translations.idiomatic: We shall climb the tower that brushes the clouds and rendezvous in the emptiness between wanderings.

sentences.zh: 」其所言人莫能曉。

translations.literal: " What he spoke none could understand.
translations.idiomatic: No one could fathom his words.

sentences.zh: 季龍遣驛馬送還本縣，既出城，請步，云：「我當有所過，君至合口橋見待。

translations.literal: Shi Hu sent post horses to escort him back to his native county; having left the city, he asked to go on foot, saying, "I must make a stop; you await me at the He-kou Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu sent him home by relay; outside the walls he insisted on walking, saying, "I have an errand—meet me at Forkmouth Bridge.

sentences.zh: 」使人如言而馳，至橋，麻襦已先至。

translations.literal: " The messenger rode hard as told; arriving at the bridge, Ma Ru was already there first.
translations.idiomatic: The runner spurred on as bid yet found Ma Ru waiting when he reached the span.

sentences.zh: 後慕容俊投季龍屍于漳水，倚橋柱不流，時人以為「一柱殿下」即謂此也。

translations.literal: Later Murong Jun cast Shi Hu's corpse into the Zhang River; it lodged against a bridge pier and would not float; people of the time thought "beneath a single-pillar hall" referred to this.
translations.idiomatic: Later Murong Jun threw Shi Hu's body into the Zhang—where it snagged on a bridge pier and refused to float; folk then saw the prophecy of the "one-pillar hall" in that very pier.

sentences.zh: 及元帝嗣位江左，亦以為「天馬」之應云。

translations.literal: When Yuan-di succeeded in the left bank of the Yangzi, they likewise deemed it the verification of the "heaven steeds."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yuan took the throne south of the Yangzi, courtiers likewise cited it as proof of the "heavenly horses" omen.

sentences.zh: 單道開

translations.literal: Shan Daokai.
translations.idiomatic: Shan Daokai

sentences.zh: 單道開，敦煌人也。

translations.literal: Shan Daokai was a man of Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Shan Daokai came from Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 常衣粗褐，或贈以繒服，皆不著，不畏寒暑，晝夜不臥。

translations.literal: Constantly he wore coarse hemp; if given silk robes he would not wear them; he feared neither cold nor heat; day and night he did not lie down.
translations.idiomatic: He always wore burlap rejects; silks offered him went unworn; heat and cold never troubled him, and he never slept by day or night.

sentences.zh: 恆服細石子，一吞數枚，日一服，或多或少。

translations.literal: Constantly he ingested fine pebbles, swallowing several at once, once a day, more or less.
translations.idiomatic: He swallowed several small stones each day, in greater or lesser number.

sentences.zh: 好山居，而山樹諸神見異形試之，初無懼色。

translations.literal: He loved dwelling in mountains; mountain-tree spirits showed strange forms to test him—at first he had no fear.
translations.idiomatic: He preferred hermitage in the hills; genii of grove and crag shifted shape to test him, yet he never flinched.

sentences.zh: 石季龍時，從西平來，一日行七百里，其一沙彌年十四，行亦及之。

translations.literal: In Shi Jilong's time he came from Xiping, traveling seven hundred li in one day; one novice śrāmaṇera of fourteen years kept pace in the march.
translations.idiomatic: Under Shi Hu he marched from Xiping seven hundred li in a single day; a fourteen-year-old novice matched his pace.

sentences.zh: 至秦州，表送到鄴，季龍令佛圖澄與語，不能屈也。

translations.literal: Reaching Qinzhou, he was memorialized and sent to Ye; Shi Hu ordered Fotucheng to speak with him and could not bend him.
translations.idiomatic: Local officials memorialized and sent him to Ye; Shi Hu set Fotucheng to debate him and neither could break the other.

sentences.zh: 初止鄴城西沙門法綝祠中，後徙臨漳昭德寺。

translations.literal: At first he lodged at the shrine of the monk Fachin west of Ye; later he moved to Zhaode Temple in Linzhang.
translations.idiomatic: First he stayed at Monk Fachin's sanctuary west of Ye, then moved to Zhaode Monastery at Linzhang.

sentences.zh: 于房內造重閣，高八九尺，于上編管為禪室，常坐其中。

translations.literal: Inside his cell he built a double gallery eight or nine chi high, wove bamboo into a meditation chamber atop it, and often sat therein.
translations.idiomatic: Within his room he raised a loft eight or nine feet high, lattice-wove canes into a meditation cell at the top, and habitually sat there.

sentences.zh: 季龍資給甚厚，道開皆以施人。

translations.literal: Shi Hu supplied him lavishly; Daokai gave it all away to others.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu lavished stipends on him, yet he passed every gift to the needy.

sentences.zh: 人或來諮問者，道開都不答。

translations.literal: When people came to consult and question, Daokai answered none.
translations.idiomatic: Questioners who sought counsel received no reply.

sentences.zh: 日服鎮守藥數丸，大如梧子，藥有松蜜姜桂伏苓之氣，時復飲荼蘇一二升而已。

translations.literal: Daily he took several pellets of "stabilizing" medicine, wutong-seed-sized, the medicine having the scent of pine honey, ginger, cinnamon, and poria; at times he drank one or two sheng of tusu only.
translations.idiomatic: He swallowed a few wutong-sized "steadying" pills each day—scented of pine honey, ginger, cinnamon, and poria—and occasionally drank a liter or two of herb broth, nothing more.

sentences.zh: 自雲能療目疾，就療者頗驗。

translations.literal: He claimed he could cure eye ailments; those who received treatment found it often verified.
translations.idiomatic: He claimed he could heal the eyes, and patients often went away cured.

sentences.zh: 視其行動，狀若有神。

translations.literal: Observing his movements, he seemed as if possessed by spirits.
translations.idiomatic: His gait and manner looked almost otherworldly.

sentences.zh: 佛圖澄曰：「此道士觀國興衰，若去者，當有大亂。

translations.literal: Fotucheng said, "This Daoist observes the state's rise and fall; if he leaves, there will be great turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: Fotucheng said, "This adept reads the kingdom's fate; should he depart, great upheaval will follow.

sentences.zh: 」及季龍末，道開南渡許昌，尋而鄴中大亂。

translations.literal: " At the end of Shi Hu's reign Daokai crossed south to Xuchang; soon Ye fell into great chaos.
translations.idiomatic: Toward Shi Hu's end Shan Daokai crossed south to Xuchang; chaos soon engulfed Ye.

sentences.zh: 至京師，後至南海，入羅浮山，獨處茅茨，蕭然物外。

translations.literal: He reached the capital, later reached the South Sea, entered Mount Luofu, dwelt alone in a thatched hut, aloof from the world.
translations.idiomatic: He went to the capital, then to the southern sea, withdrew to Mount Luofu, and lived alone in a brush hut, utterly beyond worldly dust.

sentences.zh: 年百餘歲，卒於山舍，敕弟子以屍置石穴中，弟子乃移入石室。

translations.literal: Past a hundred years he died in a mountain hut; he ordered disciples to place the corpse in a stone grotto; the disciples instead moved it into a stone chamber.
translations.idiomatic: He lived past a century and died in his mountain lodge, commanding disciples to lay his body in a rock hollow; they laid him in a stone cell instead.

sentences.zh: 陳郡袁宏為南海太守，與弟穎叔及沙門支法防共登羅浮山，至石室口，見道開形骸如生，香火瓦器猶存。

translations.literal: Yuan Hong of Chen commandery was South Sea prefect; with his brother Yingshu and the monk Zhi Fafang together they climbed Mount Luofu, arriving at the stone chamber mouth; they saw Daokai's form as if alive, incense-fire earthenware still present.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Hong of Chen, serving as South Sea prefect, climbed Luofu with his brother Yingshu and Monk Zhi Fafang; at the mouth of the stone cell they found Shan Daokai's corpse lifelike, incense bowls still in place.

sentences.zh: 宏曰：「法師業行殊群，正當如蟬蛻耳。

translations.literal: Hong said, "The master's practice transcends the crowd—this is rightly like cicada sloughing.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Hong said, "The master's vocation set him apart—surely this is the cast-off husk of a cicada.

sentences.zh: 」乃為之贊雲。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he composed a eulogy for him.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore composed a verse in his honor.

sentences.zh: 黃泓

translations.literal: Huang Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Hong

sentences.zh: 黃泓，字始長，魏郡斥丘人也。

translations.literal: Huang Hong, style name Shizhang, was a man of Chiqiu in Wei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Hong, courtesy name Shizhang, was a native of Chiqiu in Wei commandery.

sentences.zh: 父沈，善天文秘術。

translations.literal: His father Shen was skilled in astronomy and secret arts.
translations.idiomatic: His father Huang Shen excelled at astronomy and occult techniques.

sentences.zh: 泓從父受業，精妙逾深，兼博覽經史，尤明《禮》《易》。

translations.literal: Hong studied from his father, his refinement growing ever deeper; he also broadly read the classics and histories, especially mastering the Rites and Changes.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Hong learned from his father, surpassing him in subtlety, and broad reading made him a master of the Book of Rites and Book of Changes.

sentences.zh: 性忠勤，非禮不動。

translations.literal: By nature loyal and diligent, without ritual propriety he did not act.
translations.idiomatic: Loyal and diligent by temperament, he never stirred without propriety.

sentences.zh: 永嘉之亂，與渤海高瞻避地幽州，說瞻曰：「王浚昏暴，終必無成，宜思去就以圖久安。

translations.literal: During the Yongjia turmoil he fled with Gao Zhan of Bohai to shelter in Youzhou, and he urged Zhan, "Wang Jun is benighted and cruel and will surely accomplish nothing in the end; you should consider staying or going to plan long stability.
translations.idiomatic: When Yongjia's wars scattered the realm, he fled with Gao Zhan of Bohai to Youzhou and warned him, "Wang Jun is violent and foolish—nothing lasting can come of him; weigh whether to stay or leave if you seek peace.

sentences.zh: 慕容廆法政修明，虛懷引納，且讖言真人出東北，儻或是乎？

translations.literal: Murong Hui's laws and governance are cultivated and clear; he opens his mind and draws men in; moreover prophecies say the true man will arise in the northeast—perhaps this is it?
translations.idiomatic: Murong Hui governs with clarity, welcomes talent openly, and omens place the "true man" in the northeast—could that be he?

sentences.zh: 宜相與歸之，同建事業。

translations.literal: We ought together to submit to him and jointly establish enterprise."
translations.idiomatic: Let us both go to him and build something lasting together."

sentences.zh: 」瞻不從。

translations.literal: " Zhan did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Zhan refused.

sentences.zh: 泓乃率宗族歸廆，廆待以客禮，引為參軍，軍國之務動輒訪之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Hong led his clan to submit to Hui; Hui received him with guest rites, appointed him army counselor, and in military and state affairs invariably consulted him.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Hong led his kinsmen to Murong Hui, who honored him as a guest, named him staff adviser, and sought his counsel on every civil and military matter.

sentences.zh: 泓指說成敗，事皆如言。

translations.literal: Hong pointed out success and failure; events all matched his words.
translations.idiomatic: His forecasts of victory and defeat came true every time.

sentences.zh: 廆常曰：「黃參軍，孤之仲翔也。

translations.literal: Hui always said, "Counselor Huang is Our Zhongxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Hui often said, "Counselor Huang is my Yu Fan."

sentences.zh: 」及皝嗣位，遷左常侍，領史官，甚重之。

translations.literal: " When Huang succeeded, he was promoted to Left Regular Attendant, heading the office of historians, and was greatly esteemed.
translations.idiomatic: When Murong Huang succeeded, Huang Hong rose to Left Regular Attendant and chief historiographer, deeply trusted.

sentences.zh: 石季龍攻皝，皝將走遼東，泓曰：「賊有敗氣，無可憂也，不過二日，必當奔潰。

translations.literal: Shi Hu attacked Huang; Huang was about to flee to Liaodong; Hong said, "The foe has the qi of defeat—nothing to worry about; within two days they will surely flee in collapse.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Hu struck Murong Huang, who prepared to bolt for Liaodong, Huang Hong said, "The enemy already wears defeat—worry not; within two days they will rout themselves.

sentences.zh: 宜嚴勒士馬，為追擊之備。

translations.literal: You should strictly marshal men and horses and make ready to pursue and strike.
translations.idiomatic: Muster your troops for a hard pursuit.

sentences.zh: 」皝曰：「今寇盛如此，卿言必走，孤未敢信。

translations.literal: " Huang said, "Now the raiders are this strong; you say they will surely flee—We do not dare believe.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Huang replied, "The invaders are overwhelming—how can I trust talk of their flight?

sentences.zh: 」泓曰：「殿下言盛者，人事耳，臣言必走者，天時也，胡足為疑！

translations.literal: " Hong said, "What Your Highness calls 'strong' is human circumstance; what your servant says will flee is heaven's season—what is there to doubt!
translations.idiomatic: Huang Hong answered, "Your Highness sees their strength in human terms; I see their rout in heaven's sign—what room for doubt!

sentences.zh: 」及期，季龍果退，皝益奇之。

translations.literal: " When the term came, Shi Hu indeed withdrew; Huang all the more marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: On schedule Shi Hu retreated, and Murong Huang prized him the more.

sentences.zh: 及慕容俊即王位，遷從事中郎，儁聞冉閔亂，將圖中原，訪之於泓，泓勸行，儁從之。

translations.literal: When Murong Jun assumed the princely throne, he was promoted to palace internuncio; when Jun heard of Ran Min's rebellion and intended to seize the Central Plain, he consulted Hong; Hong urged the campaign; Jun followed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Murong Jun took the throne, Huang Hong became palace secretary; learning of Ran Min's revolt, Murong Jun planned a push into the Central Plain, asked Huang Hong, accepted his counsel to march, and acted on it.

sentences.zh: 及僭號，署為進謀將軍、太史令、關內侯，尋加奉車都尉、西海太守、領太史令、開陽亭侯，又封平舒縣五等伯，常從左右，諮決大事，靈台令許敦害其寵，諂事慕容評，設異議以毀之，及以泓為太史靈台諸署統，加給事中。

translations.literal: When he usurped the imperial style, he was appointed Advance-Strategy General, Grand Astrologer, Marquis Within the Pass; soon added Cavalry-guard Commandant, West Sea grand warden, concurrent Grand Astrologer, Kaiting Village Marquis; further ennobled as fifth-rank baron of Pingshu county, always attending left and right, deciding great affairs; Lingtai Director Xu Dun envied his favor, flattered Murong Ping, raised contrary views to slander him, whereupon he appointed Hong superintendent of the Lingtai and Grand Astrology offices, plus Requested-within-the-Palace.
translations.idiomatic: After Murong Jun claimed the throne, Huang Hong received a string of posts—general of forward counsel, grand astrologer, marquis within the passes—soon augmented by commandant of the imperial carriage, West Sea governor while still astrologer, Kaiting precinct nobleman, and fifth-rank baron of Pingshu; he stayed at the ruler's elbow advising state policy. Lingtai chief Xu Dun resented his favor, curried Murong Ping's goodwill, and carped against him until the court consolidated Huang Hong's observatory and astrologer duties and added palace secretary to his title.

sentences.zh: 泓待敦彌厚，不以毀己易心。

translations.literal: Hong treated Dun all the thicker, not changing his mind because of slander against himself.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Hong treated Xu Dun with greater kindness and let no slander shake him.

sentences.zh: 慕容暐敗，以老歸家，歎曰：「燕必中興，其在吳王，恨吾年過不見耳。

translations.literal: When Murong Wei was defeated, he retired old to his home, sighing, "Yan must rise again—its locus is the Prince of Wu; I regret my years are past and I shall not see it.
translations.idiomatic: After Murong Wei's defeat he went home in old age and sighed, "Yan will rise again under the Prince of Wu—I only regret my years will not last to see it.

sentences.zh: 」年九十七卒。

translations.literal: " He died at age ninety-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died at ninety-seven.

sentences.zh: 卒後三年，偽吳王慕容垂興焉。

translations.literal: Three years after his death the false Prince of Wu Murong Chui arose.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later the "Prince of Wu," Murong Chui, restored the Yan cause as predicted.

sentences.zh: 索紞

translations.literal: Suo Dan.
translations.idiomatic: Suo Dan

sentences.zh: 索紞，字叔徹，敦煌人也。

translations.literal: Suo Dan, style name Shuche, was a man of Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Suo Dan, courtesy name Shuche, was from Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 少游京師，受業太學，博綜經籍，遂為通儒。

translations.literal: In youth he traveled the capital, studied in the Imperial Academy, broadly mastered the classics, and became a thorough scholar.
translations.idiomatic: He studied at the capital's Imperial Academy in youth, mastered the canon, and became an erudite Confucian.

sentences.zh: 明陰陽天文，善術數占侯。

translations.literal: He understood yin-yang and astronomy, and was skilled in numerology and prognostication.
translations.idiomatic: He was adept at yin-yang lore, astronomy, numerology, and omen reading.

sentences.zh: 司徒辟，除郎中，知中國將亂，避世而歸。

translations.literal: The Minister of Education summoned him; he was appointed court gentleman; knowing the Central States would soon be in chaos, he withdrew from the world and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: The minister summoned him to a gentleman post, but foreseeing turmoil in the heartland he resigned and went home.

sentences.zh: 鄉人從紞占問吉凶，門中如市，紞曰：「攻乎異端，戒在害己；

translations.literal: Countrymen followed Dan for auspice questions about fortune and misfortune; his gate was like a market; Dan said, "To attack divergent paths—warning is in harming oneself;
translations.idiomatic: Villagers swarmed his door for divination until it looked like a market. Suo Dan said, "The Analects warn against heterodox pursuits—they ruin the seeker;

sentences.zh: 無為多事，多事多患。

translations.literal: Do not make many affairs; many affairs mean many troubles."
translations.idiomatic: Meddling breeds trouble; trouble breeds disaster."

sentences.zh: 」遂詭言虛說，無驗乃止。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he spoke deceptively vague talk; when nothing verified they stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore fed them nonsense until lack of results cooled their zeal.

sentences.zh: 惟以占夢為無悔吝，乃不逆問者。

translations.literal: Only in dream divination was there no shame or regret, and then he did not reject questioners.
translations.idiomatic: Only dream interpretation carried no ill omen for the client, so he never turned such callers away.

sentences.zh: 孝廉令狐策夢立冰上，與冰下人語。

translations.literal: The filial-incorrupt Linghu Ce dreamed he stood on ice conversing with someone beneath the ice.
translations.idiomatic: The candidate Linghu Ce dreamed he stood on the ice talking to a man below.

sentences.zh: 紞曰：「冰上為陽，冰下為陰，陰陽事也。

translations.literal: Dan said, "On ice is yang, beneath ice is yin—it is a yin-yang matter.
translations.idiomatic: Suo Dan said, "Ice above is yang, water below is yin—this is the encounter of yin and yang.

sentences.zh: 士如歸妻，迨冰未泮，婚姻事也。

translations.literal: The gentleman as if taking a wife—when the ice has not yet melted—it is a marriage matter.
translations.idiomatic: As the Book of Songs says of the groom crossing the ford before the ice melts, this speaks of betrothal.

sentences.zh: 君在冰上與冰下人語，為陽語陰，媒介事也。

translations.literal: You on ice conversing with one beneath ice—yang speaks to yin—it is a matchmaking matter.
translations.idiomatic: You, yang on the surface, speak with yin below—a go-between's work.

sentences.zh: 君當為人作媒，冰泮而婚成。

translations.literal: You shall act as matchmaker for others; when the ice melts the marriage is accomplished."
translations.idiomatic: You will broker another's marriage, and the wedding will conclude when the ice breaks up."

sentences.zh: 」策曰：「老夫耄矣，不為媒也。

translations.literal: " Ce said, "This old man is senile—I will not act as matchmaker."
translations.idiomatic: Linghu Ce replied that he was too old to broker weddings.

sentences.zh: 」會太守田豹因策為子求鄉人張公徵女，仲春而成婚焉。

translations.literal: It happened that Prefect Tian Bao of the commandery, through Ce, sought the daughter of his townsman Zhang Gongzheng for his son; in the second month of spring the marriage was completed.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Tian Bao then used Linghu Ce as intermediary to win Zhang Gongzheng's daughter for his son, and the pair wed that mid-spring.

sentences.zh: 郡主簿張宅夢走馬上山，還繞舍三周，但見松柏，不知門處。

translations.literal: The commandery chief clerk Zhang Zhai dreamed a horse galloped up a mountain, circled his house three full turns, yet he saw only pines and cypresses and could not find the gate.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Clerk Zhang Zhai dreamed of a horse charging uphill, cantering three circuits around his home amid evergreens, with no doorway in sight.

sentences.zh: 紞曰：「馬屬離，離為火。

translations.literal: Dan said, "The horse belongs to li; li is fire.
translations.idiomatic: Suo Dan said the horse stood for the trigram li, and li meant fire.

sentences.zh: 火，禍也。

translations.literal: Fire means calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Fire portended disaster.

sentences.zh: 人上山，為凶字。

translations.literal: A man on a mountain forms the graph xiong ('inauspicious').
translations.idiomatic: Man plus mountain spelled the character for ill omen.

sentences.zh: 但見松伯，墓門象也。

translations.literal: Yet seeing only pine and cypress is the image of a tomb gate.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing only evergreens evoked a cemetery gate.

sentences.zh: 不知門處，為無門也。

translations.literal: Not knowing where the gate is means there is no gate.
translations.idiomatic: The missing gate meant there would be no escape.

sentences.zh: 三周，三期也。

translations.literal: Three circuits mean three cycles.
translations.idiomatic: Three rounds foretold three years.

sentences.zh: 後三年必有大禍。

translations.literal: After three years there will certainly be a great disaster.
translations.idiomatic: A major catastrophe would strike within three years.

sentences.zh: 」宅果以謀反伏誅。

translations.literal: " Zhai indeed was executed for plotting rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhai was later put to death for treason, as foretold.

sentences.zh: 索充初夢天上有二棺落充前，紞曰：「棺者，職也，當有京師貴人舉君。

translations.literal: At first Suo Chong dreamed two coffins fell from the sky before Chong; Dan said, "A coffin is zhi ('office'); a capital noble ought to recommend you.
translations.idiomatic: Suo Chong dreamed twin coffins drop from heaven; Suo Dan read "coffin" as high office and predicted a metropolitan patron would nominate him.

sentences.zh: 二官者，頻再遷。

translations.literal: Two offices mean repeated promotions.
translations.idiomatic: Two coffins meant two successive advancements.

sentences.zh: 」俄而司徒王戎書屬太守使舉充，太守先署充功曹而舉孝廉。

translations.literal: " Before long Minister of Education Wang Rong wrote instructing the prefect to recommend Chong; the prefect first appointed Chong merit clerk and then nominated him filial-incorrupt.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rong soon wrote the prefect, who first named Suo Chong merit clerk and then raised him as filial-incorrupt.

sentences.zh: 充後夢見一虜，脫上衣來詣充。

translations.literal: Later Chong dreamed a barbarian stripped his upper garment and came to Chong.
translations.idiomatic: Suo Chong later dreamed a tribesman doff his jacket and approach him.

sentences.zh: 紞曰：「虜去上中，下半男字，夷狄陰類，君婦當生男。

translations.literal: Dan said, "The barbarian removes the middle from shang; the lower half is the graph nan ('male'); the barbarian is a yin class of being—your wife shall bear a son.
translations.idiomatic: Suo Dan parsed the "barbarian" glyph: remove the middle stroke of shang and the lower half reads "male," so a foreign yin omen meant his wife would deliver a boy.

sentences.zh: 」終如其言。

translations.literal: " In the end it was as he said.
translations.idiomatic: The birth matched his reading exactly.

sentences.zh: 宋桷夢內中有一人著赤衣，桷手把兩杖，極打之。

translations.literal: Song Que dreamed someone inside the inner chambers wore crimson; Que held two staves and beat him fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: Song Que dreamed a red-clad intruder in the women's quarters whom he struck with twin rods.

sentences.zh: 紞曰：「內中有人，肉字也。

translations.literal: Dan said, "Someone inside the inner chambers is the graph rou ('flesh').
translations.idiomatic: Suo Dan said "person within inner rooms" formed the character for flesh.

sentences.zh: 肉色，赤也。

translations.literal: Flesh color is red.
translations.idiomatic: Flesh implied crimson garb.

sentences.zh: 兩杖，箸象也。

translations.literal: Two staves are the image of chopsticks.
translations.idiomatic: Twin sticks stood for chopsticks.

sentences.zh: 極打之，飽肉食也。

translations.literal: Beating fiercely means eating meat to satiety.
translations.idiomatic: The beating meant feasting on meat until full.

sentences.zh: 」俄而亦驗焉。

translations.literal: " Soon it likewise verified.
translations.idiomatic: The dream soon proved true.

sentences.zh: 黃平問紞曰：「我昨夜夢舍中馬舞，數十人向馬拍手，此何祥也？

translations.literal: Huang Ping asked Dan, saying, "Last night I dreamed horses dancing in my house and several dozen men clapping toward the horses—what sort of auspice is this?"
translations.idiomatic: Huang Ping asked Suo Dan about a dream of capering horses and a crowd applauding them indoors.

sentences.zh: 」紞曰：「馬者，火也，舞為火起。

translations.literal: " Dan said, "The horse is fire; dancing means fire rising.
translations.idiomatic: Suo Dan said horses signified fire, and dancing meant flames mounting.

sentences.zh: 向馬拍手，救火人也。

translations.literal: Clapping toward the horse means men who fight fire.
translations.idiomatic: Applauding the steeds depicted firefighters at work.

sentences.zh: 」平未歸而火作。

translations.literal: " Before Ping returned home, fire broke out.
translations.idiomatic: A blaze erupted before Huang Ping reached his door.

sentences.zh: 索綏夢東有二角書詣綏，大角朽敗，小角有題韋囊角佩，一在前，一在後。

translations.literal: Suo Sui dreamed two horned documents came east to Sui; the large horn was rotten, the small horn bore an inscription and a leather satchel hung from the horn; one was in front, one behind.
translations.idiomatic: Suo Sui dreamed two horn-marked writs arrive from the east, one decayed, one inscribed, with a tagged pouch and one horn leading, one trailing.

sentences.zh: 紞曰：「大角朽敗，腐棺木。

translations.literal: Dan said, "The large horn rotten means a decayed coffin board.
translations.idiomatic: The crumbling great horn stood for rotten coffin wood.

sentences.zh: 小角有題，題所詣。

translations.literal: The small horn having an inscription means the inscription states the destination.
translations.idiomatic: The smaller horn's text marked where the blow would fall.

sentences.zh: 一在前，前紞凶也。

translations.literal: One in front—that configuration was inauspicious for Dan.
translations.idiomatic: The foremost placement spelled personal misfortune for Suo Dan.

sentences.zh: 一在後，後背也。

translations.literal: One behind—'behind' is 'back,' meaning contrary.
translations.idiomatic: The rear position read as "contrary," a breach of taboo.

sentences.zh: 當有凶背之問。

translations.literal: There ought to be a calamity concerning 'contrary.'
translations.idiomatic: He foresaw news tied to that reversal.

sentences.zh: 」時綏父在東，居三日而凶問至。

translations.literal: " At that time Sui's father was in the east; within three days ill tidings arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Suo Sui's father was eastward; within three days mourning news came.

sentences.zh: 郡功曹張邈嘗奉使詣州，夜夢狼啖一腳。

translations.literal: Commandery merit clerk Zhang Miao once went on mission to the province and dreamed a wolf gnawed one foot.
translations.idiomatic: Merit clerk Zhang Miao, traveling to the provincial seat, dreamed a wolf chewed his foot.

sentences.zh: 紞曰：「腳肉被啖，為卻字。

translations.literal: Dan said, "Foot flesh gnawed away forms the graph que ('withdraw').
translations.idiomatic: Suo Dan read gnawed foot-flesh as the character for retreat.

sentences.zh: 」會東虜反，遂不行。

translations.literal: " It happened that eastern barbarians rebelled, and he therefore did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern tribes rose in revolt, so the journey was canceled.

sentences.zh: 凡所占莫不驗。

translations.literal: In all he prognosticated, nothing failed to verify.
translations.idiomatic: Every omen he read came true.

sentences.zh: 太守陰澹從求占書，紞曰：「昔入太學，因一父老為主人，其人無所不知，又匿姓名，有似隱者，紞因從父老問占夢之術，希申鄙藝，審測而說，實無書也。

translations.literal: Prefect Yin Dan sought his divination books; Dan said, "Long ago I entered the Grand Academy; through one old man as host—who knew everything and hid his name, somewhat like a recluse—I followed the old man to ask the art of dream divination, hoping to extend my mean skill; I examined and spoke from insight; truly there are no books."
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Yin Dan asked for written manuals; Suo Dan swore he had learned dream lore from an anonymous sage at the academy and owned no texts, only tested judgment.

sentences.zh: 」澹命為西閣祭酒，紞辭曰：「少無山林之操，遊學京師，交結時賢，會中國不靖，欲養志終年。

translations.literal: " Dan appointed him libationer of the west pavilion; Dan declined, saying, "In youth I had no mountain-forest resolve; I studied in the capital and befriended leading men of the age; as the Central States were not tranquil, I wished to cultivate my aims to the end of my years.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Dan named him west-pavilion libationer, but Suo Dan refused, citing no hermit vocation, capital schooling, and a wish to retire quietly amid turmoil.

sentences.zh: 老亦至矣，不求聞達。

translations.literal: Old age has also arrived; I do not seek renown.
translations.idiomatic: He added that old age had come and he craved no fame.

sentences.zh: 又少不習勤，老無吏幹，濛汜之年，弗敢聞命。

translations.literal: Moreover in youth I did not practice diligence; in age I lack clerkly capacity; in the Meng-si twilight of life I dare not accept the command."
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded no talent for administration and declined office in his declining years.

sentences.zh: 」澹以束帛禮之，月致羊酒。

translations.literal: " Dan therefore presented him bundled silk and monthly sheep and wine.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect instead sent silk bundles and monthly provisions of mutton and wine.

sentences.zh: 年七十五，卒於家。

translations.literal: At age seventy-five he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: Suo Dan died at home aged seventy-five.

sentences.zh: 孟欽

translations.literal: Meng Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Qin

sentences.zh: 孟欽，洛陽人也。

translations.literal: Meng Qin was a man of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Qin came from Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 有左慈、劉根之術，百姓惑而赴之。

translations.literal: He had the arts of Zuo Ci and Liu Gen; the common people were deluded and flocked to him.
translations.idiomatic: He wielded thaumaturgy like Zuo Ci and Liu Gen, drawing credulous crowds.

sentences.zh: 苻堅召詣長安，惡其惑眾，命苻融誅之。

translations.literal: Fu Jian summoned him to Chang'an, detested his misleading the masses, and ordered Fu Rong to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian called him to Chang'an, loathed his sway over the populace, and told Fu Rong to kill him.

sentences.zh: 俄而欽至，融留之，遂大宴郡僚，酒酣，目左右收欽。

translations.literal: Before long Qin arrived; Rong detained him and then feasted the commandery staff; when the wine was warm he signaled attendants to seize Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Qin appeared; Fu Rong detained him, wined his officials, then signaled guards to arrest him mid-banquet.

sentences.zh: 欽化為旋風，飛出第外。

translations.literal: Qin transformed into a whirlwind and flew out beyond the compound.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Qin became a whirlwind and shot past the manor walls.

sentences.zh: 頃之，有告在城東者，融遣騎追之，垂及，忽然已遠，或有兵眾距戰，或前有溪澗，騎不得過，遂不知所在。

translations.literal: Shortly someone reported him east of the city; Rong sent riders in pursuit; as they nearly caught him he was suddenly far away, or there were troops blocking battle, or ravines lay ahead so the horses could not cross; thus his whereabouts were unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Riders chased reports east of town, but phantoms of armies and gorges kept them from closing in, and he vanished.

sentences.zh: 堅未，復見於青州。

translations.literal: Toward the end of Fu Jian's reign he was seen again in Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Fu Jian's rule he resurfaced in Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 苻朗尋之，入於海島。

translations.literal: Fu Lang searched for him; he entered an island in the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Lang tracked him to a sea isle and lost him there.

sentences.zh: 王嘉

translations.literal: Wang Jia.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jia

sentences.zh: 王嘉，字子年，隴西安陽人也。

translations.literal: Wang Jia, style name Zinian, was a man of Anyang in Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jia, courtesy Zinian, hailed from Anyang in Longxi.

sentences.zh: 輕舉止，醜形貌，外若不足，而聰睿內明。

translations.literal: His bearing was light and his looks ugly; outwardly he seemed deficient, yet he was keen and bright within.
translations.idiomatic: He seemed slovenly and homely yet was razor-sharp inside.

sentences.zh: 滑稽好語笑，不食五穀，不衣美麗，清虛服氣，不與世人交遊。

translations.literal: Witty, fond of speech and laughter, he ate not the five grains, wore not fine silks, purified himself on qi, and did not mingle with the world.
translations.idiomatic: He jested constantly, shunned grain and brocade, lived on breath discipline, and shunned society.

sentences.zh: 隱于東陽穀，鑿崖穴居，弟子受業者數百人，亦皆穴處。

translations.literal: He hid in the valley of Dongyang, dwelling in cliff-hewn caves; disciples who received his teaching were several hundred, and they too dwelt in caves.
translations.idiomatic: He herded hundreds of pupils into cliff caverns near Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 石季龍之末，棄其徒眾，至長安，潛隱於終南山，結庵廬而止。

translations.literal: At the end of Shi Jilong's reign he abandoned his followers, came to Chang'an, and secretly hid on Mount Zhongnan, tying up a hut and stopping there.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Hu's regime collapsed he left his flock for Chang'an and built a hidden hut on Zhongnan.

sentences.zh: 門人聞而復隨之，乃遷於倒獸山。

translations.literal: Disciples heard and again followed him; he therefore moved to Mount Daoshou.
translations.idiomatic: Students found him again, so he relocated to Mount Daoshou.

sentences.zh: 苻堅累徵不起，公侯已下咸躬往參詣，好尚之士無不師宗之。

translations.literal: Fu Jian repeatedly summoned him but he would not rise; dukes and marquises downward all went in person to consult him; gentlemen of enthusiasm none failed to honor him as teacher.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian's repeated calls went ignored while nobles and scholars made pilgrimages to study under him.

sentences.zh: 問其當世事者，皆隨問而對。

translations.literal: On matters of the present age he answered as each question came.
translations.idiomatic: He fielded contemporary questions without hesitation.

sentences.zh: 好為譬喻，狀如戲調；

translations.literal: He loved to make parables; his manner was like jest.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke in riddling parables like a comic.

sentences.zh: 言未然之事，辭如讖記，當時鮮能曉之，事過皆驗。

translations.literal: When he spoke of things not yet happened, his words were like prophecy records; at the time few could understand; after events passed, all verified.
translations.idiomatic: His future-tense riddles baffled listeners until hindsight proved each clue.

sentences.zh: 堅將南征，遣使者問之。

translations.literal: When Fu Jian was about to march south he sent an envoy to ask him.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of Fu Jian's southern campaign an envoy sought his oracle.

sentences.zh: 嘉曰：「金剛火強。

translations.literal: Jia said, "Diamond hard, fire strong."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jia answered with the gnomic line "Vajra fierce, fire fierce."

sentences.zh: 」乃乘使者馬，正衣冠，徐徐東行數百步，而策馬馳反，脫衣服，棄冠履而歸，下馬踞床，一無所言。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he mounted the envoy's horse, straightened cap and robes, slowly rode east several hundred paces, then whipped the horse in a gallop back, cast off clothes, threw away cap and shoes, returned, dismounted, squatted on a couch, and said nothing at all.
translations.idiomatic: He borrowed the courier's mount, paraded eastward, wheeled at a gallop, shed cap and boots, then sat mute on a bench.

sentences.zh: 使者還告，堅不語，復遣問之，曰：「吾世祚云何？

translations.literal: The envoy returned and reported; Jian spoke nothing, again sent to ask, saying, "How fares my dynastic fortune?"
translations.idiomatic: The baffled envoy reported; Fu Jian sent again to ask how long his line would endure.

sentences.zh: 」嘉曰：「未央。

translations.literal: " Jia said, "Weiyang."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jia replied "Weiyang," which courtiers misread as endless blessing.

sentences.zh: 」咸以為吉。

translations.literal: " All deemed it auspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone took it for a promise of enduring rule.

sentences.zh: 明年癸未，敗於淮南，所謂未年而有殃也。

translations.literal: The next year, guiwei, he was defeated south of the Huai; this is what is meant by the wei year still having calamity.
translations.idiomatic: The next year guiwei brought disaster at Fei River—"not ended" had meant the wei year would still know woe.

sentences.zh: 人侯之者，至心則見之，不至心則隱形不見。

translations.literal: Those who waited on him, if utterly sincere then saw him; if not utterly sincere then he hid his form and was not seen.
translations.idiomatic: He appeared only to the utterly sincere and stayed invisible to half-hearted callers.

sentences.zh: 衣服在架，履杖猶存，或欲取其衣者，終不及，企而取之，衣架逾高，而屋亦不大，覆杖諸物亦如之。

translations.literal: His clothes hung on racks, shoes and staff still there; if someone wished to take his garments they could never reach them; standing on tiptoe to take them, the clothes rack grew higher, yet the room was not large; covering staff and other objects likewise behaved so.
translations.idiomatic: His robe and staff seemed ordinary yet eluded grasp, the rack rising when stretched for, though the chamber never widened.

sentences.zh: 姚萇之入長安，禮嘉如苻堅故事，逼以自隨，每事諮之。

translations.literal: When Yao Chang entered Chang'an he treated Jia as in Fu Jian's former practice, forced him to accompany himself, and consulted him on every affair.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang, conquering Chang'an, courted Wang Jia as Fu Jian had and dragooned him into counsel.

sentences.zh: 萇既與苻登相持，問嘉曰：「吾得殺苻登定天下不？

translations.literal: When Chang was locked with Fu Deng in stalemate he asked Jia, "Can I kill Fu Deng and settle All-under-Heaven?"
translations.idiomatic: During the standoff with Fu Deng, Yao Chang asked whether he could slay his rival and pacify the realm.

sentences.zh: 」嘉曰：「略得之。

translations.literal: " Jia said, "In rough terms you will obtain it."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jia answered, "You will gain it in part."

sentences.zh: 」萇怒曰：「得當云得，何略之有！

translations.literal: " Chang angrily said, "Obtain is obtain—what is this 'in part'!"
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang fumed that victory should be total, not partial.

sentences.zh: 」遂斬之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he executed him.
translations.idiomatic: He had Wang Jia beheaded in wrath.

sentences.zh: 先此，釋道安謂嘉曰：「世故方殷，可以行矣。

translations.literal: Before this, the monk Dao'an had said to Jia, "The world's troubles are just swelling; you may go."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Shih Dao'an had urged him to flee mounting chaos.

sentences.zh: 」嘉答曰：「卿其先行，吾負債未果去。

translations.literal: " Jia answered, "You may go first; I have a debt unpaid and cannot yet leave."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jia answered that Dao'an should leave first while he still owed fate a reckoning.

sentences.zh: 」俄而道安亡，至是而嘉戮死，所謂「負債」者也。

translations.literal: " Before long Dao'an died; by this time Jia was executed—this is what is meant by 'debt.'
translations.idiomatic: Dao'an died soon after; Wang Jia's execution fulfilled the dark sense of "debt."

sentences.zh: 苻登聞嘉死，設壇哭之，贈太師，諡曰文。

translations.literal: When Fu Deng heard Jia had died he set up an altar and wept for him, posthumously awarding Grand Preceptor and posthumous name Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng mourned him with rites and posthumous honors as Grand Preceptor Wen.

sentences.zh: 及萇死，萇子興字子略方殺登，「略得」之謂也。

translations.literal: When Chang died, Chang's son Xing, style name Zilue, then killed Deng—this is what 'in rough terms obtain it' referred to.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang's son Yao Xing, whose courtesy was Zilue, later slew Fu Deng—fulfilling the cryptic "partial gain."

sentences.zh: 嘉之死日，人有隴上見之。

translations.literal: On the day Jia died, someone saw him on the Long uplands.
translations.idiomatic: The day he died, witnesses still saw him walking the Long plateau.

sentences.zh: 其所造《牽三歌讖》，事過皆驗，累世猶傳之。

translations.literal: The "Pulling Three Songs Prophecy" that he composed—after events passed all verified; successive ages still transmit it.
translations.idiomatic: His doggerel prophecy cycle proved true in every line and stayed in folk memory.

sentences.zh: 又著《拾遺錄》十卷，其記事多詭怪，今行於世。

translations.literal: He also wrote the "Gathered Relics Record" in ten scrolls; its records are mostly uncanny and strange, and today circulates in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His ten-scroll miscellany of marvels remains in print.

sentences.zh: 僧涉

translations.literal: Monk She
translations.idiomatic: The monk She (Seng She)

sentences.zh: 僧涉者，西域人也，不知何姓。

translations.literal: Seng She was a man of the Western Regions; his surname is not known.
translations.idiomatic: Seng She came from the Western Regions; his family name was lost.

sentences.zh: 少為沙門，苻堅時入長安。

translations.literal: In youth he became a monk; in Fu Jian's time he entered Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: He tonsured young and reached Chang'an under Fu Jian.

sentences.zh: 虛靜服氣，不食五穀，日能行五百里，言未然之事，驗若指掌。

translations.literal: Empty and still he ingested qi, ate not the five grains, could travel five hundred li in a day, and spoke of things not yet happened with verification like pointing at his palm.
translations.idiomatic: He lived on breath, crossed five hundred li daily without grain, and foretold the future with uncanny precision.

sentences.zh: 能以秘祝下神龍，每旱，堅常使之咒龍請雨。

translations.literal: He could by secret invocations bring down divine dragons; whenever drought came, Jian constantly had him curse dragons to beg rain.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned rain-dragons by esoteric spells whenever drought struck.

sentences.zh: 俄而龍下缽中，天輒大雨，堅及群臣親就缽觀之。

translations.literal: Before long a dragon descended into the bowl; Heaven at once sent great rain; Jian and the host of ministers went in person to the bowl to observe it.
translations.idiomatic: A dragon coiled in an alms bowl and heaven opened; Fu Jian and his court peered in.

sentences.zh: 卒于長安。

translations.literal: He died in Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: He passed away in Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 後大旱移時，苻堅歎曰：「涉公若在，豈憂此乎！」

translations.literal: Later, after long drought, Fu Jian sighed, "If Duke She were alive, how would I worry over this!"
translations.idiomatic: Years of drought later made Fu Jian lament that without She their rains would never return.

sentences.zh: 郭黁

translations.literal: Guo Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wu

sentences.zh: 郭黁，西平人也。

translations.literal: Guo Wu was a man of Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wu hailed from Xiping.

sentences.zh: 少明《老》《易》，仕郡主簿。

translations.literal: In youth he understood the Laozi and Changes; he served as commandery chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Youthful mastery of the Laozi and Zhouyi won him the chief clerk's post.

sentences.zh: 張天錫末年，苻氏每有西伐之問，太守趙凝使黁筮之，黁曰：「若郡內二月十五日失囚者，東軍當至，涼祚必終。

translations.literal: In the last years of Zhang Tianxi, whenever the Fu clan raised questions of a western campaign, Prefect Zhao Ning had Wu divine it; Wu said, "If by the fifteenth day of the second month within the commandery a prisoner escapes, the eastern army will arrive and Liang's mandate will end."
translations.idiomatic: As Former Qin threatened Hexi, Prefect Zhao Ning had Guo Wu cast lots: a jailbreak on the fifteenth of the second month would herald eastern invasion and the fall of Former Liang.

sentences.zh: 」凝乃申約屬縣。

translations.literal: " Ning therefore issued orders to the subordinate counties.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ning wired every county to tighten the jails.

sentences.zh: 至十五日，鮮卑折掘送馬於凝，凝怒其非駿，幽之內廄，鮮卑懼而夜遁。

translations.literal: On the fifteenth day the Xianbei Zhejue presented horses to Ning; Ning, angry they were not swift mounts, confined them in the inner stable; the Xianbei feared and fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: On that day Xianbei herdsmen delivered horses Zhao Ning disliked and locked up, provoking a night stampede that broke custody.

sentences.zh: 凝以告黁，黁曰：「是也。

translations.literal: Ning reported it to Wu; Wu said, "It is so.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ning told Guo Wu, who said the omen had struck.

sentences.zh: 國家將亡，不可復振。」

translations.literal: The state is about to perish; it cannot be revived."
translations.idiomatic: Former Liang was finished beyond recovery.

sentences.zh: 苻堅末，當陽門震，刺史梁熙問黁曰：「其祥安在？

translations.literal: Near the end of Fu Jian's reign the Dangyang Gate quaked; Inspector Liang Xi asked Wu, "Wherein lies its auspice?"
translations.idiomatic: When Dangyang Gate shook late in Fu Jian's day, Governor Liang Xi asked Guo Wu what it portended.

sentences.zh: 」黁曰：「為四夷之事也。

translations.literal: " Wu said, "It concerns the affairs of the four barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wu read it as a sign involving foreign powers.

sentences.zh: 當有外國二王來朝主上，一當反國，一死此城。

translations.literal: There ought to be two kings from abroad who come to court to the sovereign; one ought to return to his state, one will die in this city.
translations.idiomatic: Two frontier kings would visit the throne: one would go home, the other would die in the capital.

sentences.zh: 」歲餘而鄯善及前部王朝於苻堅，西歸，鄯善王死于姑臧。

translations.literal: " After a year and more Shanshan and the king of the Front Division came to court to Fu Jian; returning west, the king of Shanshan died at Guzang.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year Shanshan and the anterior-branch Yarkand ruler paid homage to Fu Jian; the Shanshan ruler died at Guzang on the westward journey.

sentences.zh: 呂光之王河西也，西海太守王楨叛，黁勸光襲之。

translations.literal: When Lü Guang became king of the lands west of the River, West Sea Administrator Wang Zhen rebelled; Wu urged Guang to strike him.
translations.idiomatic: After Lü Guang took Hexi, rebel West Sea prefect Wang Zhen drew Guo Wu's advice to attack.

sentences.zh: 光之左丞呂寶曰：「千里襲人，自昔所難，況王者之師天下所聞，何可僥倖以邀成功！

translations.literal: Guang's left aide Lü Bao said, "To raid someone a thousand li away has been difficult since antiquity, moreover a kingly host famed to All-under-Heaven—how may one hazard luck to beg success!"
translations.idiomatic: Left aide Lü Bao warned that long-range surprise strikes were notorious gambles even for a celebrated royal army.

sentences.zh: 黁不可從，誤人大事。

translations.literal: Guo Wu must not be followed—it would ruin the great affair.
translations.idiomatic: He insisted Guo Wu's counsel would wreck the campaign.

sentences.zh: 」黁曰：「若其不捷，黁自伏鈇鉞之誅。

translations.literal: " Wu said, "If it is not victorious, Wu himself will submit to execution by axe and halberd.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wu swore to face the headsman's axe if the raid failed.

sentences.zh: 如其克也，左丞為無謀矣。

translations.literal: If it conquers, then the left aide will have been without strategy."
translations.idiomatic: Victory would expose Lü Bao as the fool, he added.

sentences.zh: 」光從而克之。

translations.literal: " Guang followed him and conquered.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang took the gamble and won.

sentences.zh: 光比之京管，常參帷幄密謀。

translations.literal: Guang compared him to Jing Fang and Guan Lu and constantly joined him in curtain counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang ranked him with Jing Fang and Guan Lu and kept him in secret strategy sessions.

sentences.zh: 光將伐乞伏乾歸，黁諫曰：「今太白未出，不宜行師，往必無功，終當覆敗。

translations.literal: When Guang was about to attack Qifu GanGui, Wu remonstrated, saying, "Now Venus has not yet risen; it is not fitting to launch troops; if you go you will certainly gain no success and in the end will overturn in defeat."
translations.idiomatic: Before the Qifu GanGui campaign Guo Wu warned that Venus had not appeared and marching would end in rout.

sentences.zh: 」太史令賈曜以為必有秦隴之地。

translations.literal: " Grand Astrologer Jia Yao thought there would certainly be the territory of Qin and Long.
translations.idiomatic: Court astrologer Jia Yao instead promised conquest of the Qin-Long region.

sentences.zh: 及克金城，光使曜詰黁，黁密謂光曰：「昨有流星東墮，當有伏屍死將，雖得此城，憂在不守。

translations.literal: When they took Jincheng, Guang sent Yao to question Wu; Wu secretly told Guang, "Yesterday a shooting star fell east—there ought to be corpses strewn and a general dead; though you gain this city, the worry is in not holding it.
translations.idiomatic: After Jincheng fell, Guo Wu privately told Lü Guang a fallen meteor meant pyrrhic gain and shaky tenure.

sentences.zh: 正月上旬，河冰將解，若不早渡，恐有大變。

translations.literal: In the first third of the first month the river ice will melt; if you do not cross early, I fear there will be a great change.
translations.idiomatic: He urged an early river crossing before January ice broke.

sentences.zh: 」後二日而敗問至，光引軍渡河訖，冰泮。

translations.literal: " After two days tidings of defeat arrived; Guang led the army across the river to completion, and the ice melted.
translations.idiomatic: Two days later defeat news came; Lü Guang finished his crossing just as the floes parted.

sentences.zh: 時人服其神驗。

translations.literal: People of the time admired his spirit verification.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries marveled at his precision.

sentences.zh: 光以黁為散騎常侍、太常。

translations.literal: Guang appointed Wu Cavalier Attendant-in-ordinary and Grand Master of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang named him supernumerary cavalier and grand liturgist.

sentences.zh: 黁後以光年老，知其將敗，遂與光僕射王祥起兵作亂。

translations.literal: Later, because Guang was aged, Wu knew he was about to fail; thereupon together with Guang's minister Wang Xiang he raised troops and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Lü Guang senile and doomed, Guo Wu joined Minister Wang Xiang in revolt.

sentences.zh: 百姓聞黁起兵，咸以聖人起事，事無不成，故相率從之如不及。

translations.literal: When the hundred surnames heard Wu had raised troops, all deemed a sage had begun an affair and nothing could fail; therefore they followed him in a rush as if they could not catch up.
translations.idiomatic: The populace mistook his rising for a saint-led sure victory and rushed to enlist.

sentences.zh: 黁以為代呂者王，乃推王乞基為主。

translations.literal: Wu thought that whoever replaced Lü would be surnamed Wang; he therefore set up Wang Qiji as lord.
translations.idiomatic: Reading the prophecy that Lü would yield to Wang, he enthroned Wang Qiji as figurehead.

sentences.zh: 後呂隆降姚興，興以王尚為涼州刺史，終如黁言。

translations.literal: Later Lü Long surrendered to Yao Xing; Xing appointed Wang Shang Inspector of Liang Province—in the end as Wu had said.
translations.idiomatic: When Lü Long yielded to Later Qin, Yao Xing installed Wang Shang over Liang, fulfilling Guo Wu's line.

sentences.zh: 黁之與光相持也，逃人稱呂統病死，黁曰：「未也，光、統之命盡在一時。

translations.literal: When Wu was locked with Guang in stalemate, a fugitive reported Lü Tong had died of illness; Wu said, "Not yet; Guang's and Tong's fates end at the same moment.
translations.idiomatic: During the standoff a rumor claimed Lü Tong had died; Guo Wu said both Lü lives would expire together.

sentences.zh: 」黁後統死三日而光死。

translations.literal: " Afterward Tong died and three days later Guang died.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Tong died first; Lü Guang followed three days later.

sentences.zh: 黁嘗曰：「涼州謙光殿后當有索頭鮮卑居之。

translations.literal: Wu once said, "Behind the modesty hall of Liangzhou a Suotou Xianbei will dwell."
translations.idiomatic: He prophesied Suotou Xianbei occupation behind Liangzhou's modesty hall.

sentences.zh: 」終於禿髮傉檀、沮渠蒙遜迭據姑臧。

translations.literal: " In the end Tufa Nutan and Juqu Mengxun seized Guzang in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Tufa Nutan and Juqu Mengxun alternately held Guzang, as he foretold.

sentences.zh: 黁性褊酷，不為士庶所附。

translations.literal: Wu by nature was narrow and cruel and was not attached to by gentry and commoners.
translations.idiomatic: His harsh temper won him few loyal followers.

sentences.zh: 戰敗，奔乞伏乾歸。

translations.literal: Defeated in battle, he fled to Qifu GanGui.
translations.idiomatic: Routed, he fled to Western Qin.

sentences.zh: 乾歸敗，入姚興。

translations.literal: When GanGui was defeated, he entered Yao Xing.
translations.idiomatic: After Qifu fell he entered Later Qin service.

sentences.zh: 黁以滅姚者晉，遂將妻子南奔，為追兵所殺也。

translations.literal: Wu thought that what would destroy Yao was Jin; thereupon leading wife and children he fled south and was killed by pursuing troops.
translations.idiomatic: Believing Jin would end Yao rule, he bolted south with his family and died under pursuit.

sentences.zh: 鳩摩羅什

translations.literal: Kumarajiva.
translations.idiomatic: Kumarajiva

sentences.zh: 鳩摩羅什，天竺人也。

translations.literal: Kumarajiva was a man of Tianzhu (India).
translations.idiomatic: Kumarajiva was a native of India.

sentences.zh: 世為國相。

translations.literal: For generations his house had been chief ministers of state.
translations.idiomatic: His forebears had served as Indian premiers for generations.

sentences.zh: 父鳩摩羅炎，聰懿有大節，將嗣相位，乃辭避出家，東渡蔥嶺。

translations.literal: His father Kumarayan was keen and virtuous with great integrity; about to inherit the chief ministership, he declined and left the world, crossing the Cong Ridge eastward.
translations.idiomatic: His father Kumarayan, brilliant and high-minded, renounced the hereditary premiership, took orders, and crossed the Pamirs east.

sentences.zh: 龜茲王聞其名，郊迎之，請為國師。

translations.literal: The king of Kucha heard his fame and met him beyond the walls, requesting him as national preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: The Kucha king welcomed him outside the walls and named him state chaplain.

sentences.zh: 王有妹，年二十，才悟明敏，諸國交娉，並不許，及見炎，心欲當之，王乃逼以妻焉。

translations.literal: The king had a younger sister, age twenty, talented and quick and bright; the various states sought her in marriage, and he granted none; when she saw Yan, her heart wished to have him; the king thereupon forced her to wife him.
translations.idiomatic: The princess, gifted and wooed by every realm, chose Kumarayan; the king compelled the match.

sentences.zh: 既而羅什在胎，其母慧解倍常。

translations.literal: Thereafter Kumarajiva was in the womb; his mother's wisdom doubled the norm.
translations.idiomatic: She bore Kumarajiva with twice the usual wit.

sentences.zh: 及年七歲，母遂與俱出家。

translations.literal: When he reached seven sui, his mother together with him left the household.
translations.idiomatic: At seven he tonsured with his mother.

sentences.zh: 羅什從師受經，日誦千偈，偈有三十二字，凡三萬二千言，義亦自通。

translations.literal: Kumarajiva followed a teacher to receive sutras; in a day he recited a thousand gathas; each gatha had thirty-two graphs; in all thirty-two thousand graphs; the meaning likewise penetrated of itself.
translations.idiomatic: He memorized a thousand thirty-two-character gathas daily—thirty-two thousand graphs—and grasped their sense unaided.

sentences.zh: 年十二，其母攜到沙勒，國王甚重之，遂停沙勒一年。

translations.literal: At twelve sui his mother brought him to Shule; the king of the state greatly honored him, and he therefore stopped in Shule one year.
translations.idiomatic: At twelve he toured Shule, where the king detained him a year in honor.

sentences.zh: 博覽五明諸論及陰陽星算，莫不必盡，妙達吉凶，言若符契。

translations.literal: He broadly perused the treatises of the five sciences and yin-yang and star calculation; there was none he did not exhaust; he wondrously comprehended fortune and misfortune; his words were like tally contracts.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered the five Buddhist sciences plus astrology and divination, speaking fate as if sealed by contract.

sentences.zh: 為性率達，不拘小檢，修行者頗共疑之。

translations.literal: By nature he was frank and expansive, not bound by petty restraint; practitioners together doubted him.
translations.idiomatic: His blunt, easygoing ways drew side-eyes from ascetics.

sentences.zh: 然羅什自得於心，未嘗介意，專以大乘為化，諸學者皆共師焉。

translations.literal: Yet Kumarajiva was self-content at heart and never minded; he devoted himself to converting by the Great Vehicle, and all students together took him as teacher.
translations.idiomatic: He ignored the gossip, taught Mahayana, and became the schoolmen's master.

sentences.zh: 年二十，龜茲王迎之還國，廣說諸經，四遠學徒莫之能抗。

translations.literal: At twenty sui the king of Kucha welcomed him back to the state and broadly lectured the sutras; students from the four quarters none could rival him.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to Kucha at twenty, he lectured rings of unmatched auditors.

sentences.zh: 有頃，羅什母辭龜茲王往天竺，留羅什住，謂之曰：「方等深教，不可思議，傳之東土，惟爾之力。

translations.literal: After a time Kumarajiva's mother took leave of the king of Kucha to go to Tianzhu, leaving Kumarajiva to stay, saying to him, "The profound teachings of the Great Equal Vehicle are beyond reckoning; to transmit them eastward depends on your strength.
translations.idiomatic: His mother left for India, leaving him in Kucha to carry Mahayana scripture eastward.

sentences.zh: 但於汝無利，其可如何？

translations.literal: Yet toward you there is no benefit—what can be done?"
translations.idiomatic: She warned the mission would cost him personally.

sentences.zh: 」什曰：「必使大化流傳，雖苦而無恨。

translations.literal: " Kumarajiva said, "Must cause the great teaching to flow and spread; though bitter, without regret."
translations.idiomatic: He vowed to spread the dharma regardless of personal pain.

sentences.zh: 」母至天竺，道成，進登第三果。

translations.literal: " When his mother reached Tianzhu, she completed the Way and advanced to the third fruit.
translations.idiomatic: In India she attained arhatship's third fruit.

sentences.zh: 西域諸國咸伏羅什神俊，每至講說，諸王皆長跪坐側，令羅什踐而登焉。

translations.literal: The various states of the Western Regions all submitted to Kumarajiva's spirit brilliance; whenever he reached lecture and exposition, the kings all knelt long beside the seat and had Kumarajiva tread upon them to mount.
translations.idiomatic: Western kings knelt as steps for him to mount the dais, awed by his genius.

sentences.zh: 苻堅聞之，密有迎羅什之意。

translations.literal: Fu Jian heard of it and secretly harbored intention to welcome Kumarajiva.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian coveted him from afar.

sentences.zh: 會太史奏云：「有星見外國分野，當有大智入輔中國。

translations.literal: It happened that the Grand Astrologer memorialized, saying, "A star appears in the foreign field division—there ought to be a great wise man entering to assist the Central States."
translations.idiomatic: The throne reported a foreign-field star heralding a sage for China.

sentences.zh: 」堅曰：「朕聞西域有鳩摩羅什，將非此邪？

translations.literal: " Jian said, "We have heard that in the Western Regions there is Kumarajiva—could it not be this?"
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian guessed it meant Kumarajiva.

sentences.zh: 」乃遣驍騎將軍呂光等率兵七萬，西伐龜茲，謂光曰：「若獲羅什，即馳驛送之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he sent General Who Sparks Courage Lü Guang and others leading seventy thousand troops to campaign west against Kucha, telling Guang, "If you capture Kumarajiva, immediately relay him by post."
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched Lü Guang with seventy thousand men to seize Kumarajiva and post him east at once.

sentences.zh: 」光軍未至，羅什謂龜茲王白純曰：「國運衰矣，當有勍敵從日下來，宜恭承之，勿抗其鋒。

translations.literal: " Before Guang's army arrived, Kumarajiva told the king of Kucha, Bai Chun, "The state's fortune declines; there ought to be a fierce foe coming from beneath the sun; you ought respectfully submit—do not resist his edge."
translations.idiomatic: He warned King Bai Chun of Kucha to yield to the invader from the sunrise quarter.

sentences.zh: 」純不從，出兵距戰，光遂破之，乃獲羅什。

translations.literal: " Chun did not follow; he sent troops to resist battle; Guang therefore broke him and then captured Kumarajiva.
translations.idiomatic: The king fought and lost; Lü Guang took the monk captive.

sentences.zh: 光見其年齒尚少，以凡人戲之，強妻以龜茲王女，羅什距而不受，辭甚苦至。

translations.literal: Guang saw his years and teeth were still young and toyed with him as a common man; he forced him to marry the king of Kucha's daughter; Kumarajiva refused and would not accept, his refusal words extremely bitter.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang mocked his youth, forced a royal princess on him, and met desperate refusal.

sentences.zh: 光曰：「道士之操不逾先父，何所固辭？

translations.literal: " Guang said, "A Daoist man's conduct does not surpass his late father—why so stubbornly decline?"
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang sneered that a monk need not outdo his father's worldly marriage.

sentences.zh: 」乃飲以醇酒，同閉密室。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he made him drink strong wine and together shut him in a sealed chamber.
translations.idiomatic: He plied him with liquor and locked him in an inner room.

sentences.zh: 羅什被逼，遂妻之。

translations.literal: Kumarajiva pressed by force, thereupon took her as wife.
translations.idiomatic: Broken by coercion, Kumarajiva accepted the princess.

sentences.zh: 光還，中路置軍於山下，將士已休，羅什曰：「在此必狼狽，宜徙軍隴上。

translations.literal: On Guang's return, midway he encamped the army beneath a mountain; the officers and troops had already rested; Kumarajiva said, "Here you will certainly be thrown into confusion; you ought to move the army onto the Long heights."
translations.idiomatic: On the march he warned against camping in a valley prone to flood.

sentences.zh: 」光不納。

translations.literal: " Guang did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang ignored him.

sentences.zh: 至夜，果大雨，洪潦暴起，水深數丈，死者數千人，光密異之。

translations.literal: By night it indeed rained heavily; violent floods suddenly rose; the water depth was several zhang; the dead were several thousand persons; Guang secretly marveled.
translations.idiomatic: Night rains drowned thousands in a flash flood, and Lü Guang secretly marveled.

sentences.zh: 光欲留王西國，羅什謂光曰：「此凶亡之地，不宜淹留，中路自有福地可居。

translations.literal: Guang wished to retain the king in the western states; Kumarajiva told Guang, "This is a land of violent death; it is not fitting to linger long; midway there is naturally a blessed land where you may dwell."
translations.idiomatic: When Lü Guang meant to stay west, Kumarajiva called the site deadly and pointed to Liangzhou as the true seat.

sentences.zh: 」光還至涼州，聞苻堅已為姚萇所害，於是竊號河右。

translations.literal: " Guang returned to Liang Province; hearing Fu Jian had already been murdered by Yao Chang, he thereupon usurped title west of the River.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang withdrew to Hexi, learned Fu Jian was dead, and carved out his own regime.

sentences.zh: 屬姑臧大風，羅什曰：「不祥之風當有奸叛，然不勞自定也。

translations.literal: When a great wind struck Guzang, Kumarajiva said, "This ill-omened wind means there ought to be treasonous rebellion, yet without labor it will settle of itself."
translations.idiomatic: A Guzang gale prompted his forecast of brief mutiny.

sentences.zh: 」俄而有叛者，尋皆殄滅。

translations.literal: " Before long there were rebels, and soon all were exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels rose and were crushed almost at once.

sentences.zh: 沮渠蒙遜先推建康太守段業為主，光遣其子纂率眾討之。

translations.literal: Juqu Mengxun first set up Jian'an Administrator Duan Ye as lord; Guang sent his son Zuan leading hosts to punish him.
translations.idiomatic: Juqu Mengxun's puppet Duan Ye drew Lü Guang's son Lü Zuan against him.

sentences.zh: 時論謂業等烏合，纂有威聲，勢必全克。

translations.literal: Contemporary opinion deemed Ye and company a crow's host; Zuan had martial repute; the momentum was certain to achieve full conquest.
translations.idiomatic: Court gossip called Duan Ye rabble and expected Lü Zuan's prestige to crush him.

sentences.zh: 光以訪羅什，答曰：「此行未見其利。

translations.literal: Guang consulted Kumarajiva; he answered, "This march does not yet show its gain."
translations.idiomatic: Kumarajiva told Lü Guang the expedition would not pay.

sentences.zh: 」既而纂敗于合黎，俄又郭黁起兵，纂棄大軍輕還，復為黁所敗，僅以身免。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Zuan was defeated at Heli; before long again Guo Wu raised troops; Zuan abandoned the great host and returned lightly, and again was defeated by Wu, barely escaping with his life.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Zuan lost at Heli, fled Guo Wu's rising, abandoned his army, and barely escaped.

sentences.zh: 中書監張資病，光博營救療。

translations.literal: Palace Secretary Zhang Zi fell ill; Guang widely sought cure.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang scoured healers for ailing Zhang Zi.

sentences.zh: 有外國道人羅叉，雲能差資病。

translations.literal: There was a foreign monk named Luo Cha who claimed able to cure Zi's illness.
translations.idiomatic: A foreign monk named Luo Cha claimed a cure.

sentences.zh: 光喜，給賜甚重。

translations.literal: Guang rejoiced and gave rewards very heavy.
