translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang showered him with gifts.

sentences.zh: 羅什知叉誑詐，告資曰：「叉不能為益，徒煩費耳。

translations.literal: Kumarajiva knew Cha was deceitful; he told Zi, "Cha cannot bring benefit—only vex expense."
translations.idiomatic: Kumarajiva warned Zhang Zi that Luo Cha was a fraud wasting treasure.

sentences.zh: 冥運雖隱，可以事試也。

translations.literal: Though hidden fate is obscure, one may test it by affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Hidden fate could still be tested, he said.

sentences.zh: 」乃以五色絲作繩結之，燒為灰末，投水中，灰若出水還成繩者，病不可愈。

translations.literal: " Thereupon with five-colored silk he made a rope, knotted it, burned it to ash powder, cast it in water—if the ash coming out of water again formed rope, the illness could not be cured.
translations.idiomatic: He knotted colored silk, burned it to ash, and floated it—if the ash reknotted into cord, death was certain.

sentences.zh: 須臾，灰聚浮出，復為繩，叉療果無效，少日資亡。

translations.literal: In a short while the ash gathered and floated out, again becoming rope; Cha's treatment indeed had no effect; within a few days Zi died.
translations.idiomatic: The ash reformed as rope; Luo Cha failed and Zhang Zi died within days.

sentences.zh: 頃之，光死，纂立。

translations.literal: Before long Guang died; Zuan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang died and Lü Zuan took the throne.

sentences.zh: 有豬生子，一身三頭。

translations.literal: There was a pig that gave birth; one body, three heads.
translations.idiomatic: A sow farrowed a three-headed piglet.

sentences.zh: 龍出東箱井中，於殿前蟠臥，比旦失之。

translations.literal: A dragon emerged from the well in the east wing; it coiled and lay in the hall forecourt; by dawn it was lost.
translations.idiomatic: A dragon left the east-wing well, coiled before the hall, and vanished by dawn.

sentences.zh: 纂以為美瑞，號其殿為龍翔殿。

translations.literal: Zuan deemed it an auspicious prodigy and named his hall Dragon Soaring Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Zuan hailed it as an omen and renamed the hall Dragon Soaring.

sentences.zh: 俄而有黑龍升于當陽九宮門，纂改九宮門為龍興門。

translations.literal: Before long there was a black dragon that ascended at the Dangyang Nine Palaces Gate; Zuan changed the Nine Palaces Gate to Dragon Rising Gate.
translations.idiomatic: A black dragon rose at Dangyang's Nine Palaces gate, so he renamed it Dragon Rising.

sentences.zh: 羅什曰：「比日潛龍出遊，豕妖表異，龍者陰類，出入有時，而今屢見，則為災眚，必有下人謀上之變。

translations.literal: Kumarajiva said, "These days lurking dragons go abroad; the pig monster shows strangeness; the dragon is a yin class; going out and entering have their seasons—yet now they repeatedly appear—then there is calamity and fault; there ought to be a change of a subordinate plotting against his superior."
translations.idiomatic: Kumarajiva read roaming dragons and porcine freaks as yin omens of usurpation.

sentences.zh: 宜克己修德，以答天戒。

translations.literal: You ought to restrain yourself and cultivate virtue to answer Heaven's warning."
translations.idiomatic: He urged self-discipline to answer heaven's rebuke.

sentences.zh: 」纂不納，後果為呂超所殺。

translations.literal: " Zuan did not accept; afterward he was indeed killed by Lü Chao.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Zuan ignored him and fell to Lü Chao's plot.

sentences.zh: 羅什之在涼州積年，呂光父子既不弘道，故蘊其深解，無所宣化。

translations.literal: Kumarajiva's years in Liang Province were many; as Lü Guang father and son did not promote the Dao, therefore he stored his deep understanding and had nowhere to proclaim and transform.
translations.idiomatic: Years under the Lüs, who ignored the dharma, left his deepest insight untaught.

sentences.zh: 姚興遣姚碩德西伐，破呂隆，乃迎羅什，待以國師之禮，仍使入西明閣及逍遙園，譯出眾經。

translations.literal: Yao Xing sent Yao Shide to campaign west, defeated Lü Long, then welcomed Kumarajiva, treating him with rites of national preceptor, still having him enter the Ximing Pavilion and Free Roaming Garden to translate the host of sutras.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing's general crushed Lü Long, welcomed Kumarajiva as national preceptor, and housed him at Ximing and Free Roaming to translate scripture.

sentences.zh: 羅什多所暗誦，無不究其義旨，既覽舊經多有紕繆，於是興使沙門僧睿、僧肇等八百餘人傳受其旨，更出經論，凡三百餘卷。

translations.literal: Kumarajiva had much memorized by heart; there was none whose meaning and purport he did not exhaust; once he surveyed old translations many were awry; therefore Xing had the monks Seng Rui, Seng Zhao, and more than eight hundred others transmit and receive his purport, anew issuing sutras and treatises, in all more than three hundred scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He corrected flawed old translations with eight hundred assistants, issuing over three hundred new scrolls.

sentences.zh: 沙門慧睿才識高明，常隨羅什傳寫，羅什每為慧睿論西方辭體，商略同異，云：「天竺國俗甚重文制，其宮商體韻，經入管弦為善。

translations.literal: The monk Hui Rui's talent and insight were high and bright; he constantly followed Kumarajiva in transcription; Kumarajiva often for Hui Rui discussed Western phrasing, weighing sameness and difference, saying, "The customs of the Tianzhu state greatly esteem literary form; their tonal patterns, when taken into pipes and strings, are excellent.
translations.idiomatic: To his scribe Hui Rui he explained Sanskrit rhetoric and musicality.

sentences.zh: 凡覲國王，必有贊德，經中偈頌，皆其式也。

translations.literal: Whenever one has audience with a king, there must be praise of virtue; the gathas in the sutras are all of that pattern."
translations.idiomatic: Royal audiences demanded panegyric verse like sutra gathas, he explained.

sentences.zh: 」羅什雅好大乘，志在敷演，常歎曰：「吾若著筆作大乘阿毗曇，非迦旃子比也。

translations.literal: " Kumarajiva by nature loved the Great Vehicle; his aim lay in spreading and expounding; he often sighed, saying, "If I took brush to compose a Mahayana Abhidharma, I would not be matched by the Kaushthila son.
translations.idiomatic: He aspired to author Mahayana abhidharma surpassing the Sarvastivadin masters.

sentences.zh: 今深識者既寡，將何所論！

translations.literal: Now those with deep insight are few—with whom shall I discuss!"
translations.idiomatic: He groaned that few peers could debate subtle doctrine.

sentences.zh: 」惟為姚興著《實相論》二卷，興奉之若神。

translations.literal: " Only for Yao Xing did he compose the "Treatise on True Marks" in two scrolls; Xing revered him like a spirit.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the two-scroll True Mark treatise for Yao Xing alone, and the emperor worshipped him.

sentences.zh: 嘗講經於草堂寺，興及朝臣、大德沙門千有餘人肅容觀聽，羅什忽下高坐，謂興曰：「有二小兒登吾肩，欲鄣須婦人。

translations.literal: Once lecturing sutras at Caotang Monastery, Xing together with court ministers and great-virtue monks exceeding a thousand persons respectfully watched and listened; Kumarajiva suddenly descended the high seat and told Xing, "Two small children have climbed my shoulders; I must obstruct them and need a woman."
translations.idiomatic: Mid-sermon at Caotang he told Yao Xing two sprites on his shoulders demanded a woman—an occult excuse.

sentences.zh: 」興乃召宮女進之，一交而生二子焉。

translations.literal: " Xing thereupon summoned palace women and sent them in; one union and he begot two sons.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing sent palace ladies; one liaison produced twin sons.

sentences.zh: 興嘗謂羅什曰：「大師聽明超悟，天下莫二，何可使法種少嗣。

translations.literal: Xing once told Kumarajiva, "The great master's brilliance and penetration surpass All-under-Heaven—none is second—how may the seeds of the Law have few heirs?"
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing argued that such genius owed the church heirs.

sentences.zh: 」遂以伎女十人，逼令受之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon with ten singing-girls he forced him to accept them.
translations.idiomatic: He forced ten court entertainers on the monk.

sentences.zh: 爾後不住僧坊，別立解舍。

translations.literal: Afterward he dwelt not in the monks' quarters but separately set up a lay lodge.
translations.idiomatic: Kumarajiva thereafter kept a private lay cloister outside the common dormitory.

sentences.zh: 諸僧多效之。

translations.literal: The various monks for the most part imitated him.
translations.idiomatic: Lesser monks copied his householding.

sentences.zh: 什乃聚針盈缽，引諸僧謂之曰：「若能見效食此者，乃可畜室耳。

translations.literal: Kumarajiva thereupon gathered needles filling a bowl, led the various monks, and told them, "If you can imitate me and eat this, then you may keep wives."
translations.idiomatic: He filled a bowl with needles and dared the clergy to mimic his feat before taking wives.

sentences.zh: 」因舉匕進針，與常食不別，諸僧愧服乃止。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he raised a spoon and advanced the needles; they were no different from ordinary food; the various monks were ashamed and submitted and desisted.
translations.idiomatic: He ate them like rice until the monks, shamed, dropped the fad.

sentences.zh: 杯渡比丘在彭城，聞羅什在長安，乃歎曰：「吾與此子戲，別三百餘年，相見杳然未期，遲有遇于來生耳。

translations.literal: The monk Beidu in Pengcheng, hearing Kumarajiva was in Chang'an, thereupon sighed, saying, "I sported with this child; we parted more than three hundred years; meeting again is dimly without date—only in a later birth shall we encounter each other."
translations.idiomatic: The wandering monk Beidu in Pengcheng sighed that he and Kumarajiva had parted three centuries and might reunite only in another life.

sentences.zh: 」羅什未終少日，覺四大不愈，乃口出三番神咒，令外國弟子誦之以自救，未及致力，轉覺危殆，於是力疾與眾僧告別曰：「因法相遇，殊未盡心，方復後世，惻愴可言。

translations.literal: " Within a few days before Kumarajiva's end he felt the four great elements would not heal; thereupon he uttered three rounds of divine spells by mouth, ordering foreign disciples to chant them to save himself; before he could apply effort, he turned to feel peril; therefore, straining through illness, he took leave of the host of monks, saying, "Through the Law we met—yet we did not exhaust the heart; we shall resume in a later generation—grief may be spoken."
translations.idiomatic: Days before death he felt his body failing, tried spirit spells through foreign pupils, then rallied to bid the sangha farewell, mourning unfinished dharma work.

sentences.zh: 」死于長安。

translations.literal: " He died in Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: His life ended in the Jin capital.

sentences.zh: 姚興於逍遙園依外國法以火焚屍，薪滅形碎，惟舌不爛。

translations.literal: Yao Xing at the Free Roaming Garden followed foreign custom and burned the corpse with fire; when the fuel was spent the form broke apart—only the tongue did not rot.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing cremated him Indian-style at Free Roaming Garden; bones shattered but the tongue survived the pyre.

sentences.zh: 僧曇霍

translations.literal: Monk Tanhuo
translations.idiomatic: The monk Tanhuo

sentences.zh: 沙門曇霍者，不知何許人也。

translations.literal: The monk Tanhuo—none knew what place he was from.
translations.idiomatic: Tanhuo's origins were unknown.

sentences.zh: 禿髮傉檀時從河南來，持一錫杖，令人跪曰：「此是般若眼，奉之可以得道。

translations.literal: In Tufa Nutan's time he came from Henan, holding one khakkhara, ordering men to kneel, saying, "This is the eye of prajna; reverencing it, you may obtain the Way."
translations.idiomatic: Under Tufa Nutan he arrived from Henan with a staff, forcing folk to kneel and calling it the eye of wisdom.

sentences.zh: 」時人咸異之。

translations.literal: " People of the time all deemed him strange.
translations.idiomatic: Onlookers took him for a wonder.

sentences.zh: 或遺以衣服，受而投之於河，後日以還其本主，衣無所汙。

translations.literal: Some gave him clothing; he accepted and cast it into the river; later on the appointed day it returned to the original owner, the clothes without stain.
translations.idiomatic: Gifts of clothing he flung in the river; the garments returned spotless to the donors on the promised day.

sentences.zh: 行步如風雲，言人死生貴賤無毫釐之差。

translations.literal: His steps were like wind and cloud; speaking of men's death and life, noble and base, there was not a hair's breadth of error.
translations.idiomatic: He strode like storm wind and never missed a fate he foretold.

sentences.zh: 人或藏其錫杖，曇霍大哭數聲，閉目須臾，起而取之，咸奇其神異，莫能測也。

translations.literal: If someone hid his khakkhara, Tanhuo wailed several sounds, closed his eyes a moment, rose and took it; all marveled at his spirit strangeness—none could fathom him.
translations.idiomatic: Hidden staves drew wails until he recovered them by trance, baffling witnesses.

sentences.zh: 每謂傉檀曰：「若能安坐無為，則天下可定，祚胤克昌，如其窮兵好殺，禍將及己。

translations.literal: He often told Nutan, "If you can sit still in non-action, then All-under-Heaven may be settled, the throne and heirs able to flourish; if like that you exhaust armies and love killing, calamity will reach yourself."
translations.idiomatic: He urged Nutan that quiet rule would secure the throne while endless war would rebound on him.

sentences.zh: 」傉檀不能從。

translations.literal: " Nutan could not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Nutan refused the counsel.

sentences.zh: 傉檀女病甚，請救療，曇霍曰：「人之生死自有定期，聖人亦不能轉禍為福，曇霍安能延命邪！

translations.literal: Nutan's daughter was gravely ill; she begged rescue and healing; Tanhuo said, "Men's death and life each have a fixed term; even sages cannot turn misfortune into fortune—how can Tanhuo extend life!"
translations.idiomatic: When Nutan's daughter lay dying, Tanhuo refused miracles, citing fixed life spans even sages cannot bend.

sentences.zh: 正可知早晚耳。

translations.literal: One can only know whether early or late.
translations.idiomatic: He offered only a timetable, not a cure.

sentences.zh: 」傉檀固請之。

translations.literal: " Nutan firmly pressed him.
translations.idiomatic: Nutan insisted.

sentences.zh: 時後宮門閉，曇霍曰：急開後門，及開門則生，不及則死。

translations.literal: At that time the rear-palace gates were closed; Tanhuo said, "Open the rear gate with haste; if you open the gate in time then she lives; if not in time then she dies."
translations.idiomatic: With harem gates locked, Tanhuo demanded the rear portal be opened instantly to spare the princess.

sentences.zh: 」傉檀命開之，不及而死。

translations.literal: " Nutan ordered it opened; it was not in time and she died.
translations.idiomatic: Nutan complied too late and the girl died.

sentences.zh: 後兵亂，不知所在也。

translations.literal: Later, amid military chaos, none knew where he went.
translations.idiomatic: War swallowed him without trace.

sentences.zh: 台產

translations.literal: Tai Chan.
translations.idiomatic: Tai Chan

sentences.zh: 台產，字國俊，上洛人，漢侍中崇之後也。

translations.literal: Tai Chan, style name Guojun, was a man of Shangluo, a descendant of Han Palace Attendant Chong.
translations.idiomatic: Tai Chan, courtesy Guojun, of Shangluo, descended from Han courtier Tai Chong.

sentences.zh: 少專京氏《易》，善圖讖、秘緯、天文、洛書、風角、星算、六日七分之學，尤善望氣、占候、推步之術。

translations.literal: In youth he specialized in the Jing family's Changes; he was good at chart prophecy, secret weft texts, astronomy, River Chart writings, wind-angle, star calculation, and the learning of six days and seven parts; he was especially good at observing qi, prognosticating by signs, and push-step arts.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered Jing Fang's Zhouyi, apocrypha, stars, wind divination, and calendrical computation, excelling at qi-watching and omen math.

sentences.zh: 隱居商洛南山，兼善經學，泛情教授，不交當世。

translations.literal: He hid in South Mountain of Shangluo; concurrently he was good in classical learning; broadly he taught with feeling and did not mingle with the age.
translations.idiomatic: He taught classics from a hermitage on Shangluo's southern peak, shunning office.

sentences.zh: 劉曜時，災異特甚，命公卿各舉博識直言之士一人。

translations.literal: In Liu Yao's time calamities and prodigies were especially severe; he ordered dukes and ministers each to recommend one broadly learned man who spoke straight.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao, beset by omens, ordered each minister to nominate a candid scholar.

sentences.zh: 其大司空劉均舉產。

translations.literal: His Grand Minister of Works Liu Jun recommended Chan.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Minister Liu Jun nominated Tai Chan.

sentences.zh: 曜親臨東堂，遣中黃門策問之，產極言其故。

translations.literal: Yao personally came to the east hall, sent a palace attendant to examine him by question, and Chan spoke to the utmost the reasons.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao convened him at the east hall for a palace examination, and Tai Chan laid out every cause.

sentences.zh: 曜覽而嘉之，引見，訪以政事。

translations.literal: Yao read and praised him, summoned him to audience, and consulted him on government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his memorials, received him, and sought policy advice.

sentences.zh: 產流涕歔欷，具陳災變之禍，政化之闕，辭甚懇至。

translations.literal: Chan wept and sobbed, stating in full the disasters of prodigies and the gaps in governance and transformation; his words were extremely earnest.
translations.idiomatic: He wept through a thorough brief on portents and policy failures.

sentences.zh: 曜改容禮之，署為博士祭酒、諫議大夫，領太史令。

translations.literal: Yao changed countenance and treated him with rites, appointing him libationer of erudites, grandee of remonstrance, and concurrent Grand Astrologer.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao honored him with erudite libationer, remonstrance grandee, and astrologer-in-chief posts.

sentences.zh: 至明年而其言皆驗，曜彌重之，轉太中大夫，歲中三遷。

translations.literal: By the next year his words all verified; Yao all the more esteemed him, transferred him to Grand Palace Grandee, and within the year thrice promoted him.
translations.idiomatic: When every warning proved true within a year, Liu Yao thrice promoted him to grand palace grandee.

sentences.zh: 歷位尚書、光祿大夫、太子少師，位特進，金章紫綬，爵關中侯。

translations.literal: He successively held Minister, Palace Grandee, Junior Tutor to the heir, rank specially advanced, gold seal and purple ribbon, and noble title Marquis Within-the-Pass.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through minister, palace grandee, heir tutor, special advancement, gold seal purple ribbon, and marquis of Guannei.

sentences.zh: 史評

translations.literal: Historian's appraisal.
translations.idiomatic: Closing shǐ píng verdict section.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：陳戴等諸子並該洽墳典，研精數術，究推步之幽微，窮陰陽之秘奧，雖前代京管，何以加之！

translations.literal: The court historian states: Chen Xun, Dai Yang, and the various gentlemen together mastered the tomb classics, refined number arts, plumbed the subtlety of push-step reckoning, and exhausted the secret profundity of yin-yang—even the Jing and Guan of former ages, how could one add more!
translations.idiomatic: The annalist praises Chen Xun, Dai Yang, and their peers as rivaling Han augurs Jing Fang and Guan Lu.

sentences.zh: 郭黁知有晉之亡姚，去姚以歸晉，追兵奄及，致斃中途，斯則遠見秋毫，不能近知目睫。

translations.literal: Guo Wu knew Jin would destroy Yao; leaving Yao to return to Jin, pursuing troops suddenly overtook him and caused him to die midway—this then is seeing the autumn hair from afar yet failing to know what lies on one's own eyelashes.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wu foresaw Jin ending Yao yet died fleeing to Jin—sharp on distant detail, blind to the immediate.

sentences.zh: 澄什爰自遐裔，來游諸夏。

translations.literal: Cheng and Kumarajiva came from distant margins and roamed the Hua xia.
translations.idiomatic: Fotucheng and Kumarajiva crossed from the frontiers into China.

sentences.zh: 什既兆見星象，澄乃驅役鬼神，並通幽洞冥，垂文闡教，諒見珍於道藝，非取貴於他山，姚石奉之若神，良有以也。

translations.literal: As Kumarajiva already showed signs in the stars, Cheng then drove ghosts and spirits; both penetrated the hidden and bored through the dark, let fall writings and clarified teaching—truly they were treasured for the Way and arts, not prized as borrowings from other mountains; Yao and Shi revered them like spirits—indeed there was reason.
translations.idiomatic: One read the stars, the other bound ghosts; both illumined the dark and spread doctrine, earning Yao and Shi's awe on merit, not novelty.

sentences.zh: 鮑、吳、王、幸等或假靈道訣，或受教神方，遂能厭勝禳災，隱文彰義，雖獲譏於妖妄，頗有益於世用者焉。

translations.literal: Bao, Wu, Wang, Xing, and the rest either borrowed numinous Dao formulas or received instruction in divine recipes; thereby they could suppress ill omens and avert calamity, hiding texts yet manifesting meaning—though they incurred ridicule as uncanny falsehoods, they were still rather beneficial to worldly use.
translations.idiomatic: Lesser wonder-workers mixed fraud with practical charms that sometimes helped the folk.

sentences.zh: 然而碩學通人，未宜枉轡。

translations.literal: Yet great learning and penetrating men ought not bend the carriage shaft to them.
translations.idiomatic: True scholars need not hitch their wagons to such arts.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：《傳》敘災祥，《書》稱龜筮。

translations.literal: The encomium states: The Traditions narrate calamity and auspice; the Documents praise tortoise and milfoil.
translations.idiomatic: The verse cites the Zuozhuan and Shangshu on omens and divination.

sentences.zh: 應如影響，葉若符契。

translations.literal: They respond like shadow and echo; they fit like tally halves.
translations.idiomatic: Omens answer like echoes and fit like split tallies.

sentences.zh: 怪力亂神，詭時惑世。

translations.literal: Strange force and disorderly spirits deceive the age and delude the world.
translations.idiomatic: Uncanny powers and rogue spirits bewitch their times.

sentences.zh: 崇尚弗已，必致流弊。

translations.literal: To honor and elevate them without cease is sure to bring flowing abuse.
translations.idiomatic: Endless court patronage of such ways invites lasting harm.
